author: benjaminduffey
body:
## Summary

The piece that makes the approval pipeline *automatic*. Every new submission at `status='pending_review'` now triggers an async POST to the `community-review` edge function. The Arbiter runs, override rules fire, `community_decision` RPC writes the final status — all without a human clicking anything.

Before C3.4: every submission sat in the queue until an admin opened `/moderation` and acted.
After C3.4: clean submissions auto-publish; sketchy ones auto-escalate to the queue for you to review.

## Mechanics

- **`pg_net`** enabled in the `extensions` schema. Supabase ships this but doesn't default-enable it.
- **`_community_review_secrets()`** — `SECURITY DEFINER` helper that reads the endpoint URL + service-role key from `supabase_vault` by name. Service key never lives in git or in the trigger body.
- **`_community_review_dispatch()`** — trigger function. Resolves secrets, calls `net.http_post` fire-and-forget, returns. INSERT doesn't block on ~2-5s LLM latency.
- **Trigger** — `AFTER INSERT ON marketplace_listings WHEN (NEW.status = 'pending_review')`. Belt-and-suspenders filter so admin-inserted rows at other statuses don't fire spurious reviews.

## Post-deploy setup (one-time, via Studio)

```sql
SELECT vault.create_secret(
  '<service-role-key-from-Settings-API>',
  'community_review_service_key',
  'Service-role key for community-review edge function');
```

The URL secret (`community_review_url`) is already populated in the project vault pointing at `https://zacllshbgmnwsmliteqx.supabase.co/functions/v1/community-review`. Only the service-role key needs manual input since it can't be committed to git.

The migration ships a **placeholder** service-role secret so the trigger path is exercised end-to-end at deploy time (it fires, hits the edge function, gets a 401 — expected). Replace the placeholder via Studio Vault to begin real reviews.

## Verification

Live against Supabase:

| Test | Expected | Actual |
|------|----------|--------|
| Seed pending_review listing | trigger fires pg_net POST | ✓ |
| Edge function receives POST | attempts auth | ✓ |
| Auth with placeholder key | 401 'service_role required' | ✓ |
| Listing stays at pending_review | no premature decision | ✓ |
| Drop service-key secret, insert another | INSERT succeeds, trigger logs NOTICE and returns | ✓ |
| Row still lands at pending_review | human-review fallback intact | ✓ |

## Pause switch

`DELETE FROM vault.secrets WHERE name='community_review_service_key'` — trigger falls back to no-op, everything still goes to human review via `/moderation`. No redeploy needed.

## Out of scope

- **C3.2b** — full 5-agent crew (today: single Arbiter)
- **C3.3** — post-hoc validator
- **C3.5b** — kill switches as a UI affordance (today: SQL-only via vault)
- **C3.6** — golden-test eval framework

## Test plan

- [x] Migration applied to live Supabase
- [x] Trigger fires end-to-end via pg_net
- [x] Placeholder key produces expected 401
- [x] Degradation path verified (missing secret → graceful NOTICE)
- [ ] After real service-role key is populated: submit a ship, confirm auto-decision lands within seconds
- [ ] CI Playwright

author: jorenvo
body:
_assign_and_convert_leads() is biased towards team members created earlier because they're ordered by create_date, id.

When members have equal quota, the round-robin order falls back to the order of the team members. If the amount of leads distributed across the team is not a multiple of the team size, then the oldest members will get more leads assigned. This advantage repeats each time the cron runs and can add up to a big difference, the provided test case ends up assigning all 30 leads to the more senior member without the fix.

Note that the lead_day_count field used in _get_assignment_quota() doesn't solve the problem. It helps to balance leads assigned in the same 24 hour window, but because the same senior person always goes first inside one of those windows, they will always get more leads assigned to them.

To fix it we break ties in the quota randomly.

author: kadenmc
body:
## Summary

- **Root cause**: a duplicate `work_buddy.telegram.service` process was polling the same bot token. Telegram alternated `getUpdates` between them, so ~50% of consent button taps reached the instance that didn't have the prefix in its in-memory `PendingResponseStore` — producing `"This notification has expired or was already answered"` while the on-disk record was still pending. The originating operation timed out at 90s and retried, recreating the same prompt — a silent consent-failure storm.
- **Telegram service**: HTTP-probe single-instance guard on port 5125; on startup, rebuild `PendingResponseStore` from `list_pending()` so a clean restart doesn't strand consent buttons sent by the previous instance.
- **Dispatcher**: `from_config` now consults `features.<surface>.wanted` so user opt-outs are actually honored (previously only checked the static `telegram.enabled`).
- **Gateway**: after a successful consent poll, call `store.respond_to_notification` so on-disk records leave `delivered` state instead of sitting until lazy expiry. Also fix `dispatcher.dismiss(notif)` (which AttributeErrored silently inside `except: pass`) → use the correct `dismiss_others(nid, surface, delivered)`.
- **Gateway timeout hint**: branch by capability dependency. Obsidian-bridge ops get an `obsidian_retry` hint; everything else gets `retry`. Both shapes accept `{"operation_id": "op_xxx"}`.
- **`obsidian_retry` API fix**: now accepts `operation_id` directly. The original signature required the agent to re-pass `capability` + `params` after every consent timeout, which defeated the affordance. With `operation_id`, it loads the original capability and params from the operation record. Explicit `capability` / `params` remain as overrides.
- **Separately — consent gate on preferences**: `setup_wizard` was registered with `mutates_state=False` even though `mode="preferences"` with `updates` rewrites `config.local.yaml`. An autonomous agent silently opted the user out of Hindsight + Telegram via this hole 36 hours before this PR. Fix: new `apply_preference_updates()` decorated with `@requires_consent("setup.write_preferences", risk="moderate")`; wizard delegates writes to it; `setup_wizard` now correctly `mutates_state=True`. Read-only modes still don't prompt — the gate fires at runtime only when `updates` is present.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/test_consent_auto_request.py tests/unit/test_bridge_retry.py tests/unit/test_gateway_prepare.py tests/unit/test_preferences.py tests/unit/test_wizard.py` — 110 passed, 0 failed
- [x] End-to-end live: `task_create` with `summary` → consent prompt landed on Dashboard + Telegram (no Obsidian bridge available at the moment) → user approved on Telegram → no "expired" message → on-disk record transitioned `delivered → responded` → retry via `operation_id` completed (`task_id: t-572608e2`).
- [ ] Re-test once with Obsidian bridge up to confirm `obsidian_retry({"operation_id": ...})` shape works against the consent timeout hint.
- [ ] Confirm a fresh agent session can no longer call `setup_wizard(mode="preferences", updates={...})` without triggering a consent prompt.

author: shaun0927
body:
Checklist before merging this PR:
- [x] Mentioned all issues that this PR fixes or addresses.
- [x] Summarized the updates of this PR under **Summary**.
- [x] Added an entry under **Unreleased** in the [Changelog](../CHANGELOG.md).

Fixes #3075.

### Summary

`StaticCovariatesTransformer` silently truncated the column mapping when the underlying `OneHotEncoder` uses `min_frequency` or `max_categories`. As a result, `transform(...)` dropped the synthetic `{col}_infrequent_sklearn` column and `inverse_transform(...)` raised `ValueError: Shape of the passed X data is not correct`.

### Root cause

In `_create_category_mappings` (`darts/dataprocessing/transformers/static_covariates_transformer.py:298-313`):

```python
expected_names = {
    f"{col}_{cat}" for cat in transformer_cat.categories_[i]
}
while (
    feat_idx < len(feature_names)
    and feature_names[feat_idx] in expected_names
):
    ...
```

`expected_names` is built from `transformer_cat.categories_[i]`. When sklearn groups low-frequency inputs via `min_frequency` / `max_categories`, it emits an additional synthetic feature `{col}_infrequent_sklearn` that is **not** in `categories_`. The `while` loop therefore stops before consuming it, the feature is omitted from `col_map_cat`, transformed static covariates are one column short, and `OneHotEncoder.inverse_transform` refuses the shape.

`#3065` introduced this `expected_names` set to cover the `drop='first'` / `drop='if_binary'` case. That fix is correct and remains unchanged; this PR only widens the set so it matches sklearn's full output for `min_frequency` / `max_categories`.

### Fix

```diff
 expected_names = {
     f"{col}_{cat}" for cat in transformer_cat.categories_[i]
 }
+# When ``min_frequency`` or ``max_categories`` is used, sklearn
+# emits an additional synthetic feature called
+# ``{col}_infrequent_sklearn`` which is not present in
+# ``categories_``. Include it so the mapping is not
+# silently truncated.
+expected_names.add(f"{col}_infrequent_sklearn")
 while (
     feat_idx < len(feature_names)
     and feature_names[feat_idx] in expected_names
 ):
```

The literal `"infrequent_sklearn"` is sklearn's documented feature name for the collapsed bucket (see `OneHotEncoder.get_feature_names_out`), so augmenting the set is sufficient and keeps the existing `drop` behaviour untouched.

### Tests

Added `test_one_hot_encoder_with_infrequent_sklearn` to `darts/tests/dataprocessing/transformers/test_static_covariates_transformer.py`, parametrized over `min_frequency=2` and `max_categories=2`. For each variant the test:

1. Builds a list of `TimeSeries` with a single `country` static covariate where one category ("JP") is infrequent,
2. Asserts that the transformed static covariates carry every column that `transformer_cat.get_feature_names_out(...)` emits (including `country_infrequent_sklearn`),
3. Round-trips via `inverse_transform` and asserts that frequent inputs map back to their original value while infrequent inputs map to sklearn's `"infrequent_sklearn"` sentinel (this is sklearn's own contract).

### TDD verification

Without the fix, the new test fails:

```
AssertionError: assert ['country_KR', 'country_US'] == ['country_KR', 'country_US', 'country_infrequent_sklearn']
FAILED darts/tests/dataprocessing/transformers/test_static_covariates_transformer.py::TestStaticCovariatesTransformer::test_one_hot_encoder_with_infrequent_sklearn[enc_kwargs0]
```

With the fix applied, both the new tests and every existing `one_hot_encoder_*` test pass:

```
$ pytest darts/tests/dataprocessing/transformers/test_static_covariates_transformer.py \
  -k "infrequent_sklearn or one_hot_encoder_with_drop"
6 passed, 8 deselected in 7.25s
```

### Other Information

None.

author: coreyrdean
body:
Closes #52.

## Why

After a `clauck doctor` dry run, the user has to scroll up through the report, extract the recommended action, and hand-compose `clauck doctor --fix "..."`. This is friction on every invocation and worse when multiple findings exist — users either skip the fix or miscompose it. The `--fix` flow is only useful if the handoff from dry → fix is effortless.

## How

DRY mode's final exec message is now a structured JSON object instead of free-form markdown:

```json
{"report": "<markdown>", "fix_instruction": "<single-line imperative> | null"}
```

`cmd_doctor` parses the result, prints the `report` markdown as today, and — if a `fix_instruction` was queued and the CLI is attached to a tty — prompts:

```
  Queued fix: clauck doctor --fix "<instruction>"
  Proceed with fix? [Y/n]
```

On confirm it `os.execvp`s back into `clauck doctor --fix <instruction>`, preserving `--unsafe` only if the original invocation was `--unsafe`. The `fix_instruction` is passed as a single argv element — no shell expansion, no re-quoting.

Guard rails on `fix_instruction`: must be a non-empty string, single line, no embedded double-quotes (display sanity when echoed inside the outer `"..."`). If parsing fails (malformed JSON, missing `report`), the CLI falls back to printing the raw result as markdown with no queued fix — graceful degradation to pre-schema behavior.

The prompt also instructs the model to include per-finding `clauck doctor --fix "..."` code blocks under each actionable finding so the user still has copy-paste fallbacks when they want to apply only one fix from a multi-finding report.

## Why a schema, not a trailer

Initial draft embedded the fix instruction in an `<!-- DOCTOR_FIX_META {...} -->` HTML-comment trailer and regex-stripped it from the output. Switched to a proper schema field after review — the stage-1 interpreter already uses this pattern (`_parse_interpreter_result`), and a typed contract removes regex brittleness and leaves room to grow (per-item fix objects, severity, etc.) without more string hacks.

## Test plan

- [ ] `clauck doctor <actionable-context>` prints the report and ends with `Proceed with fix? [Y/n]`. Enter or `y` executes the fix; `n` exits cleanly.
- [ ] `clauck doctor <healthy-context>` (or empty / advisory-only report) prints and exits without prompting.
- [ ] `clauck doctor --unsafe <actionable-context>` carries `--unsafe` into the queued fix; plain `clauck doctor` never elevates to `--unsafe`.
- [ ] Piped / non-tty invocation (`clauck doctor ... | cat`) skips the prompt.
- [ ] Malformed JSON from the model: report still prints as raw markdown, no prompt, exit clean.
- [ ] `clauck doctor --fix` (explicit fix mode) skips schema parsing and behaves exactly as before.

author: railway-app[bot]
body:
## Problem

All async route handlers across the Express app were registered directly without a catch bridge to Express's `next(error)`. If an async controller throws before its own `try/catch` fires — for example during a MongoDB connection hiccup or an unexpected runtime error — the rejected promise goes unhandled and Express never receives the error, causing the request to hang and the reverse proxy to return a 502. The `GET /api/site-settings` and `GET /api/services` endpoints were the reported symptoms, but every route in the app shared the same exposure.

## Solution

Created `vedteix-backend/utils/asyncHandler.js`, a one-liner wrapper that resolves the handler's promise and forwards any rejection to `next`, connecting it to the existing `errorMiddleware`. Updated all 16 route files (`siteSettingsRoutes`, `serviceRoutes`, `appointmentsRoutes`, `authRoutes`, `blogRoutes`, `chatApiRoutes`, `chatRoutes`, `contactRoutes`, `dashboardRoutes`, `invoiceRoutes`, `jobRoutes`, `leadsRoutes`, `newsletterRoutes`, `portfolioRoutes`, `technologyRoutes`, `testimonialsRoutes`, `uploadRoutes`) to wrap every async handler with `asyncHandler(...)`. The controllers' own `try/catch` blocks are preserved as a first line of defence; `asyncHandler` acts as a guaranteed safety net for anything that slips through.

- **Modified** `vedteix-backend/routes/siteSettingsRoutes.js`

author: ousamabenyounes
body:
## Summary

Fixes #31722.

`isComponentName` in `rules-of-hooks` required the identifier to start with an uppercase letter, so an underscore-prefixed component like `_InternalComponent` (a common private-naming convention for "not-for-external-use" components) was rejected as neither a React component nor a custom Hook. Users then got a confusing `rules-of-hooks` error inside what is clearly a component body.

The fix widens the regex to `/^_?[A-Z]/` so a single leading underscore is permitted provided it is immediately followed by an uppercase letter. Names whose first alphabetic character is lowercase (including `_notAComponent`) continue to be rejected.

## Repro

```js
// Before: flagged with "React Hook 'useSomeHook' is called in function
//         '_SomeComponent' that is neither a React function component
//         nor a custom React Hook function."
// After: no error.
function _SomeComponent() {
  const result = useSomeHook();
  return result;
}
```

## How did you test this change?

Added two cases to `ESLintRulesOfHooks-test.js`:

- **valid**: `function _ComponentWithHook() { useHook(); }` (new behavior)
- **invalid**: `function _notAComponent() { useHook(); }` → still errors (regression guard: the underscore exemption only applies when followed by an uppercase letter)

- `ESLintRuleExhaustiveDeps-test.js`: **3644 passed / 0 failed**

### Profile system

- Replace Claude Code's `auth.method` enum (`api-key`, `oauth-token`, `gateway`) with a **named profiles system** supporting runtime switching via `claude-switch <name>` without a Nix rebuild
  - Three profile types: **`subscription`** (interactive OAuth via `.credentials.json` for full subscription features), **`oauth-token`** (env-injected token for `user:inference` scope), and **`api-key`** (third-party / gateway endpoints)
  - Each profile generates a shell script (Nix store derivation) deployed to `~/.local/state/claude-code/profiles/`, with an `active-profile` symlink selecting the active one at runtime
- Add a **profile loader** sourced by the wrapper at startup that unsets all auth env vars (hardcoded blocklist + dynamic union across profiles) before sourcing the active profile — prevents stale vars when switching between profile types
- Add **`claude-switch` CLI** (Nix-generated, on PATH) for listing and switching profiles with validation and colored output

### Infrastructure

- Make NixOS secrets provisioning **dynamic** — replace hardcoded enum and `age.secrets` attrset with generation from the union of all profiles' `requiredSecrets`
- Add **`lib/claude-profiles.nix`** as a parameter-free profile library (5 profiles: `official`, `official-token`, `corp-gateway`, `yescode`, `ikuncode`) wired once in `home/hakula.nix` via `lib.mkDefault`, so each host's entire auth config is `hakula.claude-code.auth.defaultProfile = "<name>";`

### Housekeeping

- Rename `claude-code-api-key` → `claude-yescode-api-key` and add `claude-ikuncode-api-key` for consistent namespacing of third-party API key secrets
- Rename `auth.nix` → `profiles.nix`; extract shell scripts to `scripts/` subdir

## Architecture

- **Why three profile types**: Claude Code's auth precedence is `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` > `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`+`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` > `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` > `.credentials.json`. The `subscription` type sets *no* auth env vars, letting Claude Code fall through to interactive `.credentials.json` OAuth which grants full subscription scopes (usage tracking, rate limit tier). The `oauth-token` type injects `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` for `user:inference` scope only. The `api-key` type sets `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` + `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` for third-party / gateway endpoints.
- **Why a hardcoded auth env blocklist**: The profile loader always unsets `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, and `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` regardless of which profiles are declared. This prevents externally-set auth vars (e.g., from parent shells or dotfiles) from bypassing profile switching. Per-profile model overrides and extra env vars are additionally collected at build time.
- **Why `~/.local/state/` for the symlink**: The active profile selection is mutable runtime state (changes without rebuild). XDG Base Directory spec puts runtime state in `~/.local/state/`, separate from `~/.config/` (Nix-managed). The profile *scripts* are immutable store derivations symlinked into this dir; only the `active-profile` pointer is mutable.
- **Why `--run source` over `--set`**: Profiles need all auth vars to come from a single sourced script so switching is atomic. `--run "source ${profileLoader}"` evaluates at each invocation, reading the current symlink target.
- **Why unset all vars before sourcing**: Switching from `corp-gateway` (which sets `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` and model overrides) to `yescode` (which doesn't) would leave stale env vars. The loader unsets the full union before sourcing — clean slate per invocation.
- **Why `activation` only creates symlink if missing / broken**: Preserves the user's runtime profile choice across `nixos-rebuild` / `home-manager switch`. The `[ ! -e "$link" ]` check returns false for existing valid symlinks and true for both missing and broken (stale target) symlinks.
- **Why dynamic NixOS secrets**: The previous hardcoded `age.secrets` block required touching the NixOS module for every new secret. `builtins.listToAttrs (map ... requiredSecrets)` generates the attrset from whatever the HM layer declares.
- **Why `lib/claude-profiles.nix` + wiring in `home/hakula.nix`**: Three hosts share the same 5 profiles — only `defaultProfile` differs. The library is a parameter-free data file, wired via `lib.mkDefault` in the shared HM entry point so every host reduces to one line. `corpDomain` is imported internally; `secretsDir` is no longer needed because `extraSecretEnv` lets the profile reference a secret by name and have the module resolve the absolute path.
- **Why `extraSecretEnv`**: Some profiles need env vars whose values are paths to provisioned secrets (e.g. `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=${secretsDir}/corp-cachain.crt`). Expressing this via `extraEnv` required string-interpolating `${secretsDir}` in the profile library and manually listing the secret name for provisioning. `extraSecretEnv` takes env var → secret name, lets the module resolve the absolute path at script-generation time, and auto-folds referenced secrets into `requiredSecrets`. Shares the POSIX key-name check with `extraEnv` and is forbidden for `subscription`.
- **Why `claude-` prefix on third-party secrets**: Namespaces third-party API keys (`claude-yescode-api-key`, `claude-ikuncode-api-key`) alongside existing `claude-code-oauth-token`. The LiteLLM key and corp CA cert are left unprefixed as shared infrastructure.

## Test plan

- [x] `nix flake check` passes (pre-commit hooks, all systems)
- [x] `nix build '.#homeConfigurations.hakula-linux.activationPackage'` succeeds
- [x] `nix build '.#packages.x86_64-linux.hakula-devvm-docker'` succeeds
- [x] Generated profile scripts verified correct (5 profiles: official, official-token, corp-gateway, yescode, ikuncode)
- [x] Profile loader correctly unsets all auth env vars (hardcoded blocklist + dynamic union) before sourcing
- [x] `claude-switch` script lists profiles, validates input, updates symlink
- [x] Wrapper sources profile loader before proxy and MCP guard (correct ordering)
- [x] NixOS servers (us-1 through sg-1) build without profiles (empty `profiles = {}`, no auth vars)
- [x] `nh home switch` activates successfully on hakula-linux
- [x] `claude-switch official` switches to subscription mode (no auth env vars, uses `.credentials.json`)
- [x] `claude-switch corp-gateway` restores corp gateway auth with model overrides
- [x] Verify `nix build '.#darwinConfigurations.hakula-macbook.system'` succeeds (CI)

author: trankly
body:
## Summary

Three-path routing that classifies inputs before any processing:

- **Image (JPEG/PNG/TIFF)** → vision model directly, no conversion
- **Scanned PDF (no text layer)** → render pages to PNG → vision model  
- **Digital PDF (has text layer)** → native text extraction → LLM (unchanged)

Configurable via schema YAML:
```yaml
ocr:
  vision_bypass:
    enabled: true
    when:
      - page_count <= 3
      - ocr_confidence < 0.70
      - schema_hint: receipt
```

## SROIE Benchmark (20 receipt images)

| Field | Text (OCR→LLM) | Vision (direct) | Delta |
|-------|----------------|-----------------|-------|
| Company | 60% | **95%** | **+35%** |
| Total | 90% | **95%** | +5% |
| Date | 75% | 75% | — |
| Address | 28% | 19% | -9% |
| **Overall** | 63.3% | **71.0%** | **+7.7%** |
| Latency | 6.3s | **3.0s** | **2× faster** |

The +35% on company is the OCR error accumulation elimination — thermal receipt text garbles through OCR but the vision model reads it directly from the image.

## New files

- `services/extract/vision.py` — VisionBypassConfig, should_bypass(), estimate_ocr_confidence(), vision_extract()
- `services/parse/main.py` — classify_input(), image_to_base64(), pdf_pages_to_images(), _is_scanned_pdf()
- `tests/bench/bench_sroie.py` — benchmark script
- `tests/bench/receipt_schema.yaml` — receipt schema with vision bypass config

author: verkyyi
body:
## Summary
Make the GitHub activity fetch script self-healing on fresh checkouts. Currently the workflow 403s fail with \`ENOENT\` because \`fetch-github-activity.mjs\` writes \`data/github/activity.json\` without first ensuring the parent directory exists.

## Repro
1. Fork \`agentfolio\` as a derived deploy and overlay framework files without copying \`data/\`.
2. Trigger \`Refresh GitHub Activity\` workflow.
3. See: \`Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '…/data/github/activity.json'\`.

This matches what happened in \`verkyyi/verkyyi.github.io\` after the framework overlay — the \`data/github/.gitkeep\` placeholder didn't carry over, so the workflow broke on first run.

## Fix
One-line change: add \`await mkdir(path.dirname(outPath), { recursive: true });\` before the \`writeFile\` call, and import \`mkdir\` alongside \`writeFile\`.

\`\`\`diff
-import { writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
+import { mkdir, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
…
   const outPath = path.resolve('data/github/activity.json');
+  await mkdir(path.dirname(outPath), { recursive: true });
   await writeFile(outPath, …);
\`\`\`

\`{ recursive: true }\` is a no-op when the directory already exists, so this doesn't change behavior for existing deploys.

## Side benefit
The \`data/github/.gitkeep\` placeholder becomes optional going forward. Not removing it in this PR (keeps the change minimal and avoids churn), but future forks no longer depend on it.

## Test plan
- [ ] Unit tests (\`npm test\`) still pass — they exercise \`buildActivity\`, not \`main()\`, so this is unchanged
- [ ] Delete \`data/github/\` locally, run \`node scripts/fetch-github-activity.mjs\` with a valid \`GITHUB_TOKEN\` + \`GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER\`, confirm it creates the directory and writes the file

author: technophile-04
body:
### To test:

Make sure to have clean install of se-2 because branching from `main` comes with old gitignored files which might cause type checks failure or deployments error

```shell
git clone --branch hardhat-v3-migration https://github.com/scaffold-eth/scaffold-eth-2.git se-2-hardhat-v3
```

```shell
cd se-2-hardhat-v3
yarn install
```

### Description: 

Migrated hardhat v2 -> hardhat v3 and hardhat-deploy v1 -> hardhat-deploy -> v2. 

All the magical commands and their flags work in the same way, without needing to bend and add our extra glue to make them work . 

I think this is ready to be tested as initial iteration 🙌

#### Some things to know: 

- Everything is ESM. `"type": "module"` in `package.json`, `module: "node16"` in tsconfig, `.js` extensions on every relative import
- `hardhat compile` must run before `hardhat deploy` because deploy scripts statically import from `generated/artifacts/`, and Node resolves those imports before any code runs. Our `yarn deploy` script chains `hardhat compile && tsx scripts/runHardhatDeployWithPK.ts` for exactly this reason.
- Swapped `ts-node` for `tsx` because the`ts-node` was pain with `module: node16` 
- Dropped `hardhat-gas-reporter` for now since it hasn't shipped a v3-compatible release yet (every version through 2.3.0 pins `hardhat: ^2.16.0`)
- `--reset` isn't a built-in CLI flag in v2. v2 exposes `alwaysOverride: true` per-deploy call instead. We added back the flag via a task override in `hardhat.config.ts` + a `deployWithReset` wrapper in `rocketh/config.ts`. Filed [wighawag/hardhat-deploy#592](https://github.com/wighawag/hardhat-deploy/issues/592) asking for native support.
- Etherscan V2 error messages are misleading. "Missing or unsupported chainid parameter" usually means "unsupported," not "missing." Chain 31337 (local hardhat) returns this error. 
- TODO: Get hardhat-verify working, currently the base commands uses `rocketh/verfifier` which is hardhat-deploy compatible

### Some notes: 

<details>

<summary>
    What's rocketh
</summary>

Rocketh is a framework-agnostic deployment engine. In v1, hardhat-deploy was a monolith tightly coupled to hardhat 2 internals. When hardhat 3 rewrote the plugin system, that coupling broke. So v2 pulled the deployment engine out into rocketh (framework-agnostic) and rebuilt hardhat-deploy v2 as a thin adapter that bridges hardhat 3 into rocketh. 

Architecture:

```
hardhat 3 (compilation, networks, tasks)
   └── hardhat-deploy v2 (plugin adapter)
         └── rocketh (deployment engine)
                ├── @rocketh/deploy        (deploy function)
                ├── @rocketh/read-execute  (read/write)
                ├── @rocketh/signer        (signing)
                └── @rocketh/node          (file-based env loading)
```

**Why three files under `packages/hardhat/rocketh/`**

- **`config.ts`** — named accounts (`deployer` at index 0), signer protocols (registers `privateKey` from `@rocketh/signer`), and the extension registry (`deploy` + `read` + `execute`). 
- **`deploy.ts`** — one-line glue: exports `deployScript` from `setupDeployScripts`. Every `deploy/*.ts` file imports this to wrap its script body.
- **`environment.ts`** — exports `loadAndExecuteDeploymentsFromFiles` and `loadEnvironmentFromHardhat`. These are the loaders tests and post-deploy scripts use to get a typed `env` with all deployments resolved.

The end users probably won't be required to touch this files. 

</details>


### Future TODO's 

- Using hardhat's configuration variable + keystore  
- Having the solidity test file examples as well (according to hardhat docs, both `.ts` and `.t.sol` helps in different-different way) 
- Migrating to viem 
- Tinkering with ignition, and see if it's good fit for us

## Summary
- Escape parentheses and square brackets in the directory portion of glob patterns before passing to `fast-glob`, so they are treated as literal path characters instead of extglob syntax
- Add `escapeGlobPath()` helper that targets only `()` and `[]` — characters proven to break `fast-glob`/`picomatch` matching in filesystem paths
- Add 4 test cases covering parentheses, square brackets, curly braces, and non-glob generates with special-character directories

## Test plan
- [x] All 12 existing + new tests pass (`vitest run test/core/artifact-graph/outputs.test.ts`)
- [x] Verified glob patterns resolve correctly when directory contains `()`, `[]`, `{}`

author: hua-bang
body:
## Summary
This PR refactors the canvas store's external node merging logic to improve reliability and safety when handling concurrent writes between the renderer and canvas-cli. The main improvements include extracting disk read logic into a dedicated function with retry logic, converting error handling from exceptions to explicit result types, and introducing a sentinel value to safely skip empty writes when disk state cannot be verified.

## Key Changes

- **Extract `readDiskCanvas` function**: Separated disk I/O and JSON parsing into a dedicated async function with configurable retry logic (3 attempts with 30ms backoff). This handles the common case where canvas-cli is mid-write, causing JSON parse errors that resolve on retry.

- **Introduce `DiskReadOutcome` discriminated union**: Replaced ad-hoc error handling with explicit result types (`ok`, `missing`, `unparseable`, `ioerror`), making error cases more explicit and easier to reason about.

- **Add `SKIP_WRITE` sentinel**: When the renderer requests an empty canvas write but we cannot verify the disk state (due to I/O or parse errors), return a special sentinel instead of throwing. This prevents unhandledRejection errors in the lock chain while still protecting against data loss.

- **Flatten `mergeExternalNodes` logic**: Removed nested try-catch block and simplified control flow by handling disk read outcomes at the top level. The merge reconciliation logic remains unchanged but is now more readable.

- **Improve error messaging**: Changed from throwing errors to console.warn for the empty-write-with-unverifiable-disk case, making the behavior more graceful and the intent clearer.

- **Add unhandledRejection guard in `withSaveLock`**: Added a `.catch(() => undefined)` on the tracked promise to prevent unhandledRejection errors when a save fails and no subsequent save arrives before microtask queue checks. The actual error is still propagated to the caller via the returned promise.

## Notable Implementation Details

- The retry logic in `readDiskCanvas` specifically targets the race condition where canvas-cli is writing the file. A truncated/half-written file produces a JSON parse error that typically resolves within 30ms.
- The `SKIP_WRITE` sentinel is checked at two points in the save handler: after the first merge and after the second merge, ensuring empty writes are skipped consistently.
- The merge reconciliation rules (timestamp-based conflict resolution, CLI deletion detection, external node addition) remain functionally identical but are now easier to follow without nested exception handling.

author: shibukazu
body:
## Summary
`npm install -g npm@latest` in `release.yml` fails due to a bug in the npm bundled with Node 22, so remove that step and instead invoke `npm version` / `npm publish` through `npx -y npm@latest`.

## Error observed
```
npm error code MODULE_NOT_FOUND
npm error Cannot find module 'promise-retry'
```

A known issue where `npm install -g npm@latest` breaks on the npm bundled with Node 22 (arborist can't resolve promise-retry internally).

## Fix
- Remove the `Upgrade npm for trusted publishing` step
- `npm version ...` → `npx -y npm@latest version ...`
- `npm publish ...` → `npx -y npm@latest publish ...`

This pulls a fresh, trusted-publishing / provenance-capable npm on the fly (without mutating the environment).

## Verification
Verified on this branch by temporarily adding a push trigger and running the workflow in dry-run mode: bump → commit → tag → dry-run publish ran to completion. The final commit removes the push trigger and restores `workflow_dispatch`-only.

author: luofang34
body:
## Summary

Replaces the three loosely-coupled, platform-ambiguous fields `host_os`, `host_arch`, and `libc_version` on `EnvFingerprint` with one tagged enum:

```rust
enum Host {
    Linux   { arch, libc, kernel },
    Macos   { arch, version },
    Windows { arch, version, build },
}
```

- `#[serde(tag = "os", rename_all = "lowercase")]` → JSON looks like `"host": { "os": "macos", "arch": "aarch64", "version": "26.4" }`.
- Per-OS fields force each platform to name the shape of its evidence structurally, rather than relying on string-typed `Option<String>` sentinels. A DO-330 audit asking "what does `libc_version` mean on Windows?" now has a structural answer.
- **`target_triple` stays a sibling field** on `EnvFingerprint`. A Linux host cross-compiling to `aarch64-unknown-none-elf` has distinct host and target attributes, and merging them would lose evidence.
- Unknown hosts are a `compile_error`, not an `Option<String>` fallback — an unknown platform slipping into a cert bundle as a stringly-typed tuple is exactly the silent degradation we're trying to eliminate.

## schema_version (intentionally not bumped)

`schema_version` remains `"0.0.1"`. The project has no public release, no crates.io publication, and no stability commitment (see Project Status / Platform Support sections added in #4). Bumping would imply a stability guarantee we haven't given. If/when we cut a public 0.1.0, that's the right time.

## Detection helpers

Split by target_os:

- `detect_libc_linux()` — `ldd --version` first line, falls back to musl check, `None` on both-failed.
- `detect_kernel_linux()` — `uname -r`.
- `detect_macos_version()` — `sw_vers -productVersion`.
- `detect_windows_version()` — `cmd /c ver`, bracket-extracted (`"Microsoft Windows [Version 10.0.22000.2538]"` → `"10.0.22000.2538"`).
- `parse_windows_build()` — third dotted component (→ `22000`).

## Schema and validator

- `schemas/env.schema.json` rewritten: `host` is a `oneOf` over three object shapes, `host_os`/`host_arch`/`libc_version` removed, `host` and `target_triple` added to `required`, `additionalProperties: false` on each variant.
- `cargo-evidence schema validate`'s runtime validator (`validate_env_schema`) adds `host`, `target_triple` to required and enforces `host.os ∈ {linux, macos, windows}` + `host.arch` is a string.

## Fixture regenerated in this PR

`crates/cargo-evidence/tests/fixtures/golden-dev-bundle/env.json` no longer has flat `host_os`/`host_arch`/`libc_version`; it has the new `host` object. `content_hash` rotates from `56d9d6a7…d13259e` → `570b553b…be4953`. The fixture was generated on a clean worktree with `--skip-tests` and committed byte-for-byte, so the existing `.gitattributes binary` rule and the `golden_bundle_has_no_carriage_returns` assertion keep working across platforms.

## Tests

Four new unit tests in `env::tests`:

- `test_host_linux_roundtrip` — exact JSON shape for `{os: "linux", arch, libc, kernel}`.
- `test_host_macos_roundtrip` — exact JSON shape for `{os: "macos", arch, version}`.
- `test_host_windows_roundtrip` — exact JSON shape for `{os: "windows", arch, version, build}`.
- `test_host_optional_fields_omitted_when_none` — proves `None` fields are omitted (not null) so bundles stay byte-stable when detection fails.

Plus `test_env_fingerprint_fields` updated to construct a `Host::Linux` instead of the old flat fields.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean
- [x] `cargo test --workspace` — 93/93 pass (+4 Host roundtrips)
- [x] `cargo-evidence schema show env` emits the new shape
- [x] `cargo-evidence schema validate <fixture>/env.json` succeeds
- [x] All three golden tests green (verify / no-CR / self-diff)

author: jonas-du-bois
body:
💡 **What**:
Added an optional `limitContacts` parameter to `MessageRepository.getConversationsForReport`. If provided, it first aggregates the top `N` contact IDs for the day using a fast `COUNT(*)` query, and then uses an `IN (...)` clause to fetch only the message payloads for those specific contacts. `TelegramCommandHandler.#generateBriefReport` was updated to utilize this new parameter.

🎯 **Why**:
Previously, generating reports that only needed the top 5 contacts (like the Telegram brief report) would still fetch *every single message* from the database for the current day, load them all into Node.js memory, group them, and sort them. This is inefficient and scales poorly as message volume increases.

📊 **Impact**:
Dramatically reduces database I/O and Node.js memory allocation. Benchmarks showed a ~3.8x speedup (from ~750ms to ~190ms) on a heavy simulated dataset with thousands of users.

🔬 **Measurement**:
Verified functionality using `node --test tests/integration/MessageRepository.report.test.js`. Impact was measured using temporary scripts prior to submission.

### Motivation

`WebSocketPluginConfiguration` currently passes a mutable `WebsocketClientSpec.Builder` in a way that may cause builder state to be reused across WebSocket handshakes.

Following the same approach discussed in Spring Cloud Gateway issue #2215 / PR #2216, each handshake should use a fresh builder instance to avoid cross-request state leakage.

### Description

- Updated `WebSocketPluginConfiguration#reactorNettyWebSocketClient` to provide a `Supplier<WebsocketClientSpec.Builder>` that creates a **new builder on each invocation**.
- Extended the existing `testReactorNettyWebSocketClient` (as requested) to verify behavior by checking that the internal builder supplier returns different builder instances across calls.

### Related Links

- https://github.com/spring-cloud/spring-cloud-gateway/issues/2215
- https://github.com/spring-cloud/spring-cloud-gateway/pull/2216

author: mcfn
body:
## Summary
Adds `browser start --auto-connect` (env `ACTIONBOOK_AUTO_CONNECT`) to automatically discover and attach to a locally-running Chrome with remote debugging enabled, without requiring the user to know the debug port. Inspired by vercel-labs/agent-browser's auto-connect feature.

Closes ACT-953.

## New API surface
- CLI flag: `browser start --auto-connect`
- Env: `ACTIONBOOK_AUTO_CONNECT`
- Error codes:
  - `CHROME_AUTO_CONNECT_NOT_FOUND` — no `DevToolsActivePort` file and no candidate port responding
  - `CHROME_CDP_UNREACHABLE` — candidate port found but HTTP/CDP probe failed (stale file, port occupied, Chrome exited)

## Discovery order
1. Read Chrome's `DevToolsActivePort` file (first line is the port):
   - macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/DevToolsActivePort`
   - Linux: `~/.config/google-chrome/DevToolsActivePort`
   - Windows: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Google\Chrome\User Data\DevToolsActivePort`
2. Fallback: probe `[9222, 9229]` via `GET http://127.0.0.1:<port>/json/version` with a 500ms timeout.
3. First success returns a `ws://…/devtools/browser/<id>` endpoint.
4. Stale `DevToolsActivePort` (file exists but unreachable) falls through to port probe.

## Semantics
- Session mode = Local (attaches to existing Chrome, does not spawn).
- Mutually exclusive with `--cdp-endpoint` (including config/env-derived), `--mode cloud`, `-p/--provider`, `--mode extension`.
- `--auto-connect` skips the local-session reuse path so it always performs discovery.
- `browser close --session` releases the attachment; it does **not** kill the external Chrome (locked by E2E).

## Test plan
- Unit: `parse_devtools_active_port`, platform path resolver.
- Integration (mock HTTP server): `/json/version` success / 500 / timeout / all-fail → NOT_FOUND; stale file → UNREACHABLE.
- E2E:
  - `auto_connect_attaches_to_running_chrome`
  - `auto_connect_without_running_chrome_returns_not_found`
  - `close_attached_auto_connect_session_does_not_kill_chrome`
  - `auto_connect_ignores_existing_local_session_reuse` (regression from Codex P1)
  - `auto_connect_conflicts_with_config_cdp_endpoint` (regression from Codex P2)
- Windows E2E currently `#[cfg_attr(windows, ignore)]` pending manual smoke.

## Files changed
- `packages/cli/src/daemon/browser.rs` — discovery helpers + unit/integration tests
- `packages/cli/src/error.rs` — `ChromeAutoConnectNotFound` / `ChromeCdpUnreachable` variants with `error_code()` + `hint()`
- `packages/cli/src/browser/session/start.rs` — `Cmd` flag + validation + auto-discover call, reuse guard updated
- `packages/cli/src/browser/session/restart.rs`, `src/config.rs`, `src/main.rs` — `Cmd` literal updates
- `packages/cli/tests/e2e/auto_connect.rs` (new) + registered in `tests/e2e/main.rs`

## Follow-ups (out of scope)
- Brave / Edge / Chromium-branded browsers (separate feature).
- Custom `--chrome-user-data-dir` flag.
- Configurable probe port list.
- Windows E2E automation.

### GitHub Vulnerability Alerts

#### [GHSA-3xc5-wrhm-f963](https://redirect.github.com/go-git/go-git/security/advisories/GHSA-3xc5-wrhm-f963)

### Impact
`go-git` may leak HTTP authentication credentials when following redirects during smart-HTTP clone and fetch operations.

If a remote repository responds to the initial `/info/refs` request with a redirect to a different host, go-git updates the session endpoint to the redirected location and reuses the original authentication for subsequent requests. This can result in the credentials (e.g. Authorization headers) being sent to an unintended host.

An attacker controlling or influencing the redirect target can capture these credentials and potentially reuse them to access the victim’s repositories or other resources, depending on the scope of the credential.

**Clients using `go-git` exclusively with trusted remotes (for example, GitHub or GitLab), and over a secure HTTPS connection, are not affected by this issue.** The risk arises when interacting with untrusted or misconfigured Git servers, or when using unsecured HTTP connections, which is not recommended. Such configurations also expose clients to a broader class of security risks beyond this issue, including credential interception and tampering of repository data.

### Patches
Users should upgrade to `v5.18.0`, or `v6.0.0-alpha.2`, in order to mitigate this vulnerability. Versions prior to v5 are likely to be affected, users are recommended to upgrade to a supported `go-git` version.

The patched versions add support for configuring [followRedirects](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-config#Documentation/git-config.txt-httpfollowRedirects). In line with upstream behaviour, the default is now `initial`, while users can opt into `FollowRedirects` or `NoFollowRedirects` programmatically.

#### [CVE-2026-39883](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/security/advisories/GHSA-hfvc-g4fc-pqhx)

## Summary

The fix for GHSA-9h8m-3fm2-qjrq (CVE-2026-24051) changed the Darwin `ioreg` command to use an absolute path but left the BSD `kenv` command using a bare name, allowing the same PATH hijacking attack on BSD and Solaris platforms.

## Root Cause

`sdk/resource/host_id.go` line 42:

    if result, err := r.execCommand("kenv", "-q", "smbios.system.uuid"); err == nil {

Compare with the fixed Darwin path at line 58:

    result, err := r.execCommand("/usr/sbin/ioreg", "-rd1", "-c", "IOPlatformExpertDevice")

The `execCommand` helper at `sdk/resource/host_id_exec.go` uses `exec.Command(name, arg...)` which searches `$PATH` when the command name contains no path separator.

Affected platforms (per build tag in `host_id_bsd.go:4`): DragonFly BSD, FreeBSD, NetBSD, OpenBSD, Solaris.

The `kenv` path is reached when `/etc/hostid` does not exist (line 38-40), which is common on FreeBSD systems.

## Attack

1. Attacker has local access to a system running a Go application that imports `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk`
2. Attacker places a malicious `kenv` binary earlier in `$PATH`
3. Application initializes OpenTelemetry resource detection at startup
4. `hostIDReaderBSD.read()` calls `exec.Command("kenv", ...)` which resolves to the malicious binary
5. Arbitrary code executes in the context of the application

Same attack vector and impact as CVE-2026-24051.

## Suggested Fix

Use the absolute path:

    if result, err := r.execCommand("/bin/kenv", "-q", "smbios.system.uuid"); err == nil {

On FreeBSD, `kenv` is located at `/bin/kenv`.

author: malammar
body: Thanks for the buddy port. The animations are even better than the original Claude buddy! Here's my first contribution: ## Problem `installBuddyEditor` called `ctx.ui.setEditorComponent()` which overwrote the custom editor registered by `pi-powerline-footer`. Since powerline renders its entire status bar as the first line of its editor component, this silently wiped out both the powerline status bar **and** the buddy display. Additionally, the animation timer lived inside `BuddyEditor`, so removing the editor component broke sprite animation and bubble expiry. ## Changes ### `extension/editor.ts` - Remove both `ctx.ui.setEditorComponent()` calls from `installBuddyEditor` and `clearBuddyEditor` - Add `BubbleSpeechOverlay` class: a second non-capturing overlay anchored `bottom-right`, positioned to the upper-left of the sprite, rendering the bubble text in a rounded box with a `╲` tail pointing toward the buddy. Word-wraps text to fit the overlay width. - Capture TUI reference from the sprite overlay factory and export `requestOverlayRender()` so renders can be triggered from `index.ts` - Increase sprite right margin from 1 → 2 to avoid edge clipping ### `extension/index.ts` - Import and use `requestOverlayRender` instead of a dead local TUI ref - Move the 500ms animation interval (tick, bubble expiry, hearts reset) from `BuddyEditor` into `session_start` — works regardless of whether `setEditorComponent` is used - Remove the `belowEditor` widget (name/species/rarity line below input box) — info is available in the buddy card - Add `Ctrl+Shift+B` hotkey via `pi.registerShortcut` to toggle buddy visibility ### `tsconfig.json` + `check.sh` (new) - `tsconfig.json` for type-checking the extension against pi's published `.d.ts` files - `check.sh`: runs unit tests + type check; filters known pre-existing upstream errors so only newly introduced issues fail the check ## Preview

author: gitglimpse895
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes two bugs in `PyramidAttentionBroadcastHook.new_forward`:

**1. Redundant `iteration == 0` condition**
After every `reset_state()`, both `iteration` and `cache` are reset to `0` and `None` respectively. So at iteration 0, `self.state.cache is None` is always `True`, making `self.state.iteration == 0` permanently dead code that creates a misleading impression of two independent invariants.

**2. Stale cache leaking GPU VRAM**
When outside the active timestep range, the hook was unconditionally writing `self.state.cache = output`, holding a full hidden-state activation tensor on GPU until the next generation's `reset_state()` call. For video transformers with dozens of PAB-hooked layers, this accumulates hundreds of MBs of unreleased VRAM. The fix sets `self.state.cache = None` immediately when outside the range.

This is a re-submission of #13467 (accidentally self-closed). Apologies for the noise, @sayakpaul!

author: wkarts
body:
### Motivation

- Provide robust tooling to audit, replay and reconcile individual migrations and surface detailed history for operational remediation. 
- Protect runtime from accidental PSR-4/duplicate-class risks by scanning/quarantining suspicious PHP files before running `composer`/app code. 
- Improve UX and compactness of the updater UI and add controls to opt-in migration replay from the UI/CLI.

### Description

- Added a PSR-4 guard: new `Psr4Sanitizer` support class, `Psr4SanitizeStep` pipeline step, configuration under `updater.psr4_guard`, service provider bindings, and env examples (quarantine/delete modes, filename/directory patterns). 
- Implemented a migrations audit feature: new routes (`updater.migrations.*`), views (`sections/migrations.blade.php`, `sections/migrations-show.blade.php`), controller actions (`OperationsController::migrationsAuditIndex`, `migrationAuditShow`, `reapplyMigration`), and UI controls to queue/run individual reapply with reason. 
- Enhanced idempotent migration engine: `IdempotentMigrationService` supports `replay_from_start` to forcibly reapply migrations (removes repository entry then reapplies), better error classification, recoverable-runtime warnings, safer path resolution and more robust reporting via `MigrationRunReporter`. 
- Persisted migration runtime bookkeeping: extended `StateStore` with tables and methods for migration attempts, reconcilations and reapply queue (`updater_migration_attempts`, `updater_migration_reconciliations`, `updater_migration_reapply_queue`) and helper APIs. 
- Improved migration drift detection and reconciler: `MigrationDriftDetector` extracts table names more safely, `MigrationReconciler` validates more object types (columns) and records reconciliation events into state store. 
- Updated pipeline and migrate flow: `MigrateStep` now prefers running `updater:migrate` in-process via Artisan, falls back to `IdempotentMigrationService`, and finally to a subprocess; added `--replay-from-start`/`--replay-migrations-from-start` flags propagation through `UpdateRunCommand`, `UpdaterMigrateCommand`, `TriggerDispatcher`, `UpdaterKernel` dry-run plan and `UpdaterKernel` pipeline registration. 
- Reduced default auto-reconciliation: changed `updater.migrate.reconcile_already_exists` default to `false` and adjusted places where reconciliation behavior is controlled.

author: koseonje
body:
## 문제 & 동기

v0.1.0 부트스트랩 당시 `main == develop` 상태에서 `dorny/paths-filter`가 default branch와 비교해 diff가 비는 문제가 있어 default branch를 `main`으로 전환했음. 이로 인해 일상 개발에서 PR UI / `gh pr create` 기본 base가 `main`이 되어 feature PR 작성 시 실수 위험이 누적됨.

이제 `main`이 자기 히스토리를 가져 부트스트랩 조건은 해소됐지만, **default를 곧바로 `develop`으로 되돌리면** `workflow_dispatch`로 deploy-prod를 수동 재실행할 때 paths-filter가 default(develop)와 비교해 릴리즈 직후 시점에는 diff가 비어 backend/frontend step이 skip되는 사고가 재발할 수 있음.

- 후속 작업으로 default branch 전환(`gh api ... -f default_branch=develop`) 예정
- 본 PR은 그 전환을 안전하게 만드는 **선행 조건**

## 변경 내용

- `deploy-prod.yml`의 paths-filter에 base를 명시적으로 지정 → default branch 폴백 의존 제거
  - push 이벤트: `github.event.before`로 기존과 동일 동작
  - workflow_dispatch/재실행: `HEAD~1` 폴백으로 직전 커밋 diff 사용
- `CLAUDE.md`의 Branch Strategy 섹션을 목표 상태(default = `develop`, `main`은 prod 배포 전용)로 갱신

## 영향 범위 & 리스크

- **영향 범위**: 프로덕션 배포 파이프라인(deploy-prod.yml) 의 변경 감지 로직. 정상 push 시나리오에서는 동작 동일
- **롤백 방법**: 리버트 커밋 (paths-filter는 이전대로 default branch 폴백으로 돌아감)

## 테스트

- [ ] CI 통과
- [ ] 머지 후 다음 릴리즈 PR이 `main`에 올라갈 때 `Detect Changes` job이 backend/frontend를 정상 감지하는지 Actions 로그로 확인
- [ ] 릴리즈 직후 `gh workflow run deploy-prod.yml --ref main` 수동 실행 시 step skip이 발생하지 않는지 확인

## 리뷰 포인트

1. `base: \${{ github.event.before || 'HEAD~1' }}` 표현식이 이 프로젝트의 실제 push/workflow_dispatch 시나리오를 모두 커버하는지 (특히 force-push/rebase 상황은 현재 prod 운영에서 발생하지 않음을 전제)
2. CLAUDE.md의 Branch Strategy 문구가 실제 운영 규칙과 일치하는지 — 본 PR 머지 + 이후 `gh api` default branch 전환까지 완료되어야 완전히 일치함을 인지할 것

author: thulunga
body:
## Root cause (discovered after PR 26 merged)

PR 26 switched from `(await import('yahoo-finance2')).default` to `require('yahoo-finance2')`, but that hit a different crash:

```
Error [ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED]: No "exports" main defined in
/app/node_modules/yahoo-finance2/package.json
```

Inspecting the installed package revealed the real issue: **`yahoo-finance2@2.14.0` only ships two modules — `quote` and `autoc`**. There is no `chart` method at all, and the `package.json` `exports` field has only an `"import"` condition (no `"require"`), so `require()` is impossible from our CJS-compiled Node16 output.

```json
// yahoo-finance2/package.json exports
{
  ".": { "import": "./esm/src/index.js" }
}
// esm/src/modules/ → only: autoc.js, quote.js
```

## Fix

Drop `yahoo-finance2` from both files entirely and call Yahoo Finance's HTTP API directly with native `fetch` (available in Node 20+):

| File | Before | After |
|------|--------|-------|
| `market-data.ts` | `yf.chart(symbol, {...})` | `fetch(/v8/finance/chart/{symbol}?interval=5m&range=2d)` |
| `paper-trader.ts` | `yf.quote(trade.symbol)` | `fetch(/v7/finance/quote?symbols={symbol})` |

The JSON structure returned by the raw Yahoo Finance v8 chart endpoint is exactly what `yahoo-finance2.chart()` was parsing internally — same `result.timestamp[]` + `result.indicators.quote[0].{open,high,low,close,volume}` shape. No schema changes needed downstream.

TypeScript check passes (`tsc --noEmit` exits 0).

## Test plan

- [ ] Railway logs should show no `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED` or `yf.chart is not a function` errors
- [ ] Scanner logs should show symbols with actual candle data (not "Insufficient candles (0)")
- [ ] `scan_count` in heartbeat should increment as the engine scans symbols

## Description

When editing an existing post (e.g., one originally created with Windows Live Writer), the published date gets reset to "now" instead of preserving the original date. This causes old posts to appear as newly published.

## Changes

In `Blog.EditPost()`, added a check to preserve `post.DatePublished` when it's a valid date and no explicit date override is set. The priority is:

1. User-specified date override (unchanged)
2. **New:** Existing published date from the post
3. Fall back to current time only if no valid date exists

`Blog.NewPost()` is intentionally unchanged — new posts correctly default to "now" when no override is set.

- [ ] Edit a post and set a date override — override should be used

- [ ] Edit a post originally created with Windows Live Writer — date should not change

Fixes #733

author: irahulpandey
body:
## Summary

Implement tag-based segregation of Databricks resources deployed locally vs via CI/CD, enabling governance tracking and cleanup automation.

Per official Databricks documentation, this implementation uses the new Databricks CLI (v0.218.0+) with full bundle support.

## What Changed

### Implementation
- Added `deployed_by` and `deployment_source` variables to DAB configuration for metadata tagging
- Applied segregation tags to all job resources (hello_world_job, config_demo_job)
- Configured CI/CD workflow to set deployment metadata (`deployed_by=github-actions[bot]`, `source=cicd`)
- Created comprehensive deployment documentation with tag querying examples

### CI/CD Configuration (Per Official Docs)
- GitHub Actions workflow installs official Databricks CLI v0.218.0+ via curl (from databricks/setup-cli)
- All 3 deploy targets (dev, stg, prod) configured with bundle commands
- Bundle commands: `databricks bundle deploy` and `databricks bundle run`
- Environment variables properly passed through deployment steps for resource tagging

### Documentation
- `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` — Deployment guide with tag segregation strategy and API examples
- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-17-dab-resource-segregation-design.md` — Complete design specification
- `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-17-dab-resource-segregation-implementation.md` — Implementation plan with step-by-step tasks

## Tag Structure

All Databricks resources are automatically tagged with three metadata fields:

| Tag | Local Value | CI/CD Value | Purpose |
|-----|-------------|-------------|---------|
| `deployed_by` | OS username | `github-actions[bot]` | Who/what deployed the resource |
| `source` | `local` | `cicd` | Deployment source (for segregation) |
| `environment` | `dev` (or target) | `dev`, `stg`, `prod` | Target environment |

## How It Works

**Local Deployment:**
```bash
databricks bundle deploy --target dev
# Tags: deployed_by=<your_username>, source=local, environment=dev
```

**CI/CD Deployment (automatic on branch push):**
- Push to `dev` → Deploy to dev catalog with `environment=dev`
- Push to `stg` → Deploy to stg catalog with `environment=stg`
- Push to `master` → Deploy to prod catalog with `environment=prod`
- All CI/CD deployments tagged with `deployed_by=github-actions[bot]`, `source=cicd`

## Benefits

✅ **Governance**: Track which resources are official (CI/CD) vs experimental (local)
✅ **Accountability**: Know who deployed what and when
✅ **Cleanup**: Identify and remove stale local deployments (separate cleanup job)
✅ **Auditing**: Complete lineage of deployments for compliance

## Test Plan

- [x] All unit tests pass (9/9)
- [x] DAB bundle validation passes for all targets (dev, stg, prod)
- [x] Official Databricks CLI v0.218.0+ properly installed
- [x] Bundle commands tested and verified
- [ ] CI/CD deployment to dev (will run on merge)
- [ ] CI/CD deployment to stg and prod (on respective branch pushes)

## Files Changed

**Core Implementation:**
- `databricks.yml` — Added `deployed_by` and `deployment_source` variables
- `resources/hello_world_job.yml` — Added segregation tags
- `resources/config_demo_job.yml` — Added segregation tags

**CI/CD:**
- `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` — Updated to install official Databricks CLI v0.218.0+ and set env vars for all targets (dev, stg, prod)

**Documentation:**
- `.gitignore` — Added docs folder
- `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` — New deployment guide with examples
- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-17-dab-resource-segregation-design.md` — Design specification
- `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-17-dab-resource-segregation-implementation.md` — Implementation plan

## References

- [Databricks Asset Bundles Documentation](https://docs.databricks.com/en/dev-tools/bundles/index.html)
- [Databricks CLI Installation Guide](https://docs.databricks.com/en/dev-tools/cli/install.html)

author: happylife2
body:
## Summary

This PR addresses several bugs and UX issues discovered during local development testing, along with a new feature for managing platform credentials through the UI.

### Bug Fixes

- **Fix "Use Template" ValidationError** — Built-in templates use integer IDs, but the compose view only queried the UUID-based `PostTemplate` model. Added fallback to `builtin_templates.py` and pre-fill the caption textarea from the template body.
- **Fix Inbox tab active state** — HTMX partial swaps only replace the message list, not the tab bar. The `{% if current_view %}` active class never re-rendered. Added Alpine.js client-side state toggling so clicking All/My Queue/Unassigned highlights immediately.
- **Fix tag filtering crash on SQLite** — `tags__contains=[tag]` uses PostgreSQL's JSON `@>` operator, which is not supported on SQLite. Created a shared `json_tag_contains()` utility in `apps/utils.py` that uses `__icontains` on SQLite. Updated all 6 call sites across `composer`, `calendar`, and `organizations` apps.
- **Fix file upload crash on local dev** — `STORAGES["default"]` was never set when `STORAGE_BACKEND=local`, causing `InvalidStorageError` on every media upload. Added `FileSystemStorage` as the default backend in the non-S3 branch.

### UX Improvements

- **Separate Profile and Preferences pages** — Both tabs previously rendered identical content. Profile now shows photo/name/email/password/role. Preferences shows a notification settings matrix (event types × delivery channels: In-App, Email, Webhook) with per-toggle save.
- **Upgrade all dropdown menus** — Replaced native `<select>` elements across Calendar (channels, tags, timezone), Inbox (platform, type, status, sentiment), and Organization Settings (timezone) with Alpine.js custom dropdowns. Uses `x-teleport="body"` with fixed positioning to escape `overflow: hidden` containers. Includes search, smooth transitions, and orange active-item highlighting.

### New Feature

- **Platform Credentials UI** — Full CRUD interface at **Settings → Platform Credentials** for org owners/admins to configure API keys directly from the dashboard instead of hardcoding in `.env`. Each platform card includes:
  - Guided setup with help text explaining what's needed
  - Direct links to each platform's developer console
  - Platform-specific input fields (App ID, Secret, Client Key, etc.)
  - Encrypted storage via the existing `PlatformCredential` model (AES-256-GCM)
  - Masked credential display for configured platforms
  - "Shares credentials with" info for linked platforms (e.g., Facebook/Instagram/Threads)
  - Accordion UI — only one platform setup panel open at a time
- **Connect page updated** — "Not Configured" disabled badge replaced with a "Set Up Credentials" button linking to the new settings page

## Merge Conflict Resolution

This branch was rebased onto the latest `main` to resolve two conflicts:

**`apps/composer/views.py`** — Upstream removed the old template pre-fill block entirely (the `PostTemplate.objects.get()` call that was causing the ValidationError). Our branch keeps the fixed version that catches the error, falls back to built-in templates by integer ID, and pre-fills the caption from the template body. Without this, the "Use Template" feature would have no effect at all.

**`templates/calendar/partials/publish_list_shell.html`** — Upstream updated the channel display text to use `account_name|default:account_handle` (a fallback for channels without a display name). Our branch replaces the native `<select>` with a custom Alpine.js dropdown. Resolution: kept our custom dropdown and incorporated upstream's `account_name|default:account_handle` improvement into it.

## Files Changed (16 files, +853 / -118)

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `apps/utils.py` | **New** — Shared `json_tag_contains()` for SQLite-compatible JSON tag filtering |
| `apps/accounts/views.py` | Preferences tab logic, notification prefs handler |
| `apps/calendar/views.py` | SQLite tag filter fix (4 call sites) |
| `apps/composer/views.py` | Template fallback fix, SQLite tag filter fix, caption pre-fill |
| `apps/credentials/urls.py` | Added save/remove endpoints |
| `apps/credentials/views.py` | Full credentials CRUD views with platform field definitions |
| `apps/organizations/views.py` | SQLite tag filter fix |
| `config/settings/base.py` | Added `STORAGES["default"]` for local FileSystemStorage |
| `templates/accounts/settings.html` | Conditional Profile/Preferences rendering |
| `templates/calendar/partials/publish_list_shell.html` | Alpine.js teleported dropdowns |
| `templates/credentials/list.html` | Full credentials management UI |
| `templates/inbox/feed.html` | Alpine.js tab active state |
| `templates/inbox/partials/_filter_bar.html` | Alpine.js teleported filter dropdowns |
| `templates/layouts/settings.html` | Added Platform Credentials nav link |
| `templates/organizations/settings.html` | Custom timezone dropdown with search |
| `templates/social_accounts/connect.html` | "Set Up Credentials" button |

## Test Plan

- [ ] Click a built-in template from the template gallery → compose view opens with caption pre-filled
- [ ] Click Inbox tabs (All / My Queue / Unassigned) → clicked tab highlights immediately
- [ ] Create a tag, assign to an idea, filter by tag on Kanban board → no error on SQLite
- [ ] Upload media in compose view with `STORAGE_BACKEND=local` → file saves to `media/` directory
- [ ] Visit Settings → Profile vs Preferences → each tab shows different content
- [ ] Save notification preferences → persist across page reload
- [ ] Open calendar dropdowns (Channels, Tags, Timezone) → panels appear above content, not clipped
- [ ] Visit Settings → Platform Credentials → configure a platform → status shows "Configured"
- [ ] Visit Connect Account page → unconfigured platforms show "Set Up Credentials" link
- [ ] Open one platform setup card, then click another → first one closes automatically

author: yschimke
body:
## Summary

Closes the 51 code-scanning alerts zizmor raised on main. Each rule addressed:

### `artipacked` × 18 → `persist-credentials: false`

Every `actions/checkout` step leaves the default git token on disk for the rest of the job. Unused in most of our workflows, but readable by any later step or transitive dep. Disabled wherever it wasn't actually needed; the two composite actions that do push (\`preview-baselines\`, \`preview-comment\`) already embed an explicit \`x-access-token:\` URL so they continue to work.

### \`excessive-permissions\` × 13 → explicit \`permissions:\` blocks

Every workflow now declares \`permissions: contents: read\` at the workflow level. Jobs that legitimately need more widen inline:
- \`release.yml\` → \`publish-gradle-plugin\`: \`packages: write\`; \`release\`: \`contents: write\`
- \`preview-comment.yml\` → \`compare\`: \`contents: write, pull-requests: write\`; \`cleanup\` (unchanged): \`contents: write\`

### \`template-injection\` × 15 → \`env:\` indirection

All \`\${{ inputs.* }}\`, \`\${{ github.event.* }}\`, \`\${{ needs.*.outputs.* }}\` references inside \`run:\` bodies are now bound into \`env:\` blocks and read as \`\"\$VAR\"\` in the shell. A branch / tag / PR-title containing \`\$(...)\` or backticks can no longer be interpolated as code. Applies to \`preview-baselines/action.yml\`, \`preview-comment/action.yml\`, \`preview-cleanup/action.yml\`, \`release.yml\`.

### \`cache-poisoning\` × 3 → \`cache-read-only: true\` on release

\`release.yml\`'s three \`setup-gradle\` steps now read the Gradle cache but don't write to it, so tagged release builds can't seed an entry that a later untrusted run might read.

### \`dependabot-cooldown\` × 1 → \`cooldown:\` block

\`dependabot.yml\` gets a 3-day default / 7-day major-version cooldown so a supply-chain-compromised version pulled quickly from the registry can't auto-land as a Dependabot PR in the meantime.

## Behaviour changes

None to CI semantics. The composite-action rewrites are mechanical (same script, values read via \`\"\$VAR\"\` instead of inline templates). Release builds lose Gradle cache-write but retain cache-read, so they benefit from CI-populated caches but don't themselves populate — a small time hit at release only.

## Test plan

- [x] All workflow + composite-action YAML re-validates with \`yaml.safe_load\`.
- [ ] After merge, zizmor workflow run shows 0 open alerts (verify in Security tab).
- [ ] Next PR's \`preview-comment\` action still posts a comment and pushes renders.
- [ ] Next \`Preview Baselines\` run still force-pushes to \`preview_main\`.
- [ ] Eventually: next \`v*\` tag → release workflow completes end-to-end with \`cache-read-only\`.

## Depends on

Stacked on #28 (snapshot publish fix). Rebase cleanly once that's merged.

author: neilmartin83
body:
## Summary

- Replace the hand-maintained `BackupResources` slice with a generator-emitted `backup_registry.go` plus a curated allowlist in `pro_resources.go`. Paths stop drifting from the specs; adding/removing a resource is one line.
- Closes #148 (computer groups 403) and #151 (accounts missing from backup). Also fixes a broken mobile-groups GET path and a blueprint-Configuration-rendered-as-byte-array bug.
- Supersedes #116 — the same computer/mobile-group backup failures are fixed here via the generator-driven registry, so every resource gets the right paths automatically rather than being hand-patched.

## What changed in generated output

**Deprecated / replaced endpoints:**
- Computer smart + static groups: `/v1/computer-groups` → `/v2/smart-computer-groups` + `/v2/static-computer-groups` (separately — old endpoint triggered 403s on role configs without the legacy umbrella privilege, and double-counted results).
- Mobile smart groups detail: `/v1/mobile-device-groups/{id}` → `/v1/mobile-device-groups/smart-groups/{id}` (old path 404'd).
- Classic computer/mobile EAs → modern `/v1/computer-extension-attributes` + `/v1/mobile-device-extension-attributes` (prefer modern policy; user EAs stay classic, no modern equivalent).

**Added:**
- `classic-account-users` + `classic-account-groups` via the `list_subset` plumbing #152 introduced. `FetchClassicListSubset` slices `<users>` / `<groups>` from the combined `/JSSResource/accounts` response.
- `mobile-device-groups-static-groups` subdir (previously omitted).

**Bonus fixes surfaced by the regen:**
- Mobile device smart/static groups now use correct `groupName` / `groupId` field overrides. `pro mobile-device-groups-smart-groups get --name <x>` previously silently failed — it does now work.
- Sites had no `/v1/sites/{id}` endpoint at all; the old backup was hitting a non-existent URL. New `ListOnly` flag for resources whose list response is already the full record.
- Blueprint components carry `Configuration JsonNode = json.RawMessage` ([]byte). yaml.v3 rendered this as an array of integers. JSON round-trip normalization before write.

## `_meta` block

Two new fields:
- `jamf_pro_url` — fetched best-effort from `/v1/jamf-pro-server-url`. Platform-gateway backups now carry the actual instance URL, not just the gateway host.
- `tenant_id` — populated from the resolved `PlatformOAuth2Provider` when applicable; omitted via `omitempty` for direct-auth backups.

## YAML readability

Scripts, profile payloads, and computer EA `scriptContents` now render as yaml.v3 literal-block (`|-`) scalars. Trailing newlines at EOF and trailing whitespace on each line are stripped to force yaml.v3 out of its double-quoted fallback — cosmetic only, on-disk copy only. Confirmed this does not corrupt scripts; trailing whitespace has no shell semantics and is almost always editor noise.

## Concurrency

Default lowered from 10 → 3, ceiling 50 → 5. Fanning out per-ID GETs across 17 resource types at 10-parallel each pushed modest instances into 429s. Help string updated to show the ceiling.

## Architecture

```
specs + classic/resources.yaml ──► generator/main.go ──► backup_registry.go
                                     (generateBackupRegistry)      │
                                                                   ▼
                                            pro_resources.go: curated allowlist
                                                                   │
                                                                   ▼
                                                pro_backup.go / pro_diff.go (consumers)
```

`backup_registry.go` is keyed by CLI command name and carries `{ListPath, GetPath, IsClassic, WrapperKey, SingularKey, ListSubset, NameField, IDField}`. `ResolveBackupResources()` joins the curated list against the registry; a test (`TestBackupResources_AllKeysRegistered`) fails at `make test` if a curated Key ever points at an endpoint the generator no longer produces.

## Test plan

author: mh0lt
body:
## Summary

- Fix fresh-mainnet-sync regression introduced with the chain.toml v2 merge: the publish/seed stack was running unconditionally and collided with the downloaded `chain.toml.torrent` during post-OtterSync `AddTorrentsFromDisk`, aborting the execution service with `snapshot exists with a different name: "chain.toml"`.
- Gate the three unconditional v2 call sites on the existing `--snap.p2p-manifest` flag (default `false`) so default syncs stay on the pre-v2 path while opt-in users get the full v2 flow.

## Reproduction (before this change)

```
USE_STATE_CACHE=false ./build/bin/erigon \
  --datadir=<fresh> --chain=mainnet --prune.mode=minimal
```

Fails during stage `[1/6 OtterSync]` immediately after `Downloader completed remaining snapshots`:

```
[EROR] Could not start execution service
  err="[1/6 OtterSync] after snapshot download: adding torrents from disk:
       adding torrent for chain.toml.torrent:
       snapshot exists with a different name: \"chain.toml\""
```

Collision originates in `getExistingSnapshotTorrent` ([db/downloader/downloader.go:1683](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/blob/main/db/downloader/downloader.go#L1683)) — the locally-seeded `chain.toml` torrent is already registered under that info-hash when the disk-scanned `chain.toml.torrent` tries to add.

## Change

Three gated sites, all tied to the pre-existing `--snap.p2p-manifest` flag (usage: *"Discover snapshot manifest (chain.toml) from P2P peers via ENR instead of using centralized preverified.toml"* — default `false`):

1. [node/eth/backend.go:541](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/blob/main/node/eth/backend.go#L541) — wrap the whole ENR updater / `SetNodeSourceFn` / delayed `PublishLocalChainToml` / `StartChainTomlDiscovery` / `StartTorrentPeerManager` block in `&& backend.config.Snapshot.P2PManifest`.
2. [node/eth/backend.go:1461](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/blob/main/node/eth/backend.go#L1461) — gate the initial publish in `initDownloader()`.
3. [db/downloader/downloader.go:810](https://github.com/erigontech/erigon/blob/main/db/downloader/downloader.go#L810) — gate the post-download republish using `d.manifestReady != nil`, which is the internal signal that `EnableP2PManifest()` was invoked by the backend. This also covers the loop-internal publish in `chainTomlDiscoveryLoop` (only runs under P2P manifest mode).

Default `--snap.p2p-manifest=false` ⇒ **zero v2 behaviour** ⇒ collision avoided.
Opt-in `--snap.p2p-manifest=true` ⇒ full v2 publish + discover + peer-manager flow preserved.

## Test plan

- [x] `make lint` — 0 issues
- [x] `make erigon` — builds clean
- [x] `go test -short ./db/downloader/...` — passes (`chaintoml_test.go`, `chaintoml_v2_test.go` call `PublishChainToml` directly, unaffected)
- [x] `go vet ./node/eth/... ./db/downloader/...` — clean
- [ ] Manual: fresh `--chain=mainnet` sync with default flags completes OtterSync and enters Headers stage without the collision error (reviewer to confirm on their setup — original reproducer took ~13 min to hit the crash point)
- [ ] Manual: fresh sync with `--snap.p2p-manifest=true` still performs chain.toml discovery / publishing as before (v2 behaviour preserved)

author: stffns
body:
## Summary

Closes the bootstrap loop. Shadow mode writes `shadow_disagree` tags (PR #1/2/3); this PR turns those tags into labeled training data by asking an oracle (Gemini by default) to classify the event.

## Volume measurement (drove the design)

`experiments/consolidation/shadow_dry_run.py` measures the shadow-mode disagreement rate across every scenario + every `~/.merken/*.db`. Result: **~6% on organic content** (vs ~69% on synthetic noise scenarios, which are the training distribution).

At ~6%, passive accumulation of 200 disagreements takes ~2 months. Oracle labeling is not optional -- it's necessary for a usable review cadence.

## Oracle labeling

```
merken audit --label-with gemini [--limit N]
```

- Skips events already in `merken_labels` (idempotent, re-runnable).
- Gemini as the first backend (zero-config given Jay's env keys).
- Fail-safe: per-event errors don't block the loop.

## Audit fix (pre-requisite)

While writing tests: `format_audit_row` used second-precision timestamps so two rows produced within the same second for the same policy+reason had identical titles and vstash silently dropped one. Fix: microseconds + event_title suffix.

## E2E verification against live Gemini

Ran `merken audit --label-with gemini` on `/tmp/shadow_smoke.db` (the shadow smoke from PR #2 with 1 disagreement). Gemini labeled "Sprint planning: infra team prioritized CI pipeline" as **DECISION** (conf=0.90, "Prioritization of the CI pipeline represents a lasting commitment..."). Oracle overrode nanoGPT's SKIP -- exactly the kind of correction needed to train v6. Re-run: `labeled=0 skipped=1` (idempotent).

## Test plan

- [x] 8 new unit tests for parser + loop + idempotency + error handling (stub backend, no network).
- [x] `pytest -q --ignore=tests/test_embed_model_resolution.py` = **199 passed**, 3 deselected.
- [x] `ruff check` clean on all new files.
- [x] E2E smoke against live Gemini API key.

## Scope-excluded intentionally

- No Claude backend yet (~20 lines; Gemini already covers the immediate need).
- No batching / rate limiting (Gemini Flash is cheap at this scale).
- No graduation path from shadow to primary decider (still TODO).

author: mmagn
body:
## Résumé

Dans `Instructeurs::ContactInformationsController`, `@procedure` et `@groupe_instructeur` étaient recherchés indépendamment, chacun scopé à l'instructeur courant, sans vérification que le groupe appartienne bien à la procédure. Un instructeur membre de groupes sur plusieurs procédures pouvait ainsi agir sur un groupe d'une autre procédure sous le contexte d'autorisation d'une procédure qui ne le contient pas.

La recherche du groupe est maintenant chaînée via `@procedure.groupe_instructeurs.merge(current_instructeur.groupe_instructeurs)`, garantissant la cohérence procédure/groupe à la fois avec la procédure ciblée et les groupes accessibles à l'instructeur.

## Couverture

Ajout d'un `context` de régression couvrant `#create`, `#update`, `#destroy` avec `procedure_id` et `groupe_id` appartenant à deux procédures distinctes — les requêtes incohérentes ne doivent plus modifier l'état.
