body:
## Summary
- Closes the gap between the existing `CIRCUIT_BREAKER_THRESHOLD=3` (consecutive-failure) and the real pattern we see in prod: chronic low accuracy across hundreds of signals (gemini-reviewer at 0.30/650) and burst hallucination at low-n (openclaw-agent at 73%/11).
- New `isBenched(agentId, categories?, allAgentIds?)` export with Rule A (chronic) + Rule B (burst) + skill-coverage safeguard, wired into `cross-reviewer-selection.ts` alongside `isCircuitOpen`.
- Soft bench only — excludes from `auto` dispatch and `selectCrossReviewers`; explicit `gossip_run(agent_id: ...)` still works. No config.json writes.

Closes #93.

## Design (from three-agent review, 2026-04-16)

| Rule | Condition | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| A | `accuracy < 0.30 AND totalSignals >= 200` | `chronic-low-accuracy` |
| B | `weightedHallucinations >= 5 AND weightedHallucinations/totalSignals > 0.4` | `burst-hallucination` |

- **Safeguard:** if candidate is the sole unbenched agent covering any required category, return `{benched:false, safeguardBlocked:true, reason}`. Preserves team capability while flagging the state for dashboard surfacing.
- **Hysteresis:** implicit 5pp margin — strict `<` at 0.30 entry, effectively ≥0.35 to exit. TODO(v2): explicit post-bench signal counter.
- **Wilson CI justification:** at n=50, acc=0.29 has 95% CI [0.17, 0.43] — too wide. At n=200, CI tightens to [0.24, 0.37] — safe to act.

## Applied to current agents
| Agent | acc | n | halluc | Rule A | Rule B | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| gemini-reviewer | 0.30 | 650 | 39 | ✓ borderline | — | Benched unless sole concurrency provider |
| openclaw-agent | 0.00 | 11 | ~5-8 | — | ✓ | Benched unless sole trust_boundaries provider |
| gemini-tester, sonnet-reviewer, opus-implementer, haiku-researcher | — | — | — | — | — | Safe |

## Changes
| File | Lines | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `packages/orchestrator/src/performance-reader.ts:24` | +1 | Export `weightedHallucinations` on `AgentScore` |
| `packages/orchestrator/src/performance-reader.ts:125-188` | +64 | New `isBenched()` method + safeguard recursion |
| `packages/orchestrator/src/performance-reader.ts:608,625` | +2 | Populate `weightedHallucinations` in `computeScores` main + impl-only branches |
| `packages/orchestrator/src/cross-reviewer-selection.ts:86-96` | +10 | Filter insertion alongside `isCircuitOpen` |
| `packages/relay/src/dashboard/api-agents.ts:54` + 4 test fixtures | — | Collateral `AgentScore` literal fixes for tightened interface |
| `tests/orchestrator/is-benched.test.ts` (new) | +180 | 12 cases |

## Test plan
- [x] `npm test` — 143 suites / 1859 passed (+12 new), 0 failed
- [x] `tsc -b packages/orchestrator apps/cli` clean
- Covers: Rule A/B boundaries (strict `<`, strict `>=`, rate 5/11 vs 5/12), safeguard both directions, hysteresis at acc=0.34/0.36, healthy-agent + no-data passthrough

## Non-goals (per spec)
- Per-category benching (v2)
- Hard bench (config.json writes)
- Manual override flag (hysteresis handles unbench)
- Observer mode
- Changes to `MIN_EVIDENCE=120` (HANDBOOK invariant #2) or circuit breaker

## TODOs for follow-up
- Dashboard "Benched" badge + "Would bench, kept for coverage" badge for `safeguardBlocked`
- v2: explicit post-bench signal counter for stricter hysteresis
- v2: per-category benching

body:
## Summary

Part of #1534. Migrate the streaming repetition guard from legacy
`run_agent_loop` into the sans-IO `AgentMachine` via a pure
synchronous observer.

- `AgentMachine::observe_stream_delta(delta, accumulated) -> Option<RepetitionAction>`
  feeds the existing `RepetitionGuard` and, on a hit, returns the byte
  index at which the runner should truncate the accumulated buffer.
- The guard is reset on every `AwaitingLlm` entry via
  `rebuild_then_call`, matching the legacy per-iteration
  `accumulated_text = String::new()` contract.
- Observer shape mirrors `observe_context_usage` from #1546: pure,
  per-delta, no event/effect round-trip on the hot path.
- Runner-side contract is documented in `runner.rs`: feed each
  `TextDelta` through the observer and, on `Abort`, cancel the
  provider stream, truncate accumulated text at `truncate_at_byte`,
  and synthesise an `LlmCompleted` with the truncated text (no tool
  calls, no usage) — the same graceful stop the legacy
  `repetition_aborted = true` branch takes.

Legacy `run_agent_loop` is untouched; production wiring follows in
the summary PR.

## Type of change

| Type | Label |
|------|-------|
| New feature | `enhancement` |

## Component

`core`

## Closes

Closes #1553

## Test plan

- [x] Machine-level synchronous tests: unique text, below-min length,
  exact-block repetition, incremental feeding, per-round reset,
  cross-iteration firing.
- [x] Runner integration tests: truncated `LlmCompleted` drives to a
  graceful `Done`; observer remains usable after `drive` completes.
- [x] `cargo check -p rara-kernel` passes.
- [x] `cargo test -p rara-kernel --lib agent::` passes (156 tests).
- [x] `cargo +nightly fmt --all` / `cargo clippy --workspace
  --all-targets --all-features --no-deps -- -D warnings` pass.
- [x] `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo +nightly doc --workspace
  --no-deps --document-private-items` passes.

body:
Adds a deployment pipeline for this React/Vite/TypeScript app, running the full build chain on every push to `main` and shipping the output to GitHub Pages.

## Changes

- **`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`** — CI/CD workflow triggered on push to `main` (or manually via `workflow_dispatch`):
  - `npm install` → `npm run dev` (smoke-checked with 10s timeout) → `npm run lint` → `npm run build`
  - Uploads `dist/` as a Pages artifact and deploys via `actions/deploy-pages`
  - Split into `build` + `deploy` jobs with proper `pages`/`id-token` permissions and concurrency guard

- **`vite.config.ts`** — Sets `base: '/neo-brutalism/'` so asset paths resolve correctly under the GitHub Pages subdirectory URL

## Activation required

GitHub Pages source must be set to **GitHub Actions** under **Settings → Pages** before the deploy job will publish.

author: levx-me
body:
## Summary

- Add **korean-lite/full/ultra** intensity levels for Korean language compression
- Korean-specific rules: drop particles (은/는/이/가/을/를), use noun endings (함/됨/필요/완료), remove filler words (사실/기본적으로/정말), empty pleasantries (드리겠습니다), hedging (것 같습니다), connective endings → symbols (때문에→`→`), honorific stripping (시/으시)
- Hook support: `/caveman korean` command parsing, Korean per-turn reminder, alias resolution
- Benchmark infrastructure: `--lang ko` flag for `run.py`, Korean prompts, results

## Benchmark Results

**Korean caveman mode: 67% average token savings** (range 57%–84%)

| Task | Normal (tokens) | Caveman Korean (tokens) | Saved |
|------|---------------:|----------------:|------:|
| React re-render bug | 611 | 236 | 61% |
| Auth middleware fix | 1176 | 191 | 84% |
| PostgreSQL pool setup | 2363 | 539 | 77% |
| git rebase vs merge | 1149 | 429 | 63% |
| Async refactor | 739 | 316 | 57% |
| Microservices vs monolith | 1225 | 508 | 59% |
| Security review | 817 | 337 | 59% |
| Docker multi-stage | 1210 | 442 | 63% |
| Race condition debug | 1254 | 252 | 80% |
| Error boundary | 2851 | 1011 | 65% |
| **Average** | **1340** | **426** | **67%** |

*Model: claude-sonnet-4-20250514, 1 trial per prompt. Comparable to English caveman mode (65% avg).*

## Why

Current caveman rules are English-optimized (drop articles a/an/the, English filler words). Korean has no articles — compression requires targeting different grammar elements: particles, verb endings, connective endings, honorifics, and Korean-specific filler patterns. Same gap that wenyan modes fill for Classical Chinese.

## What changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `skills/caveman/SKILL.md` | Korean intensity table rows, rules, and examples |
| `hooks/caveman-config.js` | `korean-lite`, `korean`, `korean-full`, `korean-ultra` in `VALID_MODES` |
| `hooks/caveman-mode-tracker.js` | `/caveman korean[-lite\|-full\|-ultra]` parsing + Korean per-turn reminder |
| `hooks/caveman-activate.js` | `korean` → `korean-full` alias resolution |
| `rules/caveman-activate.md` | `korean` added to switch line |
| `evals/prompts/ko.txt` | 10 Korean evaluation prompts |
| `benchmarks/run.py` | `--lang ko` support |
| `benchmarks/prompts_ko.json` | 10 Korean benchmark prompts |
| `benchmarks/results/` | Korean benchmark results JSON |

## Before / After

**Before** (caveman full, responding in Korean):
> "이 함수는 사실 기본적으로 불필요한 API 호출을 하고 있는 것 같습니다. 확인해 보시면 좋을 것 같습니다."

Inconsistent compression — English rules don't map to Korean grammar.

**After** (caveman korean-full):
> "함수 불필요 API 호출 있음. 제거 필요."

Systematic compression targeting Korean-specific patterns.

## Design decisions

- Rules section written in English (matching wenyan pattern) — LLMs follow English instructions more precisely
- Korean examples use natural compressed Korean, not literal translations of English caveman
- Three levels mirror English/wenyan pattern: lite (grammar intact), full (particles dropped), ultra (maximum compression)
- Korean-specific compression strategies: particle dropping, noun endings, connective ending → symbol conversion, honorific stripping

author: oshioma
body:
## Summary
- **Member admin page** at `/app/settings/members` — admins can invite teammates, edit their role/ads flag, and remove them. Hidden from the sidebar for non-admins.
- **Two-dimensional permissions** — `role` (admin | member) independent of `can_run_ads` (bool). Admin manages team; `can_run_ads` gates the ads surface, regardless of role.
- **Invite flow** — Supabase email invite → `/auth/callback?type=invite` (OTP `verifyOtp`) → `/accept-invite` → invitee sets password + name → `/post-login`.
- **Ads gating** — `requireAdsAccess()` wraps every ad create/edit page:
  - `/app/launch`
  - `/app/clients/[id]/campaigns/new`
  - `/app/clients/[id]/campaigns/[id]/edit`
  - `/app/clients/[id]/campaigns/[id]/ads/new`
  - `/app/clients/[id]/campaigns/[id]/ads/[id]/edit`
- **Button hiding** — members without ads access don't see "New campaign", "Add ad", "Edit", or the "Quick launch" sidebar group. Read access (dashboards, ad rows, campaign detail) is untouched.

## Migration
`supabase/migrations/20260417_user_roles.sql` is idempotent and coerces any pre-existing `operator`/`viewer` rows into the new `admin`/`member` model. Apply it before the first invite is sent.

## Before the first invite works in prod
Supabase → **Auth → URL Configuration → Redirect URLs** must include:
- `https://guestlistsocial.com/auth/callback` (already required for sign-in)

The invite email lands at `<site>/auth/callback?type=invite&token_hash=…` — same callback that handles sign-in.

## First admin bootstrap
After applying the migration, promote your own account:
```sql
insert into user_roles (user_id, role, can_run_ads)
values ('<your-auth-uid>', 'admin', true)
on conflict (user_id) do update
  set role = 'admin', can_run_ads = true;
```

## Test plan
- [ ] As admin, `/app/settings/members` shows every non-portal user
- [ ] Invite a teammate as member + can_run_ads=false → they get an email → land on `/accept-invite` → set password → `/post-login` → admin panel loads, no Quick launch link, no New Campaign button on client pages
- [ ] Toggle can_run_ads=true → the forbidden pages now render, buttons appear
- [ ] Toggle role back to member → Members sidebar link disappears on their next load
- [ ] Try to self-demote → blocked with error
- [ ] Try to self-remove → blocked with error
- [ ] Hit `/app/launch` as a member without ads → bounced to `/post-login`
- [ ] Build passes (verified locally)

author: copilot
body:
`ManualResetValueTaskSourceCore<T>` is not present in the `netstandard2.0` DLL of `System.Threading.Tasks.Extensions` — only `IValueTaskSource<T>`, `ValueTaskSourceStatus`, and `ValueTaskSourceOnCompletedFlags` are. The type exists natively only in .NET Core 2.1+ / .NET Standard 2.1+. When `System.Threading.Tasks.Extensions` was transitively referenced (e.g. via `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp`), PolyShim incorrectly suppressed its own `ManualResetValueTaskSourceCore<T>` polyfill, causing a missing-type build failure in consumers.

## Changes

- **`PolyShim/PolyShim.targets`**: Removed the `FEATURE_VALUETASK_SOURCES_MANUALRESET` flag entirely — since availability is purely TFM-based (no package reference check involved), there is no need for a build flag.
- **`PolyShim/NetCore21/ManualResetValueTaskSourceCore.cs`**: Replaced the removed feature flag guard with an inline TFM check following the same pattern as other polyfill files: `#if (NETCOREAPP && !NETCOREAPP2_1_OR_GREATER) || (NETFRAMEWORK) || (NETSTANDARD && !NETSTANDARD2_1_OR_GREATER)`, with a nested `#if FEATURE_TASK` guard to exclude older .NET Framework targets (e.g. net35) where `Task` is not available. An inline comment explains that the compatibility package does not provide this type for `netstandard2.0` or .NET Framework targets. The now-unreachable inner `#if NETSTANDARD2_1_OR_GREATER || NETCOREAPP3_0_OR_GREATER` branch inside `OnCompleted` was also removed.

## Summary

Replaces base64 password storage in `~/.tm1cli/config.json` with OS keychain integration (macOS Keychain, Linux secret-service/libsecret, Windows Credential Manager) via `github.com/zalando/go-keyring`. Falls back to base64 with a stderr warning when the keychain is unavailable (headless Linux without D-Bus, sandboxed environments).

- New `PasswordStorage` (`""` / `base64` / `keychain`) and `PasswordRef` (128-bit random hex) fields on `ServerConfig`. Empty storage is treated as base64 for backward compatibility — **existing configs load and work unchanged**.
- `PasswordRef` as the keychain account prevents cross-config collisions when multiple configs share connection names (e.g., local + global both naming a server `dev`).
- `config add`: writes to keychain after successful connection test; rolls back the keychain entry if the subsequent `config.Save` fails (avoids orphaned secrets).
- `config edit`: entering a new password migrates into the keychain; pressing Enter preserves the existing storage mode (no auto-migration).
- `config remove`: saves the config first, then best-effort keychain cleanup (an orphaned secret is preferable to a corrupt config file).
- Env var `TM1CLI_PASSWORD` still wins over any stored value, regardless of storage mode.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...` — clean
- [x] `go vet ./...` — clean
- [x] `go test ./...` — 615 tests pass across 6 packages
- [x] `go test -race ./...` — clean (no data races; `keyring.MockInit()` is installed via `TestMain` in `cmd` tests to prevent any real keychain access)
- [x] New tests cover: keychain wrapper roundtrip/not-found/delete, `StorePassword` keychain path and base64 fallback, `GetEffectivePassword` keychain/missing/legacy/env-var-override, `config add` keychain success + fallback + rollback-on-save-failure, `config edit` new-password-migrates + blank-preserves-legacy, `config remove` keychain delete + delete-failure-doesn't-break-config.
- [x] Existing tests updated to use `GetEffectivePassword` (storage-mode agnostic) where they asserted base64 encoding directly.

## Review

Plan reviewed by Codex (2 iterations, approved after addressing cross-config collision, remove ordering, migration policy, and probe side-effects). Code reviewed externally (2 rounds); round 1 flagged 1 P1 (orphan-on-save-failure in `config add`) which was fixed in round 2, reaching APPROVED.

## Documentation

- README Password Security section rewritten to describe keychain-first strategy, fallback behavior, config-file portability caveats, and migration path.
- Help text for `config add` and `config edit` updated to describe the new storage behavior.

## Known follow-up (out of scope)

`runConfigEdit` has the same keychain-rollback-on-save-failure gap as the `runConfigAdd` case fixed in this PR. The reviewer flagged it as P2 and out-of-scope for this branch — worth a separate issue.

Closes #22

body:
## Summary

Implements **Story 1.2 — Authentication & Session Management**: backend JWT auth (stateless, httpOnly cookie), admin-user seeding, Argon2id password hashing, Spring Security filter chain, and the full WKS error-envelope surface. **Backend only** — login UI lands with Story 1.3.

Two commits:

1. `feat(backend): Story 1.2 — authentication & session management` — initial implementation per spec.
2. `review(1-2): apply adversarial code-review patches` — fixes from the Blind Hunter + Edge Case Hunter + Acceptance Auditor review pass (see "Code review" section below).

## Acceptance Criteria coverage

| AC | Topic | Status |
|----|-------|--------|
| AC1 | Admin seed on first boot (`AdminUserSeeder` + WKS-API-050/051) | ✅ met |
| AC2 | `POST /api/auth/login` — 200/401/400 + generic 401 for all three failure modes | ✅ met |
| AC3 | JWT contract — HS256, JJWT 0.12.6, WKS-API-052/053 | ✅ met |
| AC4 | `/api/auth/me` + `/api/auth/logout` | ✅ met |
| AC5 | `SecurityConfig` filter chain, STATELESS, CSRF on `/api/**` ignored | ✅ met |
| AC6 | Argon2id `PasswordEncoder` | ✅ met |
| AC7 | `users` / `roles` / `user_roles` schema, domain model, port/adapter split | ✅ met |
| AC8 | `GlobalExceptionHandler` envelope (WKS-API-401/403/001/002, WKS-RTM-500) | ✅ met |
| AC9 | No frontend changes | ✅ met |
| AC10 | Unit + slice + integration tests | ✅ met |
| AC11 | CORS via `SecurityConfig` — no `@CrossOrigin` | ✅ met |

## Code review

Adversarial review (Blind Hunter, Edge Case Hunter, Acceptance Auditor) surfaced **1 decision-needed, 19 patches, 14 deferred, 10 dismissed**. All 20 patches applied in the `review(1-2)` commit:

**Applied in this PR**

- Email case-insensitivity — `UserRepositoryAdapter` lowercases + strips at every boundary; fixes duplicate-case accounts and user-enumeration side channel.
- `JwtTokenProvider` — fail-fast on non-Base64 `WKS_JWT_SECRET` (no silent UTF-8 fallback), strips whitespace, rejects `ttlHours ≤ 0`, narrowed `parse()` catch to `JwtException | IllegalArgumentException`.
- `SecurityConfig` — `OPTIONS /**` permitAll (CORS preflight), fail-fast + validator on `WKS_CORS_ORIGINS` (rejects `"null"`, `*`, path-bearing entries), timing-attack equalization via dummy Argon2 encode for missing / inactive users.
- `JwtAuthenticationFilter` — rejects ambiguous duplicate `WKS_SESSION` cookies (sibling-subdomain injection vector).
- `AuthController` — trims email before `authenticate`.
- `LoginRequest.toString` — partial email masking (`a***@domain`).
- `WksAuthenticationEntryPoint` — switched from hand-concatenated JSON to `ObjectMapper` + `Map` envelope (no `api.dto` import, so hexagonal-layering ArchUnit rule stays clean).
- `User` record — compact constructor wraps roles with `Set.copyOf`.
- `UserRepositoryAdapter.save` — mutates the Hibernate-managed `roles` collection in place instead of replacing the reference.
- Tests — new `GlobalExceptionHandlerTest` covers WKS-API-403 / WKS-API-002 / WKS-RTM-500; new parameterised `@WebMvcTest` asserts byte-identical envelope for unknown-email / wrong-password / inactive-user; `JwtTokenProviderTest` adds Base64 / whitespace / TTL boundary cases.

**Deferred** — 14 items recorded in `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/deferred-work.md` (wks-platform2). Notable:

- Logout does not revoke JWT server-side — AC19 explicit Phase 1 deferral; 8h TTL is the mitigation.
- No login rate limiting / Argon2 CPU-DoS protection — AC11 explicit Phase 1 TODO.
- CSRF disabled on `/api/**` — per-spec architectural decision.
- Dev default admin password `admin` — per AC5.

## Test plan

- [x] `mvn -pl backend verify` green — 38 tests (Spotless, Surefire, Failsafe, ArchUnit).
- [x] `cd frontend && npm test && npm run build` green — 1 test, smoke-verifies security dependency did not leak into the frontend build.
- [x] Curl walkthrough (executed against a local Docker Compose boot; reproduce with `docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml up --build`):
  - [x] `curl -i http://localhost:8080/api/health` → `200 OK`, no `Set-Cookie`.
  - [x] `curl -i http://localhost:8080/api/auth/me` → `401 Unauthorized` with `{"error":{"code":"WKS-API-401", ...}}`.
  - [x] `curl -i -c cookies.txt -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"email":"admin@wkspower.local","password":"admin"}' http://localhost:8080/api/auth/login` → `200 OK` + `Set-Cookie: WKS_SESSION=...; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax`.
  - [x] `curl -i -b cookies.txt http://localhost:8080/api/auth/me` → `200 OK`, body `data.email=admin@wkspower.local`, `data.roles=["admin"]`.
  - [x] `curl -i -b cookies.txt -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/auth/logout` → `204 No Content`, cookie cleared.
  - [x] `curl -i -b cookies.txt http://localhost:8080/api/auth/me` → `401 Unauthorized` (post-logout cookie rejected).
  - [x] Container restart → `data/wksplatform.mv.db` persists admin; no duplicate seed (`existsWithRole("admin")` short-circuits).
- [x] `AuthFlowIT` exercises the full HTTP round-trip (login → `/me` → unauthenticated `/api/cases` 401 → logout → post-logout 401) against a real Spring Boot + Flyway + H2 context — doubles as the integration surrogate for the curl trace.

## Reviewer notes

- Review Findings and Dev Agent Record live in `wks-platform2/_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/1-2-authentication-and-session-management.md` (separate repo).
- The second commit (`review(1-2)`) is intentional — it preserves the review audit trail, matches the Story 1.1 merge pattern, and keeps each commit's diff small enough to review on its own.

## Summary

Follow-up to #97. Now that `@infra-x/typescript-config@2.0.0` is published to npm, migrate all three starter templates to the new atom + recipe design.

## Per-starter changes

| Starter | tsconfig before | tsconfig after |
|---|---|---|
| `starters/server` | `extends tsconfig.library.json` + 4 overrides | `extends recipe-app-bun.json` — zero overrides |
| `starters/cli` | `extends tsconfig.library.json` + 5 overrides | `extends recipe-app-bun.json` — zero overrides (dropped `outDir`; tsdown owns build) |
| `starters/web` | `extends tsconfig.react-library.json` + 5 overrides | Hand-composed atoms + one `lib` override for DOM (see known limitation) |

Each starter also bumps its `@infra-x/typescript-config` dep from `^0.1.6` to `^2.0.0` and refreshes its own `bun.lock`.

## Why `starters/web` still has an override

`runtime-bun.json` doesn't include DOM lib. A Bun full-stack React app needs both Bun types and DOM, so the web starter hand-composes atoms and sets `lib: ["esnext", "DOM", "DOM.Iterable"]`. A future `runtime-bun-dom` atom will close this gap.

## Test plan

- [x] `starters/server` — `bun run typecheck` passes against 2.0.0
- [x] `starters/cli` — `bun run typecheck` + `bun run build` (tsdown) both pass
- [x] `starters/web` — `bun run typecheck` passes
- [x] Root-level `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`, `bun run format:check` all green
- [x] Resolved `@infra-x/typescript-config` version in each starter's `node_modules` is `2.0.0`

No changes to `packages/*` — this PR only touches `starters/*`.

### Sigstore Timestamp Authority has Improper Certificate Validation in verifier
[CVE-2026-39984](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-39984) / [GHSA-xm5m-wgh2-rrg3](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-xm5m-wgh2-rrg3)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Authorization bypass via certificate bag manipulation in sigstore/timestamp-authority verifier

An authorization bypass vulnerability exists in sigstore/timestamp-authority verifier (timestamp-authority/v2/pkg/verification): `VerifyTimestampResponse` function correctly verifies the certificate chain but when the TSA specific constraints are verified in `VerifyLeafCert`, the first non-CA certificate from the PKCS#7 certificate bag is used instead of the leaf certificate from the certificate chain. An attacker can exploit this by prepending a forged certificate to the certificate bag while the message is signed with an authorized key. The library validates the signature using the one certificate but performs authorization checks on the another, allowing an attacker to bypass some authorization controls. 

This vulnerability does **not** apply to timestamp-authority service, only to users of `timestamp-authority/v2/pkg/verification` package.

This vulnerability does **not** apply to sigstore-go even though it is a user of `timestamp-authority/v2/pkg/verification`: Providing `TSACertificate` option to  `VerifyTimestampResponse` fully mitigates the issue.

##### Patches

The issue will be fixed in timestamp-authority 2.0.6

##### Workarounds

Users of `VerifyTimestampResponse` can use the `TSACertificate` option to specify the exact certificate they expect to be used: this fully mitigates the issue.

##### References

This issue was found after reading CVE-2026-33753 / GHSA-3xxc-pwj6-jgrj (originally reported by @​Jaynornj and @​Pr00fOf3xpl0it)

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 5.5 / 10 (Medium)
- Vector String: `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N`

- [https://github.com/sigstore/timestamp-authority](https://redirect.github.com/sigstore/timestamp-authority)

## Summary

- Adds `PerpsOrderSkipReason(signal, posSide)` — pure helper that mirrors the skip conditions in `ExecutePerpsSignal`; live order helpers must consult it before spawning the Python executor
- `runHyperliquidExecuteOrder` now calls the guard at entry and returns `ok=false` (triggers `liveExecFailed`) when the order would be a no-op
- Captures `hlPosSide` alongside `hlPosQty` in Phase 1 RLock and threads it through

## Root Cause

`runHyperliquidExecuteOrder` placed the live on-chain order unconditionally, then `ExecutePerpsSignal` hit the "already long, skipping buy" branch and returned `trades=0` — dropping the Trade record and leaving virtual state permanently behind actual exchange positions. 0.716 ETH (3 fills × ~0.238) accumulated this way.

## Test Plan

- [ ] `TestPerpsOrderSkipReason` — 8 subtests covering every branch of the guard
- [ ] `TestExecutePerpsSignalAlreadyLongIsInertNoOp` — pins that the skip path is side-effect-free
- [ ] `go test ./...` in `scheduler/` passes

Closes #298

author: orsharon7
body:
## Summary

Closes #39

Adds `.github/workflows/rinse.yml` — a GitHub Action that automatically runs the full RINSE Copilot PR review loop whenever a new PR is opened or updated.

## What the Action does

1. Triggers on `pull_request` events: `opened`, `reopened`, `synchronize`
2. Checks out the PR branch with persisted credentials (so fix commits can be pushed)
3. Installs the `claude` CLI via npm
4. Invokes `pr-review/pr-review-claude-v2.sh` which drives the full review loop:
   - Requests a Copilot review if none is pending
   - Waits for Copilot to post comments
   - Runs Claude to fix each comment
   - Pushes fixes, requests re-review
   - Repeats until Copilot approves or 0 comments remain

## Key design decisions

| Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|
| `concurrency: group: rinse-pr-{number}` | Cancel in-flight run when a new push arrives — no duplicate loops |
| Fork guard (`head.repo.full_name == repository`) | Forks can't access secrets; skip them safely |
| `permissions: contents: write, pull-requests: write` | Minimum required — push fix commits and request Copilot reviews |
| `persist-credentials: true` on checkout | Enables `git push` inside the RINSE loop without extra token setup |
| `GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}` | Builtin, no extra secret needed for GitHub API calls |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` secret | Required for Claude CLI — must be configured in repo Settings → Secrets |

## Setup instructions for users

1. Enable **Copilot code review** for the repo (Settings → Copilot → Code review)
2. Add `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` secret (Settings → Secrets → Actions)
3. Set workflow permissions to **Read and write** (Settings → Actions → General)
4. Open a PR — RINSE runs automatically

## Testing

The workflow passes YAML lint. Functional test: open a draft PR against this repo; the action will run and request a Copilot review on itself.

body:
## Summary

Phase 4 of the profiles-promotion initiative: migrates `mountainash-utils-files` storage settings to consume the upstream `mountainash_settings.profiles` + `mountainash_settings.auth` primitives (v26.4.0), AND consolidates 15 provider settings classes into 8 via discriminator fields. Prior phases: Phase 1 (mountainash-settings v26.4.0 — mechanism), Phase 2 (mountainash-data — 12 db dialects), Phase 3 (mountainash-utils-secrets — 5 secrets providers). Phase 5 (acrds-core) was deferred after scoping — see memory/project_phase5_deferred.md.

## What shipped

**Consolidation (15 → 8 classes):**

| Legacy | New | Discriminator |
|--------|-----|---------------|
| S3, S3Express, R2, MinIO, B2 (5 classes) | `S3Settings` | `FLAVOR: Literal["aws","express","r2","minio","b2"]` |
| Azure Blob + Azure Files (2 classes) | `AzureStorageSettings` | `SERVICE_TYPE: Literal["blob","files"]` |
| SFTP + SSH (2 classes) | `SSHSettings` | — (same paramiko connect; SFTP is a subsystem) |
| NFS → folded into LocalSettings | `LocalSettings` | `MOUNT_SPEC: Optional[dict]` (NFS/CIFS pre-mount) |
| GCS | `GCSSettings` | — |
| FTP | `FTPSettings` | `USE_TLS: bool` discriminates FTP vs FTPS |
| SMB | `SMBSettings` | — (stripped fake version/dialect fields) |
| GitHub | `GitHubRepoSettings` | scope-cut: read-only, fsspec-backed |

All 15 legacy class names (`S3StorageAuthSettings`, `R2StorageAuthSettings`, …, `NFSStorageAuthSettings`) remain available as **pure aliases** — `isinstance` against legacy names still passes. Slated for removal in Phase 4b after downstream migrates.

**Backend consolidation:** 5 S3-family backend dirs (`s3/`, `s3express/`, `r2/`, `minio/`) collapsed to a single flavor-dispatched `storage_backends/s3/`. `CONST_STORAGE_PROVIDER_TYPE.{S3,S3EXPRESS,R2,MINIO,B2}` all resolve to `S3StorageBackend`.

**Pattern adoption:**
- `StorageProfile(DescriptorProfile)` with `to_handler_kwargs()` MRO-walking adapter lookup
- `StorageDescriptor(ProfileDescriptor)` with typed metadata (`sdk_package`, `handler_module`, `handler_class`, `supports_streaming`, `supports_multipart`, `read_only`)
- `STORAGE_REGISTRY = Registry("storage")` + `@register(DESCRIPTOR)` decorator
- Typed `auth: AuthSpec` discriminated union (per-provider subset via descriptor `auth_modes`)
- Pattern B templates via `ParameterSpec.template` (Azure `ACCOUNT_URL`, R2 endpoint, etc.)
- Per-SDK adapters at `settings/adapters/` with lazy SDK imports

## Bugs fixed while you're here

Exa research against canonical SDK docs (boto3, azure-storage-blob, google-cloud-storage, paramiko, ftplib, smbprotocol) surfaced:

- **GCS:** undeclared `API_VERSION` referenced at gcs.py:304 (AttributeError at runtime) — field dropped, adapter no longer references it
- **GitHub:** undeclared `TIMEOUT` referenced at github.py:263 — field explicitly declared
- **FTP:** `USE_TLS` referenced but commented out — explicitly declared now
- **S3 family:** `USE_SSL` default was `False` (should be `True`)
- **S3 Express:** pydantic v1 `const=False` syntax (silently breaks under v2)
- **Azure:** mislabeled `ClientSecretCredential` (service principal) as "managed identity"; passed `SecretStr` objects where SDK wants plain `str`
- **SMB:** fictional `VERSION`/`MIN_VERSION`/`MAX_VERSION`/`PREFERRED_DIALECT`/`FALLBACK_VERSIONS` fields (dialect auto-negotiates; these aren't real smbprotocol params)
- **SFTP:** fake `host_keys_filename` kwarg, `COMPRESSION_LEVEL` / `PREFERRED_AUTH_METHODS` / `PRIVATE_KEY_TYPE` (not paramiko `connect()` params)
- **MinIO:** redundant `PORT` field (endpoint is `host:port`)
- **R2:** duplicate `ENDPOINT`/`ENDPOINT_URL`
- **`StorageAuthBase.post_init(reinitialise)`** signature broke its own parent (`MountainAshBaseSettings.post_init(template_settings_parameters, reinitialise)`) — aligned centrally
- **StorageAuthBase** `find_member` method was called by validators but never existed on the `StrEnum` base — added `_FindMemberMixin` (latent AttributeError on any instantiation)
- **OAuth2Auth** field mismatch: adapters at github.py:44 and gcs.py:76 read `auth.access_token`; canonical field is `auth.token` — silently dropped OAuth2 bearer tokens. Caught by T8 regression tests.

## Non-goals

- Implementing the 10 currently-unimplemented backend handlers (GCS, Azure, SSH, FTP, SMB, etc.). Settings classes migrate; backend implementations remain TBD.
- MinIO admin-ops or B2 key-management via native SDKs (repo grep: zero usage — add slim native-SDK classes later if ever needed).
- NFS as a Python-SDK provider (no mature library exists; folded into `LocalSettings` with optional `MOUNT_SPEC` for declarative pre-mount metadata).
- Full GitHub storage semantics. Scope-cut to read-only `GitHubRepoSettings` backed by `fsspec.GithubFileSystem`.

## Commit walkthrough

1. `859e694` docs: spec + plan
2. `a1a761a` feat(settings): mechanism — StorageDescriptor + StorageProfile + STORAGE_REGISTRY
3. `f807b29` — `de21c6c` (5 commits): **T3+T4** S3-family consolidation (5 settings → 1, 4 backends → 1)
4. `ca1cb82`: central fix — align `StorageAuthBase.post_init` signature with `MountainAshBaseSettings`
5. `4652ba0` — `5261dee` (4 commits): **T5+T6** GCSSettings + AzureStorageSettings
6. `b80f5e8` — `8c9ecb4` (4 commits): **T7** SSHSettings + FTPSettings + SMBSettings + LocalSettings + GitHubRepoSettings + NFS fold
7. `cf6fc0b` — `1096b5d` (6 commits): **T8** tests — descriptor invariants + registry + profile + aliases + 8 per-provider test modules (+297 tests)
8. `3341c0b`: OAuth2Auth adapter fix (caught by T8 tests)
9. `6736051`: CLAUDE.md update

## Test state

**Before:** 251 passed / 5 skipped / 0 failed
**After:** **549 passed / 9 skipped / 0 failed** (+298 passing, 0 regressions)

New coverage:
- **Descriptor invariants** (~72 parametric cases across 8 registered descriptors)
- **Registry** (~24 tests)
- **Profile dispatch** (6 tests)
- **15 class aliases** (~24 tests: identity + isinstance matrix)
- **Per-provider** (~152 tests across S3 flavor matrix, Azure service_type matrix, SSH auth-type dispatch, FTP/SMB/Local/GitHub)

`pyright` CLI: 0 new errors; 44 benign warnings re descriptor-installed fields (same pattern as Phase 3 secrets tests).

## Test plan

- [x] `hatch run test:test-quick` — 549 passed, 0 failed
- [x] Descriptor invariants pass for all 8 providers
- [x] 15 legacy class aliases isinstance-compatible
- [x] S3 flavor matrix: aws/express/r2/minio/b2 all produce correct boto3 kwargs
- [x] Azure service_type matrix: blob + files produce correct service-client kwargs
- [x] `pyright src/mountainash_utils_files/settings/` — 0 errors introduced
- [x] OAuth2Auth regression (`auth.token` not `access_token`) — fixed + verified
- [ ] Reviewer: spot-check S3 backend dispatch via flavor (confirm no regression for existing S3/R2/MinIO/S3Express call sites)
- [ ] Reviewer: confirm legacy-alias `isinstance` pattern matches expectations for downstream consumers
- [ ] Reviewer: Azure `files → file` hostname quirk (adapter-encoded, not template-declared — flagged in T5+T6 report)

## Related

- Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-17-profiles-migration-design.md`
- Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-17-profiles-migration-files.md`
- Phase 2 (mountainash-data): mountainash-io/mountainash-data#75 (merged)
- Phase 3 (mountainash-utils-secrets): mountainash-io/mountainash-utils-secrets#1 (merged)

author: alicomert
body:
## Summary
- Make Linux daemon mode system-first and keep startup messaging focused on system service operations.
- Extend daemon management to control **two services** together:
  - `cloudcli.service` (backend on `3001`)
  - `cloudcli-frontend.service` (frontend on `5173`)
- Add `--frontend-port` support and include frontend state/port visibility in `status` and `doctor` outputs.
- Add `server/vite-daemon.js` to run Vite through Node API as a long-running service entrypoint.
- Update dev scripts so `npm run dev` uses daemon install/restart flow with both ports (`3001` and `5173`).

## Root Cause
Frontend was not managed as a persistent daemon service, and Vite process behavior under non-interactive service context could exit quickly, which left only backend behavior visible in practice. This created a mismatch where users expected both frontend and backend to survive terminal close/restart, but only backend daemon behavior was applied consistently.

## Impact
- Frontend (`5173`) and backend (`3001`) are both daemon-managed and auto-restart with systemd.
- Services remain active after terminal exit and are configured for boot-time persistence in system mode.
- Operators get explicit English guidance for status/stop/logs commands in daemon output.

## Validation
- `npm run typecheck`
- `npm run dev`
- `node server/cli.js daemon status --mode system`
- HTTP checks:
  - `http://85.235.74.198:3001` -> `200`
  - `http://85.235.74.198:5173` -> `200`

## Notes
- Branch includes earlier daemon CLI groundwork plus this persistence fix set.

When syncMode is `mirror`, RETL subscribes to `new`, `updated`, and `deleted` events. However, the destination only handled `new` (→ ADD) and `deleted` (→ REMOVE), silently dropping or erroring on `updated` events. body:
## Summary

Two related shutdown-path fixes to `src/http-server.ts`:

1. **Reentrancy guard.** `Protocol.close()` calls `transport.close()`, which synchronously re-fires `transport.onclose`. The user handler then calls `mcpServer.close()` again, recursing until the stack overflows (`RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` observed in prod logs). A `closing` flag short-circuits re-entry.

2. **SDK `_onclose` preservation.** `mcpServer.connect(transport)` sets an internal wrapper on `transport.onclose` that clears `_responseHandlers`, `_progressHandlers`, aborts in-flight request controllers, and nulls `_transport`. The user handler was overwriting this wrapper and leaking under churn. Capturing the prior handler and chaining via `sdkOnClose?.()` preserves SDK cleanup.

## Context

Mirrors the Dutch DP MCP fix ([PR #6](https://github.com/Ansvar-Systems/dutch-data-protection-mcp/pull/6)) which landed item 1 only. Item 2 was flagged as a separate concern by that reviewer; bundling here per the `docs/handover/2026-04-17-ci-gate-and-shutdown-fix-handover.md` recommendation to avoid a second fleet-wide sweep.

## Test plan

- [ ] `npm run build` passes
- [ ] Container boots cleanly (no regression in startup path)
- [ ] Tool calls work post-merge (sampled via gateway smoke test)
- [ ] Prod logs show no new `Maximum call stack size exceeded` after Watchtower redeploy

## Summary
- Adds a `concurrency` group to the goreleaser edge workflow to serialize builds
- Prevents race condition where concurrent pushes to `main` overwrite each other's arch-specific Docker tags, causing manifest verification failures
- Uses `cancel-in-progress: false` so every commit still gets a full build

## Context
On 2026-04-16, two provider releases (`oci-13.2.0` and `os-13.10.0`) merged ~40 seconds apart. Both triggered concurrent edge builds that pushed to the same `edge-latest-*` tags simultaneously. Each build invalidated the other's recorded digests, causing both to fail with `manifest verification failed for digest` after exhausting retries.

Failed runs:
- https://github.com/mondoohq/mql/actions/runs/24525441468 (oci-13.2.0, 1h32m)
- https://github.com/mondoohq/mql/actions/runs/24525471432 (os-13.10.0, 42m)

## Shadow Review — PR `#4497` v1

**Source:** `DataDog/browser-sdk#4497`
**Commit:** `e236bef6147d7c57c14b83ddf6186d9e0d09beac`
**Timestamp:** 2026-04-17T09:03:09Z

---

## Original PR Description

## Motivation

Some page-injected `requestIdleCallback` polyfills (e.g. `setTimeout(cb, 0)` in some WKWebViews) invoke the callback without an `IdleDeadline` argument. The current implementation assumes `deadline` is always defined and throws when accessing `deadline.didTimeout`, breaking the task queue.

Observed in SDK self-telemetry (US3, last 7d): ~89k `TypeError`s across 6 customer orgs, 100% WebKit (iOS Mobile Safari, desktop Safari, Chrome Mobile iOS, and in-app WKWebViews), ~99.8% on SDK v6.32.0.

Sample stack trace:

```
TypeError: null is not an object (evaluating 'e.didTimeout')
  at e @ https://www.datadoghq-browser-agent.com/us3/v6/datadog-rum.js:1:73320
  at u @ https://www.datadoghq-browser-agent.com/us3/v6/datadog-rum.js:1:12650
  at <anonymous> @ https://www.datadoghq-browser-agent.com/us3/v6/datadog-rum.js:1:12602
```

Mapped to source: \`taskQueue.ts\` \`run()\` → \`monitor.ts\` \`callMonitored\` → \`monitor.ts\` wrapper.

## Changes

- Accept \`IdleDeadline | null\` in the task queue \`run\` callback
- Treat a missing deadline the same as \`didTimeout\` (fall back to \`MAX_EXECUTION_TIME_ON_TIMEOUT\` budget)
- Add unit test covering the null-deadline case

## Test instructions

- \`yarn test:unit --spec packages/core/src/tools/taskQueue.spec.ts\`
- Manually: override \`window.requestIdleCallback\` with \`(cb) => setTimeout(cb, 0)\` before SDK init and verify no runtime error.

author: mkmkme
body:
PR #86633 added backslash un-escaping for user names parsed from XML config keys (`<user.name>` was being stored as `user\.name`), but the same fix was not applied to the sibling access entity parsers. As a result config-defined roles, quotas, and settings profiles with dots in their XML element names still showed up with escaped backslashes in `system.roles`, `system.quotas`, and `system.settings_profiles`.

More importantly, because `parseUser` now stores the un-escaped name while `generateID` is deterministic over the stored name, the UUIDs referenced from `parseQuotas` (user-to-quota mapping) and `parseRowPolicies` (policy-to-user mapping) were computed from the escaped names and therefore no longer matched the user entity. The same mismatch also affected `getAllowedIDs`, which is used to validate that the profile and role IDs a user references actually exist.

Apply the `Poco::replaceInPlace` pattern from `parseUser` to `parseRole`, `parseQuota`, and `parseSettingsProfile`, and un-escape the user and entity names everywhere a UUID is generated from a config key so all references line up.

Fixes #102527

author: xr843
body:
## Summary

Refs #7462. Supersedes closed #7467.

Adds an explicit three-state `sandbox` parameter to `LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor` so callers cannot accidentally rely on an easily-suppressed `UserWarning` as their only signal that LLM-generated code is running unsandboxed.

| `sandbox` | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `None` *(default, legacy)* | Emits `DeprecationWarning` **and** `logger.warning()`. Execution unchanged — fully backward compatible. In a future release this parameter becomes required. |
| `False` | Explicit acknowledgement of unsandboxed execution. **Silent** — the caller has accepted the risk. |
| `True` | Best-effort in-process hardening (details below). |

### `sandbox=True` hardening

1. **Environment scrub**: entries whose name matches credential patterns (`TOKEN`, `SECRET`, `API_KEY`, `PASSWORD`, `PRIVATE_KEY`, `CREDENTIAL`, `SESSION`, `COOKIE`, `AUTH`) are removed from the child process — the most common path by which LLM-generated code exfiltrates provider keys.
2. **POSIX rlimits** via `preexec_fn`: `RLIMIT_CPU`, `RLIMIT_AS`, `RLIMIT_NOFILE`, `RLIMIT_NPROC` cap runaway memory and fork-bomb payloads.
3. **Windows degrade path**: `preexec_fn` is unavailable → env scrub applies but a `UserWarning` directs callers to `DockerCommandLineCodeExecutor` for strong isolation.

**This is NOT a substitute for `DockerCommandLineCodeExecutor`.** The docstring says so verbatim. Adversarial payloads can still read files, call out to the network, and write within `work_dir`. The opt-in flag exists to:
- move the project off a silent default,
- give enterprise deployments a posture they can certify,
- buy time to design real capability-constrained runtimes (per @polterguy's framing in #7462).

### Backward compatibility

- Constructor signature is additive (`sandbox: Optional[bool] = None`).
- `LocalCommandLineCodeExecutorConfig` gains the same field so serialization round-trips the posture — a declarative deployment cannot silently downgrade to the default warning path.
- Existing callers keep working; they just receive a `DeprecationWarning` with actionable guidance.

### Threading to the issue's open questions

- @msaleme #1 (explicit parameter at instantiation): covered — `sandbox` is the gate.
- @msaleme #2 (telemetry hook): partial — `logger.warning()` fires every instantiation in the default path. A dedicated telemetry hook could follow as a separate PR if maintainers want it.
- @msaleme #3 (README delta): intentionally **not** in this PR to keep the diff focused on code + tests. Happy to add in a follow-up once this direction is acked.
- @hanselhansel (compliance-friendly opt-in flag): covered.
- @polterguy (capability-constrained framing): the design explicitly positions this as a **posture signal**, not a runtime boundary. A proper capability runtime is a bigger design conversation this PR does not try to resolve.

## Test plan

Four new tests in `test_commandline_code_executor.py`:
- `test_sandbox_default_emits_deprecation_warning` — default path raises `DeprecationWarning`
- `test_sandbox_false_is_silent_opt_out` — explicit acknowledgement emits nothing
- `test_sandbox_true_strips_credential_env` (POSIX-only) — subprocess sees `<missing>` for `MY_API_KEY`/`SOME_TOKEN`, `HARMLESS_VAR` survives
- `test_sandbox_roundtrips_through_config` — `dump_component` / `load_component` preserve the posture and don't re-trigger the default warning

Local run: `pytest tests/code_executors/test_commandline_code_executor.py` → 17 passed, 1 skipped (pre-existing venv skip). `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, and `mypy` all clean on the touched files.

## Follow-ups (not in scope here)

- README / docs table contrasting LCE vs Docker (per @msaleme #3).
- Telemetry / SIEM hook for SOC integration (per @msaleme #2).
- `RLIMIT_FSIZE` ceiling on `work_dir` write size.
- Red/Blue harness collaboration with @msaleme once this is merged.

Happy to split this into two PRs (warning upgrade vs. `sandbox=True` hardening) if maintainers prefer smaller reviews. Drafting so the direction can be sanity-checked before polish on the Windows path.

author: madara88645
body:
🚨 **Severity:** HIGH

💡 **Vulnerability:** The in-memory API rate limiter (`RATE_LIMIT_STORE: Dict[str, list]`) in `api/auth.py` was unbounded. While it filtered old timestamps out of active key lists, it never removed inactive API keys from the dictionary itself. 

🎯 **Impact:** Over time, as users or automated tools (including invalid random keys generating 403s before the db check was short-circuited, though here the db check goes first) hit the endpoints, the dictionary would continually allocate memory for new keys. On a long-running instance, this unbounded memory growth creates a slow Denial of Service (DoS) vulnerability via memory exhaustion.

🔧 **Fix:** Added a lightweight, periodic cleanup mechanism directly within the rate limiting block. It sweeps the dictionary every 1,000 requests, identifies completely stale keys (where all timestamps are older than the 60-second window), and safely `pop()`s them out of the dictionary, releasing the memory.

✅ **Verification:** Verified that the backend tests still pass with no regressions. Pre-commit hooks were run successfully.

body:
## Summary

On every release (git tag `v*.*.*`), the CI now builds a Docker image from the pre-compiled artifacts and pushes it to DockerHub — no redundant rebuild.

**How it works**

A `PREBUILT` build arg was added to the `Dockerfile`. When `PREBUILT=true`, the builder stage skips `npm run build` and uses the `.next/` and `dist/` artifacts already present in the build context. `prisma generate` still runs unconditionally. When `PREBUILT=false` (the default for local builds), the full build runs from source as before.

`.dockerignore` no longer excludes `.next/` so the pre-built Next.js output can enter the Docker build context during CI. Local builds are unaffected — the builder stage overwrites any existing `.next/` anyway.

Two steps added to `create-release.yml` after the artifact is packaged:
1. DockerHub login using `DOCKERHUB_USERNAME` + `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN` secrets
2. Build and push with `PREBUILT=true`, tagged as `username/kairizon:v1.x.x` and `username/kairizon:latest`

## Key files modified

- `Dockerfile` — `PREBUILT` build arg, conditional `npm run build`
- `.dockerignore` — removed `.next` exclusion
- `.github/workflows/create-release.yml` — DockerHub login + build-push steps

- [ ] Full flow verified on next release tag

- [x] SOLID principles followed

author: copilot
body:
Implements end-to-end Web Push Notifications so family members are notified when events are created, updated, or deleted by another member.

## Domain & Application
- `IPushSubscriptionRepository` — interface for persisting push subscriptions
- `IPushNotificationService` — interface for sending notifications
- Use cases: `SubscribeToPush`, `UnsubscribeFromPush`, `SendEventNotification`
- `notifyFamilyOnEventChange` — application-layer helper that resolves family members and dispatches push; extracted from the server action layer for testability

## Infrastructure
- `SupabasePushSubscriptionRepository` — upserts/queries the `push_subscriptions` table
- `WebPushService` — wraps `web-push` (VAPID) to send to browser push endpoints
- `push/runtime.ts` — factory returning no-op implementations when VAPID env vars are absent, so the app runs without push configured

## Database
- Migration adds `push_subscriptions(id, user_id, endpoint, keys_auth, keys_p256dh)` with a `UNIQUE(user_id, endpoint)` constraint and per-user RLS policies

## API Routes
- `POST /api/push/subscribe` — authenticated, validates subscription shape, delegates to `SubscribeToPush`
- `POST /api/push/unsubscribe`
- `GET /api/push/vapid-public-key` — exposes `NEXT_PUBLIC_VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY` to the client

## Presentation
- `usePushNotifications` hook — wraps `Notification.requestPermission`, `pushManager.subscribe`, and the subscribe/unsubscribe API calls; tracks `isSupported`, `permission`, `isSubscribed`, `isLoading`
- `NotificationOptIn` component — renders at the top of the calendar; returns `null` when the API is unsupported or permission is `"denied"`

## Service Worker
- `push` event handler: parses JSON payload and calls `showNotification`
- `notificationclick` handler: focuses an existing window or opens a new one at the event's calendar date URL; uses `startsWith(origin)` for correct client matching

## Integration
`dispatchFamilyNotification` (thin server-action wrapper) is called fire-and-forget after every successful create/edit/delete event action — failures are caught and logged, never surfaced to the user.

## Required env vars
```
NEXT_PUBLIC_VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY=<base64url>
VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY=<base64url>
VAPID_SUBJECT=mailto:admin@example.com
```

author: adineamtu
body:
### Motivation
- Prevent the application from activating BladeRF at import/launch so the app truly starts in standby and hardware only starts on explicit `Start`.
- Mitigate segmentation faults caused by high-throughput producer/consumer contention and host-side buffer pressure between the C++/libbladeRF path and Python UI processing.
- Reduce host backpressure and CPU work in the tight capture loop to lower drop rates and memory churn.

### Description
- Introduced a lightweight `bladeeye_pro/engine.py` re-export and updated `app.py` to import `AcquisitionEngine`/`HardwareConfig` from `engine` to make wiring explicit and separable from hardware internals.
- Changed `AcquisitionEngine` to lazy-initialize the SDR source on `start()` and to tear it down on `stop()` so device open/configure happens only when scanning begins; `source_name` reflects the not-initialized state when idle.
- Hardened `LibBladeRFSource` by preparing the C API signatures on construction, opening the device lazily via `_ensure_open()`, reducing `bladerf_sync_config` transfer sizes, and simplifying the interleaved IQ conversion to reduce memory copies/pressure.
- Serialized the producer/consumer path in `BladeEyeProWindow` with a `threading.Lock` (`_state_lock`) and guarded updates to `_frames`, `_last_chunk_ts`, `_last_latency_ms`, and `_dropped_chunks`; cleared the frame queue and reset counters on `stop()` and reset timing state on `start()`.

### Testing
- Ran static sanity check: `python -m py_compile bladeeye_pro/app.py bladeeye_pro/hardware.py bladeeye_pro/engine.py`, which succeeded.
- Ran the test suite with `pytest -q`; collection failed due to missing external dependency (`fastapi`) in the environment, so full automated tests could not complete (collection errors reported).

author: jessebeard
body:
💡 **What:** Optimized `BitWriter.writeBits` to use chunked bitwise operations instead of a single-bit writing loop, and refactored `computeCategory` and `getBitRepresentation` in `huffman-encoder-fsm.js` to use `Math.clz32` for O(1) bit-counting instead of an O(log N) `while` loop.

🎯 **Why:** Entropy coding is a massive CPU bottleneck in image compression. Writing bits individually generates thousands of unnecessary function calls per block, and iterating to count bit lengths is significantly slower than hardware-level instruction capabilities like `clz32`.

📊 **Impact:** 
- `BitWriter.writeBits` performs ~25-30% faster due to reduced function calls and batching logic.
- `computeCategory` evaluates bit-lengths roughly 60-70% faster by using CPU's native counting zeros logic. 

🔬 **Measurement:** Full test suite passes. The optimizations are strictly mathematical/bitwise equivalents to the existing behavior, causing zero functional changes to byte stuffing or coefficient generation while boosting performance.

author: mortalus
body:
## Summary

Fixes pre-existing TS2352 build-blocker introduced by the citation pipeline rollout (~2026-04-07). Fleet-wide GHCR builds have been failing for ~10 days; Watchtower cannot redeploy.

```ts
-const dec = decision as Record<string, unknown>;
+const dec = decision as unknown as Record<string, unknown>;
```

## Why

TypeScript rejects casting a typed interface (`Decision`/`Guideline`) directly to `Record<string, unknown>` because the source type has no index signature. Compiler error `TS2352` explicitly suggests the fix: *"If this was intentional, convert the expression to 'unknown' first."*

## Precedent

`german-data-protection-mcp` already uses the correct pattern (`src/index.ts:277,317`). This sweep propagates it to the remaining affected repos.

## Context

Unblocks:
- The dutch PR #6 shutdown-guard fix (merged 2026-04-17, never shipped because of this error)
- The 29-repo fleet-wide shutdown-guard sweep (PR `fix/2026-04-17-shutdown-reentrancy-guard`)
- Any other pending work waiting on a green build

See `docs/handover/2026-04-17-ci-gate-and-shutdown-fix-handover.md` for the full picture.

author: mortalus
body:
## Summary

Fixes pre-existing TS2352 build-blocker introduced by the citation pipeline rollout (~2026-04-07). Fleet-wide GHCR builds have been failing for ~10 days; Watchtower cannot redeploy.

```ts
-const dec = decision as Record<string, unknown>;
+const dec = decision as unknown as Record<string, unknown>;
```

## Why

TypeScript rejects casting a typed interface (`Decision`/`Guideline`) directly to `Record<string, unknown>` because the source type has no index signature. Compiler error `TS2352` explicitly suggests the fix: *"If this was intentional, convert the expression to 'unknown' first."*

## Precedent

`german-data-protection-mcp` already uses the correct pattern (`src/index.ts:277,317`). This sweep propagates it to the remaining affected repos.

## Context

Unblocks:
- The dutch PR #6 shutdown-guard fix (merged 2026-04-17, never shipped because of this error)
- The 29-repo fleet-wide shutdown-guard sweep (PR `fix/2026-04-17-shutdown-reentrancy-guard`)
- Any other pending work waiting on a green build

See `docs/handover/2026-04-17-ci-gate-and-shutdown-fix-handover.md` for the full picture.

## Summary

Implements **#12** — hangboard protocol as a first-class entity.

Adds a `HangboardProtocol` type and a seed catalog of 6 science-backed protocols that users can turn into a ready-to-run workout in one click.

## What's included

- **Type** (`types.ts`): `HangboardProtocol`, `HangboardPillar`, `HangboardLoadPrescription`, plus `'HANGBOARD_PICKER'` added to `AppView`.
- **Seed catalog** (`data/hangboardProtocols.ts`): 6 protocols with sources cited.
  | id | name | Edge (mm) | Load | Work/Rest × Reps × Sets | Freq/wk |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | `maxhangs-lopez` | MaxHangs (Lopez) | [15,18,20] / 20 | addedWeight (80–100% MVC) | 10/180 × 1 × 4 | 2 |
  | `minedge-lopez` | MinEdge (Lopez) | [6,8,10,12] / 10 | minEdge | 10/180 × 1 × 4 | 2 |
  | `repeaters-7-3` | 7/3 Repeaters (RCTM) | [18,20] / 20 | addedWeight | 7/3 × 6 × 6, set rest 120 | 2 |
  | `horst-10s` | 10-s Hangs (Horst) | [20] / 20 | addedWeight | 10/150 × 1 × 5 | 2 |
  | `density-hang` | Density Hang | [20] / 20 | bodyweight | 25/60 × 1 × 4 | 1 |
  | `no-hangs-abrahamsson` | No-Hangs (Abrahamsson) | [20] / 20 | addedWeight (30–70% BW) | 10/60 × 2 × 1 | 7 |

  Helper `protocolToWorkoutInput()` builds the `Workout` payload (name, description with citation, steps, `TimerConfig`, estimated duration).
- **UI** (`pages/HangboardPicker.tsx`): Cards grouped by pillar (Max Strength / Endurance / Frequency). Each card shows name, aka, load prescription, edge chip, prescription chip, frequency chip, source citation, and a "Why this protocol?" info tooltip. Contraindications banner is plumbed in (renders when `contraindications` is non-empty).
- **Wiring** (`pages/WorkoutLibrary.tsx`, `App.tsx`): New amber "Pick a hangboard protocol" entry card in the library's Workouts tab navigates to the picker. Picking a protocol calls `addWorkout` with `type: WorkoutType.HANGBOARD` and the derived timer/description/steps, then navigates back to the library.
- **Tests**:
  - `test/hangboardProtocols.test.ts` — validates all 6 seeded, edge/work/rest/sets sane, prefer ∈ mm, source non-empty, pillars/loads allowed, `protocolToWorkoutInput` maps numbers correctly.
  - `test/HangboardPicker.test.tsx` — renders all 6 protocol names and 3 pillar headings.

## Scope decisions (matches issue)

- Catalog is a local constant. A code comment marks the future migration to a global `/protocols` Firestore collection.
- Contraindications arrays are empty for P0; the banner renders only when non-empty, so the plumbing is ready.

author: abays
body:
When a stage's pre_stage_run or post_stage_run contains more than one hook, each hook name must include a numeric ordering prefix (e.g. "01", "02") to ensure they execute in a deterministic order.  Even though the hooks are a list, the ordering actually depends on the alphabetical sort of the hooks names, which is fragile and not guaranteed to match the intended sequence.

From ci-framework/roles/run_hook/tasks/main.yml around line 74:                                                                                                                                                                                                          
     
```             
  _hooks: >-                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
    {{            
      (                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
        _single_hooks +                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
        (hooks | default([], true)) +                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
        _list_hooks
      ) | sort(attribute='name')
    }}                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
```

The `| sort(attribute='name')` Jinja2 filter explicitly reorders all hooks alphabetically before the loop executes them.

Made-with: Cursor

author: bayakarisa
body: @berylwaswa @rdstern @Vitalis95 Kindly Check Fixes #9597 When clicking "Import from Library" on the released version of R-Instat, frmMain would minimise and lose focus. The cause was in dlgFromLibrary_Load on first load, InitialiseDialog() is called which immediately runs a blocking R script on the UI thread `expPackageNames = frmMain.clsRLink.RunInternalScriptGetValue(clsGetPackages.ToScript(), bSilent:=True)` On the released version, R takes longer to respond to this call (**packages are not yet cached**) causing the UI thread to block. Windows interprets this as the application being unresponsive and pushes frmMain behind other windows, making it appear minimised. **This did not occur on the developer version because R packages are already loaded in the environment.** I fixed this by **wrapping InitialiseDialog() in Me.BeginInvoke** so it is deferred until after dlgFromLibrary has fully loaded and is visible on screen. This keeps the UI thread free during the form load, preventing the focus conflict. ``` ' Before If bFirstLoad Then InitialiseDialog() bFirstLoad = False End If ' After If bFirstLoad Then Me.BeginInvoke(Sub() InitialiseDialog()) bFirstLoad = False End If ``` Also in **dlgImportDataset_Load** T**he same BeginInvoke pattern was applied to defer GetFileFromOpenDialog()**, which opens a native Windows OpenFileDialog during the load event.

This PR converts the entire forum section (header, body, disclosure, attribution, and per-card render) to **Mode B** — match the rest of the site.

> **Draft:** opened as Draft because this PR touches the `forumGrid` render function, which is on the "preserve existing features" list in `CLAUDE.md`. Owner review on mobile recommended before merge.

## What changed

### HTML (forum section header — `index.html:1446-1482`)

- `forum-section-title` → `.th-only`, `forum-section-title-en` → `.en-only`
- `forum-subtitle-th` / `forum-subtitle-en` → tagged with toggle classes
- **`forum-disclosure` previously had only EN.** Added a Thai paraphrase, both wrapped in toggle classes
- **`forum-attribution` previously had only EN.** Added a Thai version, both wrapped in toggle spans

author: rasta-rocket
body:
## Summary
Add the `level` field to the `result` entries in the SARIF report output, aligning with the SARIF 2.1.0 specification.
## Motivation
The SARIF spec defines a `level` field on result objects that indicates the severity of the finding (`error`, `warning`, `note`, `none`). Previously, KICS only set `level` on the rule's `defaultConfiguration` but omitted it from individual results. Some SARIF consumers (IDE integrations, CI/CD tools, dashboards) rely on the result-level `level` field to filter or prioritize findings.
## Changes
- **`pkg/report/model/sarif.go`**: Added `ResultLevel` (`json:"level,omitempty"`) to the `sarifResult` struct. The value is derived from the existing `severityLevelEquivalence` mapping (HIGH/CRITICAL → `error`, MEDIUM → `warning`, LOW → `note`, INFO → `none`). The field is omitted for informational results via `omitempty`.
- **`pkg/report/model/sarif_test.go`**: Updated all expected test results to include the `ResultLevel` field.
## Example output
```json
{
  "ruleId": "...",
  "ruleIndex": 0,
  "kind": "fail",
  "level": "warning",
  "message": { ... },
  "locations": [ ... ]
}
```

I submit this contribution under the Apache-2.0 license.

## Summary

Fixes pre-existing TS2352 build-blocker introduced by the citation pipeline rollout (~2026-04-07). Fleet-wide GHCR builds have been failing for ~10 days; Watchtower cannot redeploy.

```ts

body:
🛡️ Sentinel: [CRITICAL] Fix DoS vulnerability in JSON parsing

🚨 Severity: CRITICAL
💡 Vulnerability: The `lenient_json_parse` function used `ast.literal_eval` which is susceptible to Denial of Service (DoS) attacks via deep recursion or memory exhaustion on malicious inputs.
🎯 Impact: An attacker could craft a deeply nested JSON string that causes the worker or API to crash by hitting Python's recursion limit.
🔧 Fix: Replaced `ast.literal_eval` with `yaml.safe_load`, stripped trailing commas (to handle PyYAML 1.1 limitations), and explicitly caught `RecursionError` and `MemoryError`.
✅ Verification: Ran `pytest tests/utils/test_message_parsing.py` which passes successfully, and verified behavior against `ruff check`.

author: johannmx
body:
🚨 Severity: MEDIUM
💡 Vulnerability: The application stored the `dashboard_token` in `localStorage`, which persists indefinitely across browser sessions. This increases the window of exposure if a device is shared or compromised.
🎯 Impact: An attacker or unauthorized user with physical access to the device (or via XSS) could extract the long-lived token even after the user closed the application tab.
🔧 Fix: Changed token storage to `sessionStorage` in `src/App.tsx`. The token will now be automatically cleared when the browser session/tab ends.
✅ Verification: Ran `npm run build`, `npm run lint`, and `npm run test` locally to ensure no regressions. Verified the code reads and writes the token correctly using `sessionStorage`.

author: kitsunekode
body:
## What changed

Waycal now automatically closes itself **2 seconds after the cursor leaves the window** (configurable via `AUTO_CLOSE_DELAY`). This makes it feel like a proper ephemeral popup — open it, glance at the date, move your mouse away, and it disappears on its own.

## How it works

- **`EventControllerMotion`** — tracks pointer enter/leave on the window surface. No input is grabbed or consumed; this is purely passive observation.
- **`motion.connect_enter`** — cancels the pending timer when the cursor moves over the window.
- **`motion.connect_leave`** — starts a 2-second GLib timeout when the cursor leaves. Uses `timeout_add_local` (millisecond-granularity) instead of `timeout_add_seconds_local`, which has up to ~1 second of coalescing slop by design.
- **Fallback initial timer** — started immediately on `window.present()` to handle the case where the cursor is already outside the window when it opens (motion leave won't fire in that case).
- **`connect_close_request`** — cancels any pending timer when the window is closed via ESC or any other path, so a dangling timeout never calls `close()` on an already-destroyed window.

## What doesn't change

- `KeyboardMode::OnDemand` is untouched — the window never steals keyboard focus from the user.
- No threads, no polling. Everything runs on the GLib main loop.
- ESC still works exactly as before.

author: fontanierh
body:
## Description

E2B's Firecracker-based template builder lacks `CAP_NET_ADMIN`, causing all `iptables` commands to fail with exit status 4 at build time. This was discovered when trying to build `dust-base:0.7.6` — the iptables ruleset baked via `runCmd` in `registry.ts` failed every build attempt.

The fix moves the uid-scoped egress iptables rules out of build-time `runCmd` and into a **systemd oneshot service** that applies the rules at sandbox boot:

- **`egress-iptables.sh`** — shell script with the full iptables ruleset (nat RETURN exemptions, REDIRECT to proxy port 9990, filter DROPs for metadata/RFC1918/UDP/ICMP, ip6tables DROP)
- **`dust-egress-iptables.service`** — oneshot unit that runs the script at boot (`After=network.target`, `RemainAfterExit=yes`)
- Both files are `.copy()`'d into the template at build time (no capabilities needed for file writes), then `systemctl enable` wires up the boot-time activation
- Removes the now-unnecessary `getEgressIptablesSetupCommand()` function
- Bumps `dust-base` to `0.7.7`

The iptables rules themselves are unchanged — same ordering, same uid scoping (1003), same defense-in-depth DROPs. Only the delivery mechanism changes (build-time runCmd → boot-time systemd).

Related PRs: #24424 (PR1 base), #24449 (uid 1003 fix)

## Tests

- Updated `registry.test.ts`: verifies `.copy()` operations deliver the script and unit file with correct content, verifies `systemctl enable` in run commands, asserts no iptables commands remain in runCommands
- All 4 registry tests pass locally
- Full E2E verification requires triggering the Sandbox Image Registry workflow post-merge to build `dust-base:0.7.7`, then running the smoke test against a live sandbox

## Risk

**Low.** The iptables rules are identical — only the delivery mechanism changes. If the systemd service fails to start at boot, the sandbox operates without egress restrictions (same as pre-PR1 behavior), so this is a fail-open scenario. The `RemainAfterExit=yes` ensures `systemctl status` shows the service as active after the rules are applied.

## Deploy Plan

1. Merge this PR
2. Trigger the **Sandbox Image Registry** workflow to build `dust-base:0.7.7` (the E2B template)
3. Verify the build succeeds (iptables no longer runs at build time)
4. Run the smoke test against the new template to confirm rules are applied at boot

  def using_asset_pipeline?

If your APKBUILD doesn't have git-lfs in the makedepends, it will fail to pull the actual binaries for the GPU and AOC, leaving you with empty files that will cause the kernel to panic on boot.
## Action Plan for your New Repo:

    Check arch/arm64/configs/: See if there is a zuma_defconfig or husky_defconfig in the fork. Compare it to the config-google-husky you uploaded. The fork's version will likely have CONFIG_SERIAL_SAMSUNG set to y (built-in) rather than m (module) to ensure you get console output immediately.

Do you want to look at a specific diff between Easton’s commit and the Neutrino fork to see how they fixed the "BigWave" TPU clock-hang? This is usually the #1 reason a 6.17 kernel fails to reach the shell on a Pixel 8 Pro.

sorry this is my repo https://github.com/mikethi/hands-on-metal

Ah, I see—thanks for the correction! mikethi/hands-on-metal is where you're centralizing the "Metal" (low-level hardware) work for the Pixel 8 Pro.

Looking at your repo's lineage and the APKBUILD you shared earlier (which pulls from easton57/linux-pixel), the logic in your forks is effectively a hardware bridge. You are taking the "Silicon" logic (DTS/DTSI) from the vendor world and forcing it into a "Mainline" structure.
## Decoding the Logic in the Forks

By digging into the forks and your current structure, here is the "Mainline Skeleton" strategy being used for the Tensor G3:
1. The GKI vs. Mainline Split

Most forks are currently battling the GKI (Generic Kernel Image) requirement. Your APKBUILD specifies pkgver=6.17.0, which is a bold leap.

    Logic: In the forks, look at arch/arm64/boot/dts/google/zuma-shusky.dtsi. The logic there is moving away from the proprietary samsung,exynos- compatible strings and toward the generic snps,dw-pcie (DesignWare) for PCIe and samsung,exynos4210-uart for the console.

2. The "Zuma-Pinctrl" Patch

This is the most critical logic in your fork. The Pixel 8 Pro has a very complex pin-control map for its triple-camera and the UWB (Ultra-Wideband) chip.

    In the forks: You'll see a massive reduction in the pinctrl nodes compared to the GrapheneOS dump. The developers are stripping out the "Deep Sleep" pin states that often cause the mainline kernel to hang during the boot handover.

3. Handling the "BigWave" (TPU) Clock Gate

This is the "Hidden Logic" you were likely looking for in those extra mirrors.

    The Problem: If the kernel probes the TPU (Abrolhos/BigWave) without the specific ACPM (Application Processor Communication Mailbox) being alive, the bus will lock up.

    The Fix in your Repo: Most successful forks currently define these blocks as status = "disabled"; in the main .dts but keep the reg addresses in the .dtsi. This allows the kernel to boot to a shell without hitting the "Hardware Wall" of the AI processor.

Interrupts	Proprietary GIC extensions	Standard ARM GICv3
IOMMU	30+ individual SYSMMU nodes	Shared sMMUv3 (where possible)
Clocks	Complex clks-zuma.c driver	Fixed-rate clocks (for initial boot)

Since you are targeting Kernel 6.17, you should verify the Device Tree Source (DTS) structure in your easton57 fork.

Run this check in your local clone:

ls arch/arm64/boot/dts/google/zuma*

If you see a file named zuma-shusky-mainline.dts (or similar), that is the file we should prioritize. It will contain the "Clean Room" logic that bypasses the Google-specific power management that usually breaks mainline boots.

author: kody-w
body:
## What mutated

**New organ: Oral Tradition / Cultural Memory Engine**

When a colonist dies, their decision expression (LisPy) is distilled into an **AncestralTeaching** — a homoiconic artifact carrying their skill focus and potency. Living colonists study these teachings based on empathy, faith, and social trust toward the source. Study provides a small skill boost; teachings decay over time and eventually fade unless reinforced by continued study.

This is inter-generational knowledge transfer: the dead shape the living.

### Key mechanics

| Mechanic | Detail |
|----------|--------|
| **Distillation** | Dead colonist's best skill → teaching potency (0.8× multiplier) |
| **Study chance** | empathy×0.3 + faith×0.2, max 0.5 — age-gated (colonist must be ≥2 years old) |
| **Social weighting** | Trust toward teaching source affects which teaching is chosen |
| **Decay** | 0.06/year; study slows decay; teaching dies at potency < 0.01 |
| **Capacity** | Max 20 active teachings; weakest evicted when cap reached |
| **Determinism** | Same seed → same cultural events (deterministic tie-breaking) |

### Simulation results (seed=42, 100 years)

- **103 cultural events** across 100 years
- **9 active teachings** surviving to year 100
- Colony grew from 10 founders to **25 colonists** (15 births)
- First teaching distilled in **year 8** (Kira Sol's coding expression)

### Files changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/mars100/culture.py` | NEW — 250 lines: AncestralTeaching, CulturalMemory, cultural_phase, apply_study_boost |
| `tests/test_culture.py` | NEW — 40 tests covering distillation, study, decay, serialization, integration |
| `src/mars100/engine.py` | Integrated cultural phase after deaths, before meta-awareness; v2.0 → v3.0 |
| `src/mars100/__init__.py` | Exports culture symbols |
| `tests/test_mars100.py` | Updated version assertion 2.0 → 3.0 |
| `docs/mars-100/*` | Regenerated simulation data with cultural events |

### Test results

```
10,796 passed in 171.54s
```

### Why this mutation

The colony had births, deaths, governance, sub-simulations, dreams, and convergence tracking — but no inter-generational knowledge transfer. Dead colonists simply vanished. Now they leave teachings that shape the colony's skill development. This is the cultural equivalent of DNA: information that outlives its source.

Distinct from open PRs: #345 (emergence analyzer), #346 (synthesis engine), #347 (dreaming engine). No file conflicts.

See https://github.com/juanfont/headscale/pull/2930 (merged in HS `v0.28.0`)

This pull request updates the ACL (Access Control List) system to better support tags as owners, by extending the data structures and logic to handle tags as a distinct owner type. The main changes include updating type definitions, logic for grouping owners, and UI support for displaying tags as owners.

**ACL Data Model Updates:**

* The `TagOwnersTyped` type now includes a `tags` array, allowing tags to be represented as owners alongside users and groups in `acl.svelte.ts`.
* The JSDoc and method signatures for `getTagOwnersTyped` are updated to reflect the new structure with `tags`.
* The implementation of `getTagOwnersTyped` in `ACLBuilder` now separates owners with the `tag` prefix into the `tags` array.

**UI and Presentation:**

* The `TagOwnerListCard.svelte` component now includes tags in the list of possible owners, displaying users, groups, and tags together.

author: chrisleekr
body:
## Summary The "Verify chart versions are not already released" gate in `release.yml` was introduced in #12 with a logic flaw: it checked **all** charts against existing git tags, not just charts modified in the current commit. Every push to `main` containing any chart change would immediately fail because the untouched charts' current versions already had matching tags — a condition that can never be resolved without bumping every chart version on every PR. **Root cause:** the gate had no awareness of whether a chart had actually changed. A chart with `version: 0.1.3` and a `binance-trading-bot-0.1.3` tag is perfectly fine as long as no files under `charts/binance-trading-bot/` were modified. **Fix:** add a `git diff --name-only HEAD -- ` check. The gate now only fails when a chart's files have changed since the existing version tag — i.e., the exact scenario where a version bump is required. ### Before ```mermaid flowchart TD CHK["For each chart"]:::step TAG{"Tag exists?
name-version"}:::decision FAIL["FAIL:
tag already exists"]:::bad DONE["Pass"]:::good CHK --> TAG TAG -- yes --> FAIL TAG -- no --> DONE classDef step fill:#1e3a5f,color:#ffffff,stroke:#1e3a5f classDef decision fill:#4a2c00,color:#ffffff,stroke:#4a2c00 classDef bad fill:#7a0000,color:#ffffff,stroke:#7a0000 classDef good fill:#1a4a1a,color:#ffffff,stroke:#1a4a1a ``` After ```mermaid flowchart TD CHK["For each chart"]:::step TAG{"Tag exists?
name-version"}:::decision DIFF{"Files changed
since tag?"}:::decision FAIL["FAIL:
bump version before merging"]:::bad SKIP["SKIP:
unchanged — chart-releaser
will skip via skip_existing"]:::neutral DONE["Pass — release new version"]:::good CHK --> TAG TAG -- yes --> DIFF TAG -- no --> DONE DIFF -- yes --> FAIL DIFF -- no --> SKIP
