author: mvanhorn
body:
Closes #2166

## What

Adds a one-line note in the README install section warning that the Linux release binary is linked against glibc, and pointing Alpine / musl users to either a glibc-based base image or the build-from-sources path.

## Why

The error message Alpine users see (`cannot execute: required file not found`) is opaque - it looks like a missing file but actually means bash found the binary and the kernel refused to load it because `/lib/ld-musl-*` is not the glibc dynamic linker the binary was built against. The reporter of #2166 described exactly this flow and noted "I did not find anything documented regarding any system dependencies."

## Scope

Docs-only. No code or binary behavior change. Out of scope for this PR:
- Shipping a musl-tagged release binary. That's a real option but a bigger change (CI matrix + tests). The docs change lands standalone and a musl build can be a follow-up if the maintainers want it.
- Adding an install.sh that refuses to run on musl. There's no install.sh today, so nothing to gate.

## Verified

- `grep -n "Build from sources" README.md` matches the anchor I link to (`#build-from-sources`).
- Rendered the diff locally; the blockquote renders as a callout under the Linux install snippet.

This contribution was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code).

body:
**Summary**
This PR fixes deployment defaults that can cause backend startup failure when PowerSync is enabled.

**Problem**
Backend validates that powersyncJwtSecret is at least 32 characters when powersyncUrl is set (see [settings.ts:76](vscode-file://vscode-app/Applications/Visual%20Studio%20Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html)).
Several deployment defaults used a shorter PowerSync JWT secret, which caused runtime validation failure and backend crash in default local/deploy flows.

**Changes**

- Docker Compose:
Updated backend POWERSYNC_JWT_SECRET
Updated matching PowerSync JWKS base64 key

- Kubernetes:
Updated default powersync.jwt.secretBase64

- Pulumi:
Updated backend POWERSYNC_JWT_SECRET default


**Validation**

- Ran Docker deployment flow from deploy directory
- Verified container health and service availability
- Confirmed backend starts successfully and serves health endpoint

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Low risk configuration and guardrail changes; main impact is that deployments/integrations that relied on old defaults or missing OAuth env vars will now error explicitly instead of failing later.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes PowerSync-enabled deployments by updating the default `POWERSYNC_JWT_SECRET` (and matching JWKS/base64 values) across Docker Compose, Helm `values.yaml`, Pulumi, and docs to satisfy the backend’s **32-character minimum** validation.
> 
> Improves Google and Microsoft integration startup by making `getOAuthConfig` throw a clear error when the backend returns no `client_id`, and resetting the cached config so env changes can be picked up without a restart.

author: jakex7
body:
# Why

When an iOS app extension target declares App Group entitlements (e.g. `'com.apple.security.application-groups': ['group.com.easwidgets']`) and the app group already exists in the Apple Developer team but is not linked to the target's bundle identifier, credential setup enabled the App Groups capability on the bundle but never attached the group resulting with capability on but 0 groups linked.
```
Current local entitlements:
{
  "com.apple.security.application-groups": [
    "group.com.easwidgets"
  ]
}
Will enable remote capability: com.apple.security.application-groups (App Groups).
Existing to disable:  [ 'FJXGJ28CQS_IN_APP_PURCHASE' ]
Patch Request: [ { capabilityType: 'APP_GROUPS', option: 'ON' } ]
✔ Synced capabilities: Enabled: App Groups
- Syncing capabilities identifiers
No capability identifiers need to be updated
✔ Synced capability identifiers: No updates
```
This is a regression introduced in https://github.com/expo/eas-cli/pull/3088/
Fixes https://github.com/expo/expo/issues/43677

# How

Fetch the bundle via `BundleId.infoAsync` to determine which IDs are already linked to this bundle.
- If it exists and ID is already linked -> skip.
- If it exists but is not linked -> just link.
- If it doesn't exist -> create it, then link (unchanged behavior).

# Test Plan

After this changes:
```
Current local entitlements:
{
  "com.apple.security.application-groups": [
    "group.com.easwidgets"
  ]
}
Will enable remote capability: com.apple.security.application-groups (App Groups).
Existing to disable:  [ '6C659CPDFA_IN_APP_PURCHASE' ]
Patch Request: [ { capabilityType: 'APP_GROUPS', option: 'ON' } ]
✔ Synced capabilities: Enabled: App Groups
- Syncing capabilities identifiers
Updating bundle identifier with capability identifiers: [
  {
    "capabilityType": "APP_GROUPS",
    "option": "ON",
    "relationships": {
      "appGroups": [
        "NW5UULASH8"
      ]
    }
  }
]
✔ Synced capability identifiers: Linked: group.com.easwidgets
```

author: wpank
body:
## Summary

168 commits, 499 files changed (~82K insertions). This PR brings three major workstreams together:

1. **Agent Registry & Relay** (AR01–AR07) — on-chain agent identity via ERC-8004 contracts, a WebSocket relay for agent presence/messaging, a new `roko agent serve` CLI command, Docker/Railway deployment changes, and an updated dashboard UI.
2. **UX Follow-up & Self-Hosting** (UX01–UX47) — the two remaining self-hosting P0 items (gate-failure feedback loop and PRD-publish auto-trigger), a new `roko plan validate` command, TUI performance rewrites, new HTTP endpoints, OpenAPI spec, safety enforcement, gate pipeline completion, and broad test coverage.
3. **TUI Parity** (T1–T19 + 30 individual fixes) — complete rewrite of the TUI data pipeline from polling to push-based, new widgets, modal system, keyboard navigation, and visual effects.

Plus: mirage-rs disk persistence, anvil compatibility fixes, CI workflows, and CLI refactoring.

---

## Agent Registry & Relay (AR01–AR07)

### What it is

A complete agent identity and discovery system. Agents get soulbound on-chain passports (ERC-8004), register their presence via a WebSocket relay, and become discoverable through a unified dashboard. The architecture:

```
Solidity contracts (on-chain identity)
  IdentityRegistry  — soulbound passport NFTs, 4-tier system, domain staking
  ReputationRegistry — EMA scoring with 30-day half-life decay, slashing
  ValidationRegistry — work proofs, gate results, validator attestation
        │
        │ bootstrapped into mirage fork state at startup
        ▼
mirage-rs (:8545) ←── single-origin reverse proxy ──→ agent-relay (:9011 loopback)
        ▲                                                    ▲
        │ dashboard polling                                  │ outbound WS client
        ▼                                                    ▼
mirage dashboard UI ("Agent Discovery" panel)     roko-agent-server (per-agent sidecar)
                                                         ▲
                                                         │
                                                  roko agent serve --agent-id X
```

### New binary: `agent-relay`

A standalone WebSocket presence relay (`apps/agent-relay/`). Agents connect, publish their card, and receive forwarded messages.

**Endpoints** (bound to `127.0.0.1:9011` by default, env: `ROKO_AGENT_RELAY_BIND`):

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/relay/health` | Health check |
| `GET` | `/relay/agents` | List connected agents |
| `GET` | `/relay/agents/ws` | Agent WebSocket (hello → card push → message forwarding) |
| `GET` | `/relay/cards/{id}` | Fetch stored agent card |
| `POST` | `/relay/messages` | Forward a message to an agent, await response (timeout: 15s default, 60s max) |
| `GET` | `/relay/events/ws` | Dashboard event stream (connect/disconnect/card/message events) |

**WebSocket protocol**: Agent sends `Hello` frame → relay responds `Ack` → agent pushes `Card` frame → relay forwards `Message` frames from `/relay/messages` callers → agent responds with `Response`/`Error`. Ping/pong keepalive supported.

### New CLI command: `roko agent serve`

Starts a per-agent HTTP sidecar with relay and chain registration.

```bash
roko agent serve \
  --agent-id my-agent \
  --bind 0.0.0.0:8081 \
  --relay-url http://localhost:9011 \
  --chain-rpc-url http://localhost:8545 \
  --identity-registry 0x8004A818BFB912233c491871b3d84c89A494BD9e \
  --passport-id 1 \
  --wallet-key 0x...
```

If a `roko.toml` exists with `agent.command`, it spawns a real LLM-backed agent and routes sidecar `/message` requests through it.

### Solidity contracts (`contracts/`)

Three ERC-8004 contracts with full Foundry test suites:

- **IdentityRegistry.sol** — Soulbound ERC-721 passports. 4-tier system (Protocol/Sovereign/Worker/Edge). Domain staking with auto-promotion (5K ETH → Worker, 25K → Sovereign). 1-day timelock on prompt hash changes. TEE attestation field. Capability bitmask.
- **ReputationRegistry.sol** — 7 reputation domains. EMA scoring with adaptive alpha. Authorized-source and peer-to-peer feedback flows. `slash()` with full history. 30-day half-life decay.
- **ValidationRegistry.sol** — Work proof submission with gate results array and deliverable merkle root. Per-passport gate pass rate tracking. Multi-validator attestation (auto-resolves after 3). 4 validator types (ReputationBased, StakeSecured, ZkML, TEE).

**Canonical addresses** (bootstrapped at mirage startup):
- Identity: `0x8004A818BFB912233c491871b3d84c89A494BD9e`
- Reputation: `0x8004A818BFB912233c491871b3d84c89A494Bd9F`
- Validation: `0x8004a818bfb912233c491871B3D84C89A494Bda0`

Init bytecodes are embedded in the mirage binary via `include_str!()` from `apps/mirage-rs/static/erc8004/`.

### Relay client in `roko-agent-server`

`features/relay_client.rs` — outbound WebSocket client that connects to the relay, sends Hello + Card frames, and dispatches incoming relay messages through the sidecar's `DispatchLike` trait (same code path as REST `/message`). Filters loopback addresses from relay advertisement.

`registration.rs` — builds `updateAgentCardUri(uint256,string)` calldata using alloy-primitives and submits it on-chain via `ChainWallet`. Falls back to a data-URI publisher when no wallet is configured.

### Dashboard UI changes

`apps/mirage-rs/static/js/agent_registry.js` — new "Agent Discovery" panel that merges data from chain-side `/api/agents` and relay `/relay/agents`. Shows: Agent, Role, Relay status (colored dot), Identity, Tier, Reputation, Cap Bits, Card URI, Last Seen.

`static/quickstart.sh` now supports two modes:
- **Local proof mode** (default): builds mirage + relay, seeds demo data, starts 20-agent simulation
- **Remote static mode** (`MIRAGE_DASHBOARD_RPC_URL` set): serves a static dashboard pointed at a remote mirage

### Docker & deployment changes

**`docker/mirage.Dockerfile`** — multi-stage build now compiles both `mirage-rs` and `agent-relay`. Runtime stage runs `start-mirage-with-relay.sh` which:
- Starts `agent-relay` on loopback as a background process
- Starts `mirage-rs` with `--enable-hdc --enable-knowledge --enable-stigmergy`
- Monitors both; if either dies, cleans up the other and exits

**`docker/docker-compose.yml`** changes:
- New env vars: `ROKO_AGENT_RELAY_BIND`, `ROKO_AGENT_RELAY_URL`, `MIRAGE_STATE_DIR`, `MIRAGE_SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL_SECS`
- New named volume: `mirage-state` (mounted at `/workspace/.roko`)
- Health check now probes both mirage RPC and `/relay/health`
- Port `9091` (metrics) is **no longer exposed separately**
- Start period increased from 20s to 30s

**`railway.toml`**:
- Watch patterns now include `apps/agent-relay/**` and `docker/start-mirage-with-relay.sh`
- Health check path changed to `/relay/health`
- Restart policy: `ON_FAILURE` with 3 retries

**Reverse proxy**: mirage-rs now proxies all `/relay/*` requests to the co-deployed relay on loopback. External clients only need one origin (`:8545`) for both RPC and relay APIs. Full bidirectional WebSocket bridge included.

---

## Mirage-rs Changes

### Disk persistence (`feat(mirage-rs): add disk persistence`)

New module `apps/mirage-rs/src/persist.rs` (480 lines). Periodic atomic JSON snapshots of the entire fork write layer + chain stores.

**New CLI flags**:
| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--snapshot-interval-secs` | `30` | Interval between periodic snapshots |
| `--state-dir` | `.roko/state/` | Override snapshot directory |
| `--no-persist` | off | Disable disk persistence entirely |

**Behavior change**: On startup, mirage loads the prior snapshot (if persistence is enabled) and resumes from that state. On shutdown, a final snapshot is written. Snapshots use write-then-rename for atomicity.

**Serialization**: `DirtyAccount`, `DirtyStore`, `LocalReceipt`, `LocalBlock` all gain `Serialize`/`Deserialize`. Runtime-only fields (`snapshots`, `next_snapshot_id`, `demote_protocols_to_slot_only`) are `#[serd

author: iskandr
body:
Closes #128.

## Summary

Real-data findings on a PRAD sample showed broadly-expressed surface proteins (CRIM1, HLA-F, IL6ST, FGFR1, NRP2) and housekeeping-like residuals (TBCE, NPM1, SON, DDX5, PCNP, HNRNPA1 variants) coming out as 85–99% \"tumor-attributed\" because the matched-normal + TME compartment fit couldn't absorb genes expressed across many HPA tissues — the residual defaulted into the tumor core.

A naive \"broadly expressed = never a target\" cap would also silently drop legitimate oncogenic targets (HER2 in HER2+ BRCA, MDM2 in WD/DD-LPS, GPC3 in HCC) whose targeting story is **amplification over baseline**, not baseline specificity.

This PR introduces two orthogonal per-gene gates and uses them together.

## The two gates

### 1. Tissue breadth — is this gene broadly expressed at baseline?

- Per-gene count of non-reproductive HPA tissues with nTPM ≥ 5 (HPA's detection convention).
- Peak-to-mean-of-top-N enrichment ratio < 3× so a gene strongly enriched in one tissue (KLK3 in prostate, NEUROD1 in brain, MS4A1 in B-cells) cannot trip the flag purely on low-level detection crossing many tissues.
- \`broadly_at_baseline = (n ≥ 15) AND (peak/mean_top_10 < 3×)\`.

### 2. Amplification — is this sample exhibiting above-healthy overexpression?

- \`amplification_fold = observed_tpm / max_healthy_tpm\`.
- \`amplified_over_healthy = amplification_fold ≥ 5×\`.
- When a sample exhibits amplification it IS a tumor-specificity signal regardless of HPA baseline breadth.

### Combined reader-facing flag

- \`broadly_expressed = broadly_at_baseline AND NOT amplified_over_healthy\`.
- Amplified-over-healthy genes render \`amplified N×\` in the Attribution cell and **do not get a reliability downgrade**.

## Threshold provenance

Every threshold is a module-level constant in \`plot_tumor_expr.py\` with a source comment. Tunable for tissue-specific contexts without forking call sites:

- \`HK_TISSUE_NTPM_THRESHOLD\` = 5.0 (HPA detection convention)
- \`BROAD_TISSUE_COUNT\` = 15 (30% of ~50 non-reproductive HPA tissues)
- \`BROADLY_ENRICHED_MAX_RATIO\` = 3.0
- \`BREADTH_BASELINE_TOP_N\` = 10
- \`AMPLIFICATION_MIN_FOLD\` = 5.0

## Curation takes precedence in the brief

The brief's top-3 therapy list iterates over the curated \`cancer-key-genes\` panel and deliberately does NOT filter on \`broadly_expressed\` — domain-validated targets like HER2 stay in the handoff regardless of HPA breadth. The generic Surface / Intracellular target tables (ranked by raw expression, not curation) do apply the filter via the confidence tier.

## Real-data smoke check

Classified 50+ rs-data genes through the refined gates (thresholds at module defaults):

| Class | Examples | Result |
|---|---|---|
| PRAD lineage / NEPC biomarkers | KLK3, KLK2, FOLH1, NKX3-1, HOXB13, ENO2, CHGA, ASCL1 | **clean** (tissue-restricted) |
| HK-like translation/splicing | TBCE, NPM1, RPS18, RPL5 | flagged (ext-HK + broadly-expr) or amplified depending on observed |
| Broad surface proteins | CRIM1, HLA-F, IL6ST, FGFR1, NRP2 | rendered as \`amplified N×\` because they're 6–15× above peak healthy in this sample — honest read |
| Non-amplified broad surface | CD74, HLA-B, CD44, CCND1, KRAS | \`broadly expr.\`, reliability low |
| Lymphoid lineage targets | MS4A1, CD19, CD33, CD274 | **clean** (strong tissue enrichment) |
| Cross-cancer oncogenic targets | MDM2 (5.3×), BRAF (5.2×) | amplified on this specific sample |

## Tests

- 15 new tests in \`tests/test_robust_attribution.py\` covering every branch of the classification, plus rendering and confidence-tier semantics.
- Full suite: **401 passed, 1 skipped.**

## Out of scope

- Per-cancer-type tuning of thresholds (noted above — consumers can override at module level; a dedicated parameter-overrides API can come later if needed).
- Replacing the TME-fold fallback when no decomposition runs (separate concern).

author: j3k0
body:
## Summary
Fixes #1692. Two bugs in `capacitor-plugin-cdv-purchase` when used with Capacitor 8:

- `@capacitor/core` peer is locked to `^6.0.0`, so `npm install` fails with ERESOLVE on Cap 7/8 apps.
- `Package.swift` is not in the `files` array of `capacitor/package.json`, so `npm publish` omits the SPM manifest. Cap 8 defaults to SPM, so `npx cap sync ios` warns `capacitor-plugin-cdv-purchase does not have a Package.swift` and the build breaks.

## Why CI missed it
The workflow ran `npm install $GITHUB_WORKSPACE/capacitor` (directory install). Directory installs ignore the `files` field and relax peer-dep resolution, so CI was exercising an artifact that did not match what `npm publish` ships.

## Plan
1. **This commit** — change CI to `npm pack` + install the resulting tarball. This should surface the two bugs on the Cap 8 matrix job (WIP: expect failure here to prove the repro).
2. Follow-up commits — widen peer deps, add `Package.swift` and `CapacitorPluginCdvPurchase.podspec` to the `files` array, remove the stale `ios/CapacitorPluginPurchase.podspec`.

## Test plan
- [ ] Confirm Cap 8 job fails on this commit with ERESOLVE or missing Package.swift
- [ ] After fix commits, all three Cap 6/7/8 matrix jobs pass
- [ ] Local repro (`capacitor-purchase-examples/subscriptions_v8`) succeeds after fixes

author: mobuchowski
body:
The `--consume-structured-logs` path was loading `manifest.json` eagerly the moment dbt's log file had any content — before dbt's parse phase finished writing a fresh manifest. This meant a leftover `target/manifest.json` from a prior invocation (different env vars, killed task, CI artifact cache) would silently poison all dataset identities for the entire run.

This PR fixes the root cause by removing the eager load entirely. For dbt ≥ 1.9, we instead subscribe to the `ArtifactWritten` structured log event (`artifact_type: WritableManifest`) and load the manifest exactly when dbt signals it just wrote a fresh one. For older dbt versions without that event, the manifest loads lazily on the first `NodeStart` handler call — which is inherently safe because dbt's parse phase, and therefore the manifest write, always completes before any node execution events are emitted.

As a third layer of defense, `compiled_manifest` now compares the file's modification time against the recorded process start time and logs a loud warning (skipping the load) if the manifest predates the current invocation by more than 2 seconds. This catches any future scenario where the ordering assumptions above break — such as `--no-write-json` being forced externally or dbt crashing mid-parse.

body:
## Economy Engine — New Organ for Mars-100

**The hoarding stat is no longer decorative.** Every colonist now has a wallet with abstract credits. Income, theft, taxation, inheritance, and inequality emerge from the same LisPy decision loop that drives all other behaviors.

### What mutated (T → T+1)

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/mars100/economy.py` | **NEW** — ColonyEconomy, Wallet, EconomySnapshot, tick_economy (~300 LOC) |
| `src/mars100/colonist.py` | Added `parent_ids` for lineage tracking; wealth in lispy bindings |
| `src/mars100/engine.py` | v3.0 — economy wired into tick loop after meta-awareness, before convergence |
| `src/mars100/__init__.py` | Economy exports added |
| `tests/test_economy.py` | **NEW** — 38 tests (wallet, income, theft, tax, Gini, inheritance, integration) |
| `tests/test_mars100.py` | Version assertion 2.0 → 3.0 |
| `docs/mars-100/index.html` | Full dashboard rewrite — 3-column layout with economy panel, Gini chart, wealth bars |
| `docs/mars-100/data.json` | Regenerated with economy data |

### Mechanics

- **Income**: productive actions earn credits scaled by relevant skill × hoarding retention
- **Theft**: sabotage targets least-trusted neighbor (via social graph), steals 15% of victim wealth
- **Taxes**: governance-dependent rates (anarchy=0%, dictator=20%, council=10%, custom rate support)
- **Treasury**: collected taxes fund resource improvements via spend_treasury()
- **Inheritance**: dead colonists pass wealth to lineage children (or treasury if no heirs)
- **Gini coefficient**: computed each year; inequality_crisis event fires when Gini > 0.6

### Simulation results (seed=42, 100 years)

```
Final Gini:    0.12 (low inequality — council taxation working)
Total theft:   1.53 cr
Total tax:     19.07 cr
Population:    20 alive (7 deaths, 17 births)
Sub-sims:      617
```

### Test results

```
10,852 passed in ~2 minutes (38 new economy tests + 10,814 existing)
```

### Design decisions

1. **Abstract credits, not literal resources** — avoids needing per-colonist resource inventory
2. **All economy state in ColonyEconomy** — single source of truth (no duplication on Colonist)
3. **Hoarding stat = retention multiplier** — high hoarders keep more of their income (0.6 + 0.4 × hoarding)
4. **Economy tick runs AFTER actions/births/deaths** but BEFORE convergence — wealth affects next year's decisions
5. **Conservation law enforced** — theft is zero-sum (thief gains = victim loses), taxes flow to treasury → resources

author: copilot
body:
The repository had stale schema assumptions that diverged from the real Supabase database, risking constraint violations and silent data bugs. This PR fixes the highest-priority mismatches only.

### Critical: itinerary `stayid` NOT NULL guard

Real schema enforces `itineraries.stayid UUID NOT NULL UNIQUE`. The repo was inserting `stayid: stayId ?? null`, which would fail at the DB level.

```typescript
// Before — violates NOT NULL constraint
.insert({ stayid: stayId ?? null, userid: userId })

// After — guard prevents insert without stayId, read-only fallback instead
if (!stayId) {
  console.warn('[itinerary] getOrCreateItinerary called without stayId — cannot insert');
  // fall back to read-only lookup by userid
  ...
  return fallback ? fallback.id : null;
}
```

`DbItinerary` and `DbItineraryItem` types updated to reflect real column nullability and missing fields (`title`, `status`, `source`, `endtime`, `titleoverride`, `notes`).

### Critical: stay status enum alignment

- Added `StayStatus` union type matching the real `staystatus` Postgres enum (`upcoming | active | completed | cancelled | confirmed | checked_in | checked_out`)
- `CustomerStay.status` typed as `StayStatus` instead of `string`
- `CurrentBookingView.getStatusConfig()` now handles all real enum values (previously missed `upcoming`, `checked_out`, `cancelled`)

### Booking reference clarification

Schema has both `bookingreference` (legacy VARCHAR) and `booking_reference` (active TEXT). All runtime code uses `booking_reference` exclusively. Documented in schema.ts; no code change needed.

### Schema docs rewrite (`schema.ts`)

Complete rewrite of the documentation-only schema file. Key corrections:
- `stays.status`: was `TEXT DEFAULT 'confirmed'` → now `staystatus NOT NULL DEFAULT 'upcoming'`
- `itineraries.stayid`: was nullable → now `NOT NULL UNIQUE`
- `property_rooms`: was `roomlabel, description, maxguests` → now `room_number, floor, room_type, bed_config, max_occupancy, status`
- `staff_profiles`: was email/name based → now `userid, propertyid, role, is_active`
- `stay_room_preferences` / `stay_breakfast_preferences`: was single `preference TEXT` → now structured boolean/text columns
- Added all Postgres enum type definitions

### Deferred (not in scope)

- Discover table TypeScript types (`DbDiscoverCategory`, `DbDiscoverItem`) still missing many real columns
- Phantom types in `database.ts` (`SavedItem`, `UserPreferences`, `CuratedCollection`) for tables not in schema
- `ItineraryContext` caller doesn't pass `stayId` yet — guard prevents bad inserts but creation is blocked until caller is updated
- Legacy `bookingreference` column still in DB (schema-side cleanup, not code)

author: yuga-hashimoto
body:
## Priority 1 — smart home device feel

Three production-log bugs surfaced on a real Japanese-locale tablet that had no explicit `TTS_LANGUAGE` pref set.

### Bug A — English polish reply on a Japanese tablet
- Utterance: 「宗像市の天気を教えて」 → TTS spoke: *"It is currently 16.3 degrees Celsius…"*
- Root cause: `VoicePipeline` read `PreferenceKeys.TTS_LANGUAGE` and passed the null tag straight through; `FastPathLlmPolisher.languageDirective` then hit the `else → "Respond in English."` branch.
- Fix: new top-level `resolveTtsLanguageTag()` falls back to `Locale.getDefault().toLanguageTag()` when the explicit pref is null/blank. Used on both the polish path (inside `polish()`) and the formatter path (in `VoicePipeline`). Instance method `polisher.resolveLanguageTag` shim keeps the constructor-injected supplier hook for tests.

### Bug B — "Laptop…" hallucination in the forecast reply
- Utterance: 「天気予報を教えて」 → TTS spoke: *"Laptop…"*
- Root cause: feeding a 2-day forecast JSON array to a 2B on-device model (Gemma 4 E2B) + an English directive ends up producing garbage mid-reply.
- Fix: new `FastPathResultFormatter.buildPolishSummary(toolName, data, tag)` emits short plain-text grounding facts — `Current: Munakata, 16.3°C, Clear, humidity 65%.` / `2026-04-18: min 12°C, max 18°C, Partly cloudy.` / `Abstract: …` / `Headlines: 1) …`. Polisher prompt now carries this summary instead of raw JSON and ends with an explicit "do not invent" directive. Same extraction regex as the existing `format()` path so grounding stays identical.

### Bug C — Web-search query leaks "について Web で検索して"
- Utterance: 「Google pixel 14について Web で検索して」 → DuckDuckGo returned 202 (empty) → polisher said *"I can search the web for information about…"*.
- Root cause 1: `WebSearchMatcher.japanesePatterns` accepted `(?:web\s*)?` but not the "で" particle, so the match failed on this STT form and nothing cleaned the capture group.
- Root cause 2: even when matched, the capture group still contained `について` / `に関して` / `Web で` filler.
- Fix: Japanese regex now tolerates `(?:web|ウェブ|ネット)\s*で?` between the topic connector and the search verb; new `cleanQuery()` helper strips trailing `について / に関して / を / Web で / 検索\* / ググ\* / 調べ\* / punctuation` repeatedly until stable.

## Files changed
- `app/src/main/java/com/opensmarthome/speaker/voice/pipeline/FastPathLlmPolisher.kt`
- `app/src/main/java/com/opensmarthome/speaker/voice/pipeline/FastPathResultFormatter.kt`
- `app/src/main/java/com/opensmarthome/speaker/voice/pipeline/VoicePipeline.kt`
- `app/src/main/java/com/opensmarthome/speaker/voice/fastpath/FastPathMatchers.kt`
- `app/src/test/java/com/opensmarthome/speaker/voice/pipeline/FastPathLlmPolisherTest.kt` (+8 tests)
- `app/src/test/java/com/opensmarthome/speaker/voice/pipeline/FastPathResultFormatterTest.kt` (+7 tests)
- `app/src/test/java/com/opensmarthome/speaker/voice/fastpath/WebSearchMatcherTest.kt` (+5 tests)

- [ ] Real-device smoke test on a JA tablet: 「宗像市の天気」 polish reply is Japanese
- [ ] Real-device smoke test: 「Google pixel 14について Web で検索して」 → DuckDuckGo gets query `"Google pixel 14"` only

body:
The bot runs silently idle with no observable signal rejections — no way to tell which filter stage is dropping all trades or whether the execution layer can physically reach the exchange.

## Signal Decision Pipeline (`nija_apex_strategy_v71.py`)
- `analyze_market` now returns `filter_stage: 'smart_filter' | 'market_filter' | 'no_entry'` on every `hold` path — eliminates fragile reason-string parsing upstream
- Filter-block log lines promoted from `DEBUG` → `INFO` so they're visible without `--debug`
- `_BYPASS_SMART_FILTER` responds to `NIJA_DEBUG_BYPASS_MODE` (env var re-read intentionally; importing from `trading_strategy` would create a circular dependency)

## Per-Signal Structured Logging (`trading_strategy.py`)
Every signal path — accepted or rejected — now emits a `WHY_NO_TRADE` record:
```
WHY_NO_TRADE | signal=42-BTC-USD | score=2.34 | regime=RANGING | capital=$127.50 | size=$12.00 | filters_failed=['apex_market_filter'] | decision=DROPPED
WHY_NO_TRADE | signal=42-SOL-USD | score=3.71 | regime=RANGING | capital=$127.50 | size=$15.00 | filters_failed=[]                     | decision=ACCEPTED
```
Helper defined once before the scan loop (not recreated per iteration).

## Per-Stage Filter Counters
`filter_stats` extended with `pre_apex_quality`, `pre_apex_readiness`, `pre_apex_structure`, `apex_smart_filter`, `apex_market_filter`, `apex_no_entry`. Routing uses `filter_stage` from `analyze_market`; falls back to reason-string matching for legacy paths.

## End-of-Cycle EXECUTION TRACE SUMMARY
```
── EXECUTION TRACE SUMMARY ─────────────────────────────
   apex_market_filter:       312  (68%)
   apex_smart_filter:         87  (19%)
   pre_apex_structure:        43  (9%)
🚧 PRIMARY BLOCKER: 'apex_market_filter' dropped 312 signal(s)
   → set NIJA_DISABLE_MARKET_FILTER=true to bypass (diagnostic only)
```
Uses a `_stage_bypass_var` mapping so the hint prints the real env var, not a generated name.

## Single Debug Bypass Mode
`NIJA_DEBUG_BYPASS_MODE=true` bypasses all non-critical gates in one flag:
- Pair quality, market readiness, market structure, smart filter, sniper/AI confidence, regime UNFAVORABLE, frequency-controller confidence nudge
- **CRISIS regime is never bypassed** — capital protection always wins
- Individual flags (`NIJA_BYPASS_QUALITY_FILTER`, `NIJA_BYPASS_READINESS_GATE`, etc.) still work for narrower one-at-a-time diagnosis

## Heartbeat Fallback
When no signals are queued, explicitly calls `_execute_heartbeat_trade()` if `HEARTBEAT_TRADE=true`:
- `HEARTBEAT TRADE FIRED` → execution layer reachable; strategy filters are the blocker
- Heartbeat also fails → problem is in the execution layer (broker auth / network / order API), not strategy

body:
### Motivation
- The existing before/after block was visually too large on desktop and had excessive outer padding, which wasted space.  
- The overlay image was being resized (width-based) during dragging and produced visual compression instead of a clean reveal.  
- The slider handle/divider needed to align exactly with the reveal boundary and support pointer/touch reliably.

### Description
- Reduced the block footprint by changing outer sizing classes: `max-w-5xl → max-w-3xl`, `mt-10 → mt-8`, and `p-4 sm:p-6 md:p-8 → p-3 sm:p-4 md:p-5`, and adjusted the aspect from `aspect-[16/10] → aspect-[16/9]`.  
- Reworked image layering to a true reveal: the base image is full-size and the overlay is also full-size but masked via `style={{ clipPath: \`inset(0 ${100 - position}% 0 0)\` }}` so only the visible portion changes instead of altering image width.  
- Kept both images using `fill` + `object-cover` to prevent distortion during interaction and swapped the image order to match the reveal logic.  
- Aligned the divider/handle precisely with the reveal boundary by positioning the handle container at `left: ${position}%` and centering it with `-translate-x-1/2`, preserving existing pointer event handling and keyboard support.

### Testing
- Ran `npm run lint` in the `aquadrop-landing` package and it completed with no ESLint warnings or errors.

- Provide a professional confirmation page that displays the persisted booking details after successful booking.
- Reuse existing frontend design system and UI components to keep the visual surface identical to the rest of the site.

### Description
- Introduced store API routes: `GET /store/booking-services` to list active services and `GET /store/bookings/:id` to fetch a booking with its service relation (backend files added under `backend/src/api/store/`).
- Registered middleware validation for the new `/store/booking-services` endpoint in `backend/src/api/middlewares.ts`.
- Added frontend data helpers `listStoreBookingServices` and `retrieveStoreBooking` in `frontend/src/lib/data/bookings.ts` to call the new store APIs.
- Replaced the static booking page with a dynamic flow by wiring `frontend/src/app/[countryCode]/(main)/booking/page.tsx` to a new `BookingFlow` component (`frontend/src/modules/booking/templates/booking-flow/index.tsx`), which implements service selection, calendar navigation, date selection, availability fetching, and a follow-up booking form for name/email/phone/notes.
- Added a confirmation route and template at `/[countryCode]/booking/confirmation` (`frontend/src/app/[countryCode]/(main)/booking/confirmation/page.tsx` and `frontend/src/modules/booking/templates/booking-confirmation/index.tsx`) that loads and displays booking details.

### Testing
- Ran `git diff --check` which reported no conflicts or whitespace errors.
- Ran `yarn lint` in `frontend` which failed due to an existing repository lint/config issue unrelated to this change (`@next/next/no-html-link-for-pages` path argument undefined), not introduced by these edits.
- Ran `yarn tsc --noEmit` in `frontend` which surfaced pre-existing TypeScript errors in unrelated files and therefore failed; the new files themselves are TypeScript/React-typed and compile locally but the repo contains unrelated type issues.

body:
## Summary

On `/get-a-quote` Step 5, the preferred-contact-method buttons now drive which field is required:

- **Phone** or **WhatsApp** selected → **phone** is required, email becomes optional.
- **Email** selected (default) → **email** stays required, phone stays optional.

This fixes a small UX snag where a user could select "contact me by phone" but still be forced to enter a valid email.

## What changed

`client/src/pages/GetAQuote.tsx`:

- `canProceed()` Step 5 branches on `contactMethod`. Phone is considered valid at >= 7 digits (ignoring spaces / `+` / parens).
- `touched` state extended from `{ name, email }` to `{ name, email, phone }` so phone errors only surface after blur/submit, matching name/email.
- `handleSubmit` marks phone touched too, so a failed submit surfaces the phone error.
- `Step5Contact`: derives `phonePreferred`, `emailRequired`, `phoneRequired` booleans from `value.contactMethod`. Errors only surface for the currently-required field.
- Layout: **"Preferred contact method"** buttons moved *above* the email/phone row so users know which field applies before filling, with a one-line hint underneath ("I'll reply by email ...", "I'll give you a call ...", "I'll WhatsApp you ..."). Field labels flip between `Email` / `Email (optional)` and `Phone` / `Phone (optional)` to match.
- Required-field asterisk switched from red (`text-red-500`) to teal (`#1DB48F`) and marked `aria-hidden` (the input's `required` attribute already conveys required-state to assistive tech).

## Test plan

- [ ] Step 5 with default "Email" selected: name + valid email required; phone labelled "Phone (optional)" and blank submits fine.
- [ ] Switch to "Phone": email label becomes "Email (optional)"; phone label becomes "Phone" with teal asterisk; submitting with a blank or too-short phone blocks with the "Please enter a valid phone number" error.
- [ ] Switch to "WhatsApp": same behaviour as Phone; hint text reads "I'll WhatsApp you ...".
- [ ] Switch back to "Email" after filling phone: email becomes required again, phone error clears.
- [ ] Name validation ( >= 2 chars ) still works in all three modes.
- [ ] Visual: asterisk is teal, not red.

body:
## Summary
- Implement `OPERATOR_COALESCE` in `sirius::gpu_expression_executor` using `cudf::replace_nulls` iteratively across children. First child is materialized (scalar lifted to a column), and each subsequent child replaces residual nulls — scalar replacements use the scalar overload, column replacements use the column overload. Result is wrapped via `materialize_as_ast_column` so COALESCE composes inside AST-capable parents.
- Expand `COMPARE_IN` numeric dispatch to cover INT8, UINT{8,16,32,64}, BOOL8, DECIMAL{32,64,128}, and TIMESTAMP_{D,S,MS,US,NS}. BOOL8 dispatches via `uint8_t` because `std::vector<bool>::data()` is deleted.
- Tighten a couple of AST-mode wraps in `gpu_execute_case.cpp` and `gpu_execute_function.cpp` so materialized children are registered as AST leaves consistently.

## Notes
- Short-circuit: children are materialized only if there are nulls in current result. `count_ast_ops` returns 0 for COALESCE, matching the materialize-only path.

## Test plan
- [x] `build/release/extension/sirius/test/cpp/sirius_unittest \"[expression_executor][experimental]\"` — 73 test cases / 3219 assertions pass.
- [x] New `TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE(\"experimental execute COALESCE\")` across `mat`, `ast_interpret`, `ast_jit` strategies covering:
  - col + scalar fallback fills every null
  - col + col leaves residual nulls where both are null
  - col + col + scalar chain fills every null
  - col + col + col leaves residual nulls where all three are null
- [x] New `TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE(\"experimental select COALESCE nested in predicate\")` — `COALESCE(col0, 0) > 20` exercises AST parent → materialized child handoff.
- [x] SQLLogicTests covering COALESCE end-to-end through the planner.

author: jsboige
body:
## Summary

Bumps `mcps/internal` submodule pointer from `48366b48` → `dd6fb078` to incorporate [jsboige-mcp-servers PR #123](https://github.com/jsboige/jsboige-mcp-servers/pull/123) which fixes an inputSchema asymmetry blocking nanoclaw restart for 3 days.

## Context

PR #1457 (parent, merged 2026-04-17 15:01Z) and PR #120 (submodule, merged 15:00Z) introduced v3 `mentions[]` / `crossPost[]` for `roosync_dashboard` (issue #1363). The Zod `DashboardArgsSchema` was updated correctly at runtime, but the JSON `inputSchema` advertised to MCP clients was not. Result: clients passing `mentions` or `crossPost` got `additionalProperties: false` rejections.

Both PRs were merged with **0 reviews, 0 comments, 24 seconds apart** — classic self-merge vibecoding pattern that PR #1464 (coordinator skeptical posture) was explicitly designed to prevent.

## What this PR does

- Bumps submodule pointer to include [PR #123](https://github.com/jsboige/jsboige-mcp-servers/pull/123) which adds `mentions` and `crossPost` properties to the `roosync_dashboard` inputSchema mirroring the existing Zod runtime schema.
- 5 commits included: #119 merge, #120 merge, #1410 ux-fixes (baseline discovery + stale decisions), #123 inputSchema fix.

## Review

PR #123 was reviewed by sk-agent critic (glm-5.1) before merge per CLAUDE.md rule #16:
- Schema correctness: fields and types match Zod reference
- XOR / conditional required: relies on Zod runtime enforcement (pragmatic — over-constraining JSON Schema would cause false rejections)
- Verdict: APPROVED, no breaking changes

## Impact

- Unblocks nanoclaw restart (3 days pending)
- Enables v3 mentions / crossPost dispatch from clients (notifications to other machines, cross-dashboard replication)
- No runtime behavior change (Zod already enforced; this just advertises the shape)

## Test plan

- [x] CI green on PR #123 (6/6 checks pass)
- [ ] Post-merge: Restart MCP server on ai-01, verify `roosync_dashboard` accepts `mentions[]` / `crossPost[]` without `additionalProperties` errors

body:
This pull request introduces the extraction of the  root CA certificate from a PEM bundle (if avaiable) and integrates it into the certificate request reconciliation process. It also updates the Go version used in CI workflows to 1.26.2. The most important changes are:

**Certificate Authority Extraction:**

* Added a new function `extractCAFromPEMBundle` in `internal/controllers/pem_chain.go` to scan a PEM bundle and return the root CA certificate, identified as a self-signed CA.
* Updated the `CertificateRequestReconciler` in `internal/controllers/certificaterequest_controller.go` to set the `Status.CA` field using the extracted root CA when a certificate is issued.
* Added comprehensive unit tests in `internal/controllers/pem_chain_test.go` to verify correct extraction of the root CA from various PEM bundle scenarios.

**This is a backport of PR #11702 as merged into main (314863e3a7f92d51fbeeeb27332a74a376440f8d).**

##### SUMMARY
If a CD-ROM device is placed in a position above number 3 (i.e. 4, 5...), booting from an ISO is not possible. This problem can be observed when provisioning VMs from built-in XenServer/XCP-ng VM templates that by default have no CD-ROM device attached. CD-ROM is later attached to the provisioned VM but only after all disks have been attached. If 4 or more disks are attached, CD-ROM ends up being pushed to a position above number 3 preventing the boot. This PR fixes this issue.

- CD-ROM handling code has been moved before disk handling code. This more closely mimics XenCenter/XCP-ng Center behavior. CD-ROM device, if added, will now grab position 3 before any disk grabs it.

author: singhharsh1708
body:
## Fix `FieldError` for Magnus/Linear integrators when `OrdinaryDiffEqDifferentiation` is loaded

**Fixes #3232**

### Problem

Solving a non-autonomous linear ODE with any Magnus integrator (e.g. `MagnusGL6`, `MagnusGL8`, `LieEuler`, `CG2`, etc.) crashes with a `FieldError` when `OrdinaryDiffEqDifferentiation` is loaded (which happens automatically via `DifferentialEquations.jl`):

```
FieldError: type OrdinaryDiffEqLinear.MagnusGL6 has no field `autodiff`,
available fields: `krylov`, `m`, `iop`
```

### Root Cause

`MagnusGL6 <: OrdinaryDiffEqLinearExponentialAlgorithm <: OrdinaryDiffEqExponentialAlgorithm{0, false, ...}`

In `OrdinaryDiffEqDifferentiation/src/alg_utils.jl`, the generic dispatch:

```julia
function _alg_autodiff(alg::Union{
        OrdinaryDiffEqExponentialAlgorithm{CS, AD},
        OrdinaryDiffEqAdaptiveExponentialAlgorithm{CS, AD},
    }) where {CS, AD}
    return alg.autodiff  # ← crashes: Magnus types have no autodiff field
end
```

catches all `OrdinaryDiffEqLinearExponentialAlgorithm` subtypes because they inherit from `OrdinaryDiffEqExponentialAlgorithm{0, false, ...}`. These algorithms are matrix-exponential methods that never use ForwardDiff/FiniteDiff — they only have fields `krylov`, `m`, and `iop`.

### Fix

Add a more-specific `_alg_autodiff` override that intercepts `OrdinaryDiffEqLinearExponentialAlgorithm` before the generic `ExponentialAlgorithm` dispatch:

```julia
function _alg_autodiff(::OrdinaryDiffEqLinearExponentialAlgorithm)
    return Val{false}()
end
```

This is consistent with how `OrdinaryDiffEqCore` already handles these types in `prepare_alg` and `has_autodiff`.

### Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `OrdinaryDiffEqDifferentiation.jl` | Import `OrdinaryDiffEqLinearExponentialAlgorithm` from Core |
| `alg_utils.jl` | Add `_alg_autodiff` override returning `Val{false}()` |
| `differentiation_traits_tests.jl` | Regression test verifying `_alg_autodiff`, `prepare_alg`, and `forwarddiffs_model` |

### Testing

All 3 regression assertions pass with clean precompilation:
```
✓ _alg_autodiff returns Val{false}()
✓ prepare_alg returns alg unchanged  
✓ forwarddiffs_model returns false
```

body:
## Fixes #68065

`sessions_send` with a non-zero timeout previously returned `status=timeout` whenever the wait window expired, even when the target agent had already accepted the message and produced a reply after the window closed.

### Behavior contract

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Reply arrives *just after* the timeout window | `status: "timeout"` | `status: "ok"` with the late reply |
| Run accepted but no new reply within window | `status: "timeout"` | `status: "accepted"` |
| Run truly stalled / not accepted | `status: "timeout"` | `status: "timeout"` (unchanged) |
| Fire-and-forget (`timeoutSeconds: 0`) | `status: "accepted"` | `status: "accepted"` (unchanged) |

### Implementation

Adds `compensateAfterWaitTimeout()` in `src/agents/run-wait.ts` that reads the latest assistant reply snapshot after a timeout and checks whether a new reply materialized since the pre-send baseline. The timeout handler in `sessions-send-tool.ts` now calls this before returning a hard timeout.

### Test coverage

- **`src/agents/run-wait.test.ts`** — 3 new tests in a `compensateAfterWaitTimeout` describe block:
  - new reply found after timeout → returns `accepted` with reply
  - no new reply but run accepted → returns `accepted` without reply
  - compensation itself fails → falls back to hard timeout
- **`src/agents/tools/sessions.test.ts`** — 1 new test: fire-and-forget (`timeoutSeconds=0`) stays on the `accepted` path without triggering compensation or `agent.wait`
- All 42 tests in the targeted test files pass (16 in run-wait, 26 in sessions)

### Production provenance

We have been running this fix as a dist-level patch in production. This PR is the source-level equivalent, adapted to the current upstream main branch. Reference third-party implementation: wade-microblueworld/openclaw@bfe3a59

### Note on full test suite

The full `pnpm test` run has 2 pre-existing failures on upstream `main` that are unrelated to this change (`src/plugins/bundle-commands.test.ts`, `src/commands/gateway-status/helpers.test.ts`). All files touched by this PR pass cleanly.

- Behavior or issue addressed: `sessions_send` post-timeout compensation should preserve canonical delivery metadata and should expose compensation read failures instead of hiding them behind a generic timeout.
- Real environment tested: Local macOS source worktree `/tmp/openclaw-pr68196`, Node v25.8.1, branch `fix/sessions-send-timeout-compensation`, commit `37c9ac3c48a`.

- Observed result after fix: The regression coverage now verifies that accepted timeout compensation keeps `delivery: { status: "pending", mode: "announce" }`, skipped compensation keeps skipped announce metadata, and terminal timeout errors include the compensation read failure text.
- What was not tested: Live Telegram or Feishu channel delivery was not exercised for this PR because the changed behavior is the `sessions_send` tool result/compensation contract.

- Behavior or issue addressed: `sessions_send` should not report a hard send failure when the first `agent.wait` times out but the nested agent run has already been accepted and can still produce a reply. The caller should get either the late reply or an accepted/pending delivery state instead of a misleading failure.

author: revision-co-ltd
body:
## Summary

When `requireMention: true` is set on a LINE group, text messages are correctly gated by `resolveInboundMentionDecision`, but non-text messages (image, sticker, video, audio, file, location) always bypass the gate via `canDetectMention: message.type === "text"`. The LINE Messaging API never delivers `mention.mentionees` on non-text messages, so a bot cannot be @-mentioned on an image in a group, yet the handler still calls `processMessage` for every piece of unaddressed media. In busy groups this leads to the agent processing large volumes of images/stickers/videos that were never directed at it.

This PR adds an opt-in `requireMentionForNonText?: boolean` to `LineGroupConfig` (default `false`). When enabled, non-text messages participate in the same mention gate as text, and because LINE does not expose a native bot mention on those messages they are skipped under `requireMention` — matching how WhatsApp/Telegram/Discord/Slack groups behave: unaddressed media does not trigger a reply.

Because the default is `false`, the historical fail-open behavior is fully preserved. The existing test ``allows non-text group messages through when requireMention is set (cannot detect mention)`` continues to pass unchanged.

## Why an opt-in and not a default change

Flipping the default would be a behavior change for every deployment that currently relies on non-text group media reaching the bot (e.g. groups that send images for the agent to analyze without explicit @-mention). Keeping it opt-in preserves that flow while giving operators a one-line knob to bring LINE in line with other channels.

## Example config

\`\`\`jsonc
{
  "channels": {
    "line": {
      "accounts": {
        "default": {
          "groups": {
            "G0123456789abcdef": {
              "requireMention": true,
              "requireMentionForNonText": true
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
\`\`\`

body:
Fixes #4131. Separate issue #4139 was filed for the pre-existing scoping bug on the Occurrence Map link — out of scope here.

## Summary
- Single-observation popup is now a Bootstrap `.media` layout: thumbnail on the left; species name (bold italic for non-deprecated, italic-only for deprecated), observed date, `Confidence: NN%`, location link, small muted coordinates on the right. The observation link opens in a new tab (`target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"`).
- Multi-observation popup: `"N Observations [Show All] [Map All]"` — count first, two small buttons, extra breathing room before the first taxon link. Up to three most-recent taxon links, `…` if more, no date/confidence.
- Marker color now communicates consensus: blue for groups / location-only; green (≥ 80%), orange (0 < x < 80%), red (≤ 0%) for singles. Rectangles share the same palette.
- A bounding box that would render sub-pixel (< 15×15 px) at the current zoom is swapped for a same-color square marker — otherwise it disappeared entirely on world-zoom maps.
- Google Maps InfoWindow chrome tightened (`.gm-style-iw-c`, `-d`, `-chr`) so the close-X sits in the corner and the popup has no dead top space.

## Implementation
- **`Mappable::MapSet`**: `compute_color` picks blue vs traffic-light using `Vote.percent(vote_cache)`; `single_observation?` counts observations, not all objects (fixes the "blue markers everywhere" bug where a single obs bucketed with its own location passed `@objects.size == 2` and was mis-colored).
- **`Mappable::MinimalObservation`**: new optional attrs `name_id`, `text_name`, `display_name`, `when`, `vote_cache`, `thumb_image_id`.
- **`Observations::MapsController`**: selects the new columns; bulk-loads `text_name` + `display_name` from `Name` (alongside the existing bulk location load) — no N+1.
- **`map_controller.js`**: per-marker color via `colored_circle_icon`; rectangles via `strokeColor`; overlay construction deferred to the first map `idle` event so `map.getProjection()` is available for the pixel-size check; `rectangleTooSmall(bounds)` falls back to `colored_square_icon`.
- **`MapHelper`** and **`Components::Map`**: parallel popup rebuilds so every map surface (obs index, obs show, location show, name distribution, herbarium, project maps) gets the new layout.
- **`_maps.scss`**: InfoWindow chrome overrides, thumbnail edge-stripping (`text-decoration`, `border`, `outline`, `box-shadow` all zeroed with `!important` because the iw stylesheet loads after ours), button spacing + focus-visible handling.

## Tests
- 8 `MapSet#compute_color` cases covering each color band, 80% and 0% boundaries, group/location-only fallback, and the regression where a single obs bucketed with its location was mis-colored.
- Map component tests assert popup carries color + name + date + confidence (plain `Confidence: NN%`, no pill/dot), `target="_blank"` + `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, most-recent-first ordering in groups, `…` overflow beyond 3.
- Existing controller and class tests still pass.

author: copilot
body:
In `fastmcp>=3.2.0`, `ToolTask.result` is `async def result(self)`, not an attribute. The three call sites in `MCPToolManager.call_tool` used bare attribute access, capturing the bound coroutine method instead of the `CallToolResult`. `_normalize_mcp_tool_result` then found no `content`/`structured_content`/`data` on a method object and returned an empty payload — surfacing as null tool output in the UI for any tool using the ToolTask path.

### Changes

- **`atlas/modules/mcp_tools/client.py`** — `tool_task.result` → `await tool_task.result()` at all three call sites (immediate return, first wait, post-polling wait)
- **`atlas/tests/test_adaptive_task_polling.py`** — `mock_task.result = mock_result` → `mock_task.result = AsyncMock(return_value=mock_result)` so mocks model the real coroutine contract; bare attribute access would now fail the tests
- **`CHANGELOG.md`** — Added entry

```python
# Before (captures bound method, not the result)
result = tool_task.result

# After (awaits the coroutine, gets CallToolResult)
result = await tool_task.result()
```

author: darwinboersma
body:
## Summary

Adds an optional `pre_install_command` input to the `publish-npm-package` reusable workflow. Runs after checkout + JFrog auth but before `yarn install --immutable`, at the **repo root** (not `working_directory`).

Enables fully ephemeral codegen workflows — provider repos can generate a typed client package from their OpenAPI spec at build time without committing any generated code to git.

## Use case

```yaml
uses: tetrascience/ts-ci-cd-lib/.github/workflows/publish-npm-package.yml@main
with:
  working_directory: client
  pre_install_command: "yarn install && npx generate-service-client"
  prerelease_tag: alpha
secrets:
  AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.JFROG_ARTIFACTORY_WRITE_NPM_AUTH }}
  REGISTRY: ${{ secrets.JFROG_ARTIFACTORY_NPM_VIRTUAL_URL }}
  PUBLISH_REGISTRY: ${{ secrets.JFROG_ARTIFACTORY_WRITE_NPM_URL }}
```

The `pre_install_command` step:
1. Runs `yarn install` at the repo root (installs `@tetrascience-npm/request` which ships `generate-service-client`)
2. Runs `npx generate-service-client` which reads `serviceClient` config from the root `package.json` and produces `client/` with `package.json`, `yarn.lock`, and generated TypeScript

Then the normal workflow takes over: `yarn install --immutable` (in `client/`), `yarn build`, publish.

## Changes

- **`publish-npm-package.yml`**: new `pre_install_command` input (string, default `""`, optional). Runs in a step with `working-directory: "."` so it always executes at repo root regardless of `working_directory` input.
- **`README.md`**: documented in the inputs table.

Backwards-compatible — defaults to empty string (step is skipped via `if`).

## Test plan

- [x] Existing callers unaffected (no input = no step)
- [x] New input documented in README

author: alberts
body:
## What changed
This updates MicMaxer so selected microphones are tracked more reliably across device hot-plugging, default-input changes, and live volume changes. The app now refreshes device state dynamically, preserves selected devices even when they are temporarily disconnected, and keeps live volume listeners synchronized with the currently selected connected microphones.

It also refactors tray and timing dependencies behind small interfaces so the startup, menu, and periodic-maintenance paths can be tested without talking to the real systray implementation or a real ticker.

## Why
Over time the app could stop re-maxing a microphone until restart, and it handled devices being added, removed, or reselected poorly. The root cause was that listener registration and device discovery were too static: they were tied to startup assumptions and not refreshed robustly as the system audio topology changed.

## Impact
Selected microphones now recover more cleanly when devices are unplugged and reattached, and live event-driven resets apply to all selected connected microphones instead of only the active default input. The tray menu also stays in sync with the current device set.

## Validation

author: markdav-is
body:
## Summary

This PR introduces **Proof of Life**, a complete .NET 10 Aspire-based system for tracking who has logged into Microsoft Teams or used M365 today, broken down by department. Managers can view their full org-chart subtree, and external systems can report presence via a simple REST API.

## Key Changes

### Core Application
- **ProofOfLife.Api** — ASP.NET Core backend with:
  - Real-time Microsoft Graph Change Notifications for Teams presence (webhook-based, ~seconds latency)
  - Backstop polling every 30 minutes to catch missed notifications
  - In-memory presence store with department/org-chart enrichment
  - REST endpoints for querying presence and recording external signals
  - API key + JWT authentication

- **ProofOfLife.Web** — Blazor Server frontend with:
  - Department dashboard showing daily presence summary
  - Manager org-chart view (recursive) with presence indicators
  - Azure AD / MSAL authentication
  - Real-time refresh capability

- **ProofOfLife.Bot** — Silent Teams bot that:
  - Records any Teams activity as proof of life
  - Never responds to users; purely observational

- **ProofOfLife.ServiceDefaults** — Shared OpenTelemetry, health checks, and service discovery for Aspire

### Infrastructure & Deployment
- **Terraform** modules for Azure:
  - AKS cluster with Workload Identity
  - Azure Container Registry
  - Azure AD app registrations (API, Web, Bot)
  - Key Vault for secrets
  - Virtual networking with pod subnets
  
- **Kubernetes manifests** for:
  - Deployments (API, Web, Bot) with 2 replicas and rolling updates
  - Services, Ingress (NGINX + cert-manager)
  - ConfigMaps and Secrets
  - Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (API: 2–10 replicas, 70% CPU target)
  - RBAC (ServiceAccount, ClusterRole)

### Presence Detection Scripts
- **LoginEventDetector.ps1** — Windows Event Log watcher (Event ID 4624/4648) that reports logons to the API
- **OfficeActivityHook.ps1** — WMI process monitor for Office app launches (Word, Excel, Teams, etc.)
- **Install-LoginDetector.ps1** — Task Scheduler installer for the login detector

### Build & Deployment Automation
- **build-and-push.sh** — Docker image build and ACR push
- **deploy.sh** — Kubernetes deployment with image substitution
- **package-bot-manifest.sh** — Teams app manifest packaging
- **terraform-init.sh** — Remote state bootstrap

## Notable Implementation Details

1. **Graph Subscriptions** — `GraphSubscriptionService` manages per-user presence subscriptions with:
   - Batch creation (50 at a time) to avoid throttling
   - Automatic renewal 5 minutes before expiry (58-minute lifetime)
   - Full sync every hour to catch new users and clean stale entries
   - Lifecycle event handling (reauthorizationRequired, subscriptionRemoved)

2. **Webhook Security** — Graph notifications validated via `clientState` HMAC; subscription IDs verified against known set before processing

3. **Presence Enrichment** — User cache populated during sync stores display name, department, job title, and manager ID for webhook notifications

4. **Multi-Signal Detection**:
   - Real-time Teams presence via Graph webhooks
   - Windows login events via PowerShell
   - Office app launches via WMI
   - External API for custom signals

5. **Manager Org View** — Recursive component renders full downstream org-chart with presence indicators; uses Graph delegated permissions (User.Read, Directory.Read.All)

6. **Aspire Orchestration** — AppHost coordinates API + Web in development with service discovery and environment variable injection

## Documentation
- Comprehensive README with architecture diagram, quick-start guide, Azure AD setup, user secrets, and deployment instructions
- Inline code comments for complex services (subscriptions, webhooks, polling)
- Terraform variable validation and output exports
- Teams bot manifest template with deployment notes

body:
Same team number can be registered under multiple programs (e.g. 252A in both VRC and VEXIQ). Keying favorites by teamNumber alone caused the second program to be silently rejected on add, removed both on remove, and lit the heart on the wrong program's team page.

Switch the favorites key to (teamNumber, matchType) and update all four call sites (search results, team detail, compare, favorites) to pass matchType. The favorites page now also matches each saved entry to the fresh row of the same matchType, so 252A favorited as VEXIQ no longer displays as the VRC variant just because /api/teams returns both rows.

author: jaayslaughter-cpu
body:
# PR #336 — MLB Stats API Layer

## Problem
FanGraphs API is 403-blocked on Railway (PR #335 added pybaseball fallback, but pybaseball also requires periodic manual cache seeding). Neither source self-updates through the season — pitcher K% in April is wrong by June if the Postgres cache isn't manually refreshed.

## Solution
New `mlb_stats_layer.py` — automatic, self-healing, season-long pitcher + batter stats via `statsapi.mlb.com` (Railway-confirmed reachable). Fetches every DataHub cycle, caches to Postgres + disk so Railway restarts are instant.

## Files Changed

### `mlb_stats_layer.py` *(new — 664 lines)*
- Fetches today's probable starters from `/api/v1/schedule?hydrate=probablePitcher,lineups`
- Per pitcher: `/api/v1/people/{id}?hydrate=stats(group=pitching,type=season,season=2026)` → ERA, WHIP, K%, BB%, FIP, xFIP proxy, SIERA proxy, CSW% proxy, SwStr% proxy
- Per confirmed lineup batter: same endpoint with `group=hitting` → AVG, OBP, SLG, ISO, BABIP, wOBA proxy, wRC+ proxy, K%, BB%
- 3-tier cache: in-memory → disk (`/tmp/propiq_mlbstats_cache_{date}.json`) → Postgres `fg_cache` table
- Cache key is **date-stamped** — auto-refreshes every morning through the whole season with zero manual intervention
- Public interface: `get_pitcher(name)`, `get_batter(name)` — identical signatures to `fangraphs_layer`

### `fangraphs_layer.py` *(modified — delegation chain)*
`get_pitcher()` and `get_batter()` now:
1. Try `mlb_stats_layer` first (Railway-safe, always fresh)
2. Fall back to FanGraphs cache (populated if FanGraphs ever un-403s)
3. Return `{}` → agents use `LEAGUE_DEFAULTS` as before

Zero agent changes required.

### `tasklets.py` *(modified — 10 lines in DataHub)*
`run_data_hub_tasklet()` now calls `mlb_stats_layer.warm_cache(hub)` before the FanGraphs pre-warm. Passes the hub dict so the stats layer reuses already-fetched starter/lineup lists — no duplicate schedule calls.

### `requirements.txt`
No new dependencies — `requests` already present. `pybaseball>=2.2.7` retained from PR #335 as 4th-tier fallback.

## Expected Log Output (first boot after deploy)
```
[MLBStats] Schedule: 14 probable starters, 180 confirmed batters
[MLBStats] Loaded 14 pitchers  180 batters for 2026-04-18 (via statsapi.mlb.com)
[MLBStats] Postgres cache saved (2026-04-18)
[DataHub] MLB Stats API cache warm.
```

Subsequent restarts same day:
```
[MLBStats] Loaded 14 pitchers 180 batters for 2026-04-18 (Postgres cache)
```

## Metric proxies (explicit in code — upgradeable without interface change)
| Slot | Proxy used | Correlation |
|------|-----------|-------------|
| `csw_pct` | `k_pct` | ~0.85 |
| `swstr_pct` | `k_pct * 0.52` | regression constant |
| `xfip` | `fip` | HR regressed to avg — identical early season |
| `siera` | `fip` | best without strand-rate |
| `wrc_plus` | derived from SLG+OBP+league context | directional |

## No Breaking Changes
- All 17 agents call `fangraphs_layer.get_pitcher()` / `get_batter()` — unchanged
- League defaults unchanged
- Postgres schema unchanged (uses existing `fg_cache` table)
- Redis hub structure unchanged

## Closes
Supersedes pybaseball-only fallback from PR #335 for daily-accuracy pitcher stats.

<!-- This is an auto-generated description by cubic. -->

## Summary by cubic
Add a self-updating MLB Stats API layer that pulls daily pitcher and batter stats from statsapi.mlb.com and caches them across memory, disk, and Postgres. Agents now get fresh, Railway-safe stats with no manual seeding or code changes.

- **New Features**
  - New `mlb_stats_layer.py` fetches probable starters and confirmed lineup batters, then per-player season stats via `/people`; computes proxies for CSW%, SwStr%, xFIP, SIERA, and wRC+; cache keys are date-stamped for daily refresh.

body:
## Summary

- **Fixed immediate failure**: `pulumi/actions` was invoked with `command: version` which is invalid — the deploy workflow correctly omits the command parameter to just install the CLI
- **Added full resource cleanup**: Teardown now deletes Wrangler-deployed Workers (API + Tail) and the AI Gateway, which were created outside Pulumi and never cleaned up
- **Added environment selector**: Can now tear down staging or production (was hardcoded to production only)
- **Fixed keep_data logic**: Properly enumerates Pulumi resource URNs and excludes D1 databases, instead of fragile wildcard URN matching

## What was wrong

The error from the logs:
```
Error: Input was not correct for command. Valid alternatives are: up, update, refresh, destroy, preview, output
```

This was caused by line 52-54 in the old workflow:
```yaml
- name: Install Pulumi CLI
  uses: pulumi/actions@v6.6.1
  with:
    command: version  # <-- not a valid command
```

The deploy-reusable.yml correctly uses the action without a command (which just installs the CLI).

Beyond the immediate fix, the teardown was incomplete. The deploy pipeline creates these resources outside Pulumi:
- **API Worker** (`sam-api-prod`) — deployed by `wrangler deploy`
- **Tail Worker** (`sam-tail-worker-prod`) — deployed by `wrangler deploy`  
- **AI Gateway** — created by `configure-ai-gateway.sh` via Cloudflare API

None of these were cleaned up by `pulumi destroy`.

## Test plan

- [ ] Trigger teardown workflow on staging with `DELETE` confirmation — verify it completes without errors
- [ ] Verify all Cloudflare resources are removed (Workers, D1, KV, R2, DNS, Pages, AI Gateway)
- [ ] Re-deploy staging to confirm a fresh deploy works after full teardown
- [ ] Test `keep_data: true` option preserves D1 databases while removing everything else

## Agent Preflight

- **Change classification**: `infra-change`
- **Impact analysis**: Teardown is manual-only (`workflow_dispatch`), no risk to automated deploys
- **Constitution check**: Resource names derived from `RESOURCE_PREFIX` env var (configurable, not hardcoded)

## Staging Verification

N/A — this is a workflow file change. The workflow itself is the verification (must be triggered manually via GitHub Actions UI). Cannot be tested via Playwright against the live app.

body:
This pull request introduces several important updates to the project's developer documentation, CI workflows, and configuration files. The main focus is on modernizing the CI environment (Node.js and GitHub Actions), improving the release and publishing process (especially for browser extensions), and providing thorough documentation for contributors and maintainers. Notably, it adds a new workflow for Chrome OAuth token renewal, updates the Chrome publishing guide, and removes the legacy ESLint configuration.

**CI/CD and Build Process Modernization**

- **Node.js and GitHub Actions Upgrades:**  
  - All workflows now use Node.js 24.x and the latest stable versions of `actions/checkout` and `actions/setup-node` for improved security and compatibility.  
  - Updated the SonarQube scan action to v7.1.0 for better code analysis.  
  [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-bc668a2c9f2299cef15b222055b4b4d5311646caec2e7610e540cee18ae9b948L14-R19) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-232ead425069ad86b523a739aa18b77f9088cd61a4b40c6a374d9774ff78cfc8R10-R22) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-5895707186d21bd3672c2faf7743c1cd2d656de088cdec80dc676ed8e3f22bceL14-R18)

- **Release and Publishing Workflow Improvements:**  
  - The publishing workflow now combines browser extension publishing steps into a single `Publish Extensions` step, using a unified secrets structure for Chrome, Firefox, and Edge, simplifying maintenance and reducing duplication.  
  - Upgraded the release action to v1.21.0 for both draft and official releases.  
  [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-232ead425069ad86b523a739aa18b77f9088cd61a4b40c6a374d9774ff78cfc8L37-R39) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-232ead425069ad86b523a739aa18b77f9088cd61a4b40c6a374d9774ff78cfc8L46-R69) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-bc668a2c9f2299cef15b222055b4b4d5311646caec2e7610e540cee18ae9b948L37-R37)

**Documentation Enhancements**

- **New and Updated Contributor Docs:**  
  - Added `AGENTS.md`, a comprehensive architecture and onboarding guide for the extension, including file structure, data flow, and contribution conventions.  
 
  - Revamped `docs/chrome-refresh-token-setup.md` to document the new official method for managing Chrome Web Store OAuth tokens via GitHub Actions, reflecting recent Google policy changes and the new workflow.  
 

- **New Chrome OAuth Token Renewal Workflow:**  
  - Introduced `.github/workflows/renew-chrome-token.yml` to automate checking, renewing, and updating the Chrome Web Store refresh token, including notification and secret management.  
 

**Configuration and Miscellaneous**

- **ESLint Configuration Cleanup:**  
  - Removed the legacy `.eslintrc.json` file, possibly in favor of a new linting setup.  
 

- **VSCode Settings Update:**  
  - Added terminal command auto-approval settings to `.vscode/settings.json` for a smoother development experience.  
 

These changes collectively improve maintainability, developer onboarding, and the reliability of the extension's publishing process.

## Summary
Five fixes from a static security review targeting the HTTP transport, federation protocol, and search query sanitizer:

- **Slowloris mitigation**: add `ReadTimeout` (60s) and `WriteTimeout` (120s) to all HTTP listeners
- **announce_peer URL validation**: reject non-http/https endpoint schemes
- **Vector clock size cap**: `MergeCapped` rejects merges exceeding 256 entries to prevent clock inflation attacks
- **FTS5 unbalanced quote safety**: strip all quotes when count is odd, preventing syntax errors that leak raw queries

Also includes a 24-scenario security pentest playbook for runtime testing.

body:
## Shadow Review — PR `#2853` v1

**Source:** `DataDog/dd-sdk-ios#2853`
**Commit:** `228c6aaf4ddf94524a5b97d6f7e9414b0c26b17b`
**Timestamp:** 2026-04-17T16:34:11Z

---

## Original PR Description

### What and why?

Introduces the `SpanSnapshot` value type and wires a notification hook into the span finish lifecycle. This is the second building block for client-side stats (CSS): it captures lightweight, immutable span data needed for stats computation before the sampling decision, ensuring all spans (including sampled-out ones) contribute to accurate metrics.

### How?

- **`SpanSnapshot`**: New `Sendable` + `Encodable` struct capturing span fields relevant to stats: service, resource, operation, duration, error, span kind, top-level, measured, peer tags, and service source. Also introduces a `Nanoseconds` typealias for clarity.
- **`DDSpan.createSnapshot()`**: Private method called in `finish()` before the sampling check. Resolves service/resource/operation using the same `SpanTagsReducer` logic as `SpanEventBuilder`.
- **`DatadogTracer.onSpanFinished`**: Optional callback property (not stored per-span). Set once during `Trace.enableOrThrow()` when stats is enabled; writes snapshots to the `ClientStatsFeature` scope.
- **16 unit tests** covering snapshot creation, tag extraction, peer tags, service source, sampling-independent capture, and callback wiring.

author: gustavscirulis
body:
### Why?

When AI analysis fails (wrong API key, exceeded credits, rate limit), the error is silently stored but the user only sees a generic "Analysis failed" label. Users need to see the actual error to diagnose and fix the issue. Additionally, batch analysis keeps running after the first failure, wasting API calls that will also fail.

### How?

Added an `analysisAlertError` property to `ImportService` (Mac) and `AnalysisCoordinator` (iOS) that drives a native `.alert()` with a human-readable message based on the HTTP status code. All batch analysis loops now break on first failure, so remaining items stay unanalyzed until the user explicitly retries.

<details>
<summary>Implementation Plan</summary>

# Plan: Surface AI analysis error messages via alert + stop batch on failure

## Context

When AI analysis fails (wrong API key, exceeded credits, rate limit), the error is captured and stored on `MediaItem.analysisError` but the user only sees a generic "Analysis failed" label. Additionally, batch analysis keeps running after the first failure, wasting API calls that will also fail. The user needs to see the actual server error in an alert, and batch analysis should stop on first failure.

## Approach

1. Add an `analysisAlertError: String?` property to `ImportService` (Mac) and `AnalysisCoordinator` (iOS)
2. Set it on failure, clear it when starting a new analysis attempt
3. Break batch loops on first failure
4. Wire a `.alert()` modifier in `ContentView` (Mac) and `MainView` (iOS) bound to this property
5. Keep existing inline "Analysis failed" labels — they mark which items failed

## Files to modify

### Mac app

**`SnapGrid/SnapGrid/Services/ImportService.swift`**
- Add `var analysisAlertError: String?` property
- Change `analyzeItem` → `@discardableResult func analyzeItem(...) async -> Bool`
  - Clear `analysisAlertError` at start
  - Return `false` and set `analysisAlertError` in catch block
  - Return `true` on success
- In `analyzeUnanalyzedItems`: break loop when `analyzeItem` returns `false`

**`SnapGrid/SnapGrid/Views/ContentView/ContentView.swift`**
- Add `.alert("Analysis Failed", ...)` modifier bound to `importService.analysisAlertError`
- Fix SyncWatcher callback loop (line ~300-308) to break on first failure
- Fix `retryAnalysis` (line ~796) to run sequentially in one Task and break on failure

### iOS app

**`ios/SnapGrid/SnapGrid/Services/AnalysisCoordinator.swift`**
- Add `var analysisAlertError: String?` property
- Clear it at start of `analyzeItems` loop
- Set it in catch block and `break` to stop the batch

**`ios/SnapGrid/SnapGrid/Views/Main/MainView.swift`**
- Add `.alert("Analysis Failed", ...)` modifier bound to `analysisCoordinator.analysisAlertError`

## Verification

1. Mac: Set an intentionally wrong API key, import an image → alert should show the server error (e.g., "API error (401): ...")
2. Mac: Import multiple images with wrong key → only the first should attempt analysis, rest remain unanalyzed (no error flag set)
3. Mac: Fix key, press retry → analysis succeeds, alert doesn't appear
4. iOS: Same flow via AnalysisCoordinator
5. Build both apps to verify no compile errors

</details>

author: hariyenuganti
body:
## Summary

A user-submitted role with a long paragraph-style description (no artificial
line breaks) visibly overflowed the job-details container to the right. The
description text extended past the cover image's rounded corner and bled off
the container.

## Root cause

`.job-info__right` sits inside a flex container but had no width constraint
and no `min-width: 0`. By default, flex children refuse to shrink below
their intrinsic content width — which is fine for short content, but a long
paragraph pushed the flex child to match the paragraph's natural width and
overflowed the parent.

The seeded dataset all had short, tidy descriptions, so this was latent.
The first real user submission surfaced it.

## Fix

```css
.job-info__right {
  flex: 1;        /* take all remaining space */
  min-width: 0;   /* allow shrinking below intrinsic content width */
  padding-right: 42px;
}

.job-info__description {
  overflow-wrap: anywhere;   /* break unusually long tokens */
  white-space: pre-wrap;     /* preserve user-typed line breaks */
}
```

## Test plan

- [x] Seeded a reproduction job with the exact overflowing description
- [x] Confirmed `.job-info__right` width constrained to 523px (vs unbounded before)
- [x] Description wraps naturally inside the cover-image-width boundary
- [x] Bonus: pasting a multi-paragraph description now preserves line breaks

author: shortbird
body:
## Summary
- Primary: evidence/moment/task uploads now go direct-to-Supabase via signed URL instead of multipart-through-backend. Fixes the 142MB worker memory overflow seen in prod (v1 Safari hit `/api/evidence/documents/<id>/upload`) and raises the video cap from 50MB to 500MB.
- Bundled with all in-flight v2 work: feed (LinkPreviewCard + FeedCard/FeedItemMenu/DocumentViewer), journal (LearningEventCard, QuestTasksSection, TaskPickerSheet, attach-to-task API), communication (ChatWindow + GroupChatWindow), new services (apiError, sentry, useAppActive, useLinkPreview), auth store + push notifications updates, render.yaml + eas.json bumps.

## What the new upload flow looks like
1. Client POSTs `{filename, file_size, ...}` to `.../upload-init`; backend returns a Supabase pre-signed URL + token.
2. Client PUTs the file body directly to Supabase (never touches our worker memory).
3. Client POSTs `{storage_path, bucket}` to `.../upload-finalize`; backend verifies the file landed, runs video post-processing (duration validation, thumbnail, background transcode), and returns the URL + metadata.

Init/finalize endpoint pairs added on evidence_documents (task + block), learning_events, parent + advisor learning_moments, and generic uploads. Legacy multipart endpoints stay (capped at 50MB) for any unmigrated caller.

## Supabase changes (already applied to prod)
- `quest-evidence` and `user-uploads` bucket `file_size_limit` raised to 500MB (were NULL). Migration file: `supabase/migrations/20260417_raise_evidence_bucket_file_size_limit.sql`.

## Test plan
- [x] Backend: 315 unit tests pass (15 new MediaUploadService tests, 16 new evidence_documents signed-upload route tests, 13 new cross-route signed-upload tests).
- [x] v1: 419 vitest tests pass (5 new signedUpload helper tests).
- [x] v2: 55 tests pass on changed surfaces (5 new signedUpload helper tests + updated CaptureSheet test). The 6 failures in `authStore.test.ts` are pre-existing on develop.
- [x] Manual local test: user confirmed v1 evidence upload flow works end-to-end at http://localhost:3000 (small image + medium video).

## Things to watch after merge
- First real-user video upload >50MB -- confirm Render workers no longer spike on memory.
- `/api/evidence/documents/<id>/upload-finalize` on a large video: the video post-processing still downloads the file to a backend tmpfile for thumbnail + duration (stream-to-disk, no memory buffering). If that ever becomes a worker saturation issue, the follow-up is to move it to a background job.

body:
## What this does

Replaces 9 instances of `.split(SEP)[0]` / `.split(SEP)[-1]` with the minimally-splitting equivalent:

- `x.split(SEP)[-1]` → `x.rsplit(SEP, maxsplit=1)[-1]` (last segment)
- `x.split(SEP)[0]`  → `x.split(SEP, maxsplit=1)[0]` (first segment)

Pure micro-optimization, no behavior change. `ruff check` passes locally after these edits.

## Why now

Dependabot PR #410 (weekly uv-upgrade) bumps `ruff` to a version that enables rule **PLC0207** ("String is split more times than necessary"). The new ruff finds these pre-existing instances and fails CI on every PR — including itself. Fixing them on `main` first lets #410 rebase clean and merge on its own, and keeps CI green for every subsequent PR.
