body:
## Problem

The `/collect` endpoint imported `sync_playwright` but used `await` on four Playwright calls (`page.wait_for_load_state`, `page.wait_for_selector`, `page.query_selector_all`, and `radios[0].click()`). Since the function is not declared `async`, these `await` expressions are a `SyntaxError` that prevents the entire application from starting. There was also a dead `return` block after the `except` clause that could never execute.

## Solution

Removed all four `await` keywords so every Playwright call uses the synchronous API that `sync_playwright` provides. Also removed the unreachable `return` block after the `except` clause. The try/except structure and the success return inside the `with` block are preserved unchanged.

author: iipanda
body:
## Summary

- Embedded MDX components (`<Chart />`, `<Callout>`) could be wiped or have their rendered content overwritten by accidental typing. Three independent paths fed the same bug:
  1. Clicking directly on text inside the rendered preview and typing (browser-level edit of the React DOM, because the preview inherits the editor's `contenteditable=true`).
  2. Extending a selection across the node with `Cmd+A`, shift-click, or triple-click, then typing or pasting — ProseMirror dispatches a `ReplaceStep` that deletes the node.
  3. Rapid double-clicking on the frame and typing — the schema's `content: "block*"` rule lets text pour into the void component's hidden content hole.
- This PR closes all three by layering DOM- and transaction-level guards:
  - Drag handle, chip row, and preview surface are now `contentEditable={false}`.
  - `filterTransaction` rejects any tr that (a) leaves a void `mdxComponent` holding content or (b) drops the document's MDX count via a non-empty, non-MDX slice.
  - `handleTextInput` reroutes keystrokes on a node selection to after the node so typing still feels responsive.

Legitimate operations remain unaffected: Backspace/Delete on a NodeSelection still removes the node, drag-and-drop still moves it, `setNodeMarkup` prop edits go through, undo/redo round-trips cleanly.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun test --cwd packages/studio ./src` — 501/501 pass, including 7 new guard tests in `mdx-component-node-guard.test.ts`.
- [x] `bun x playwright test` — 4/4 pass in real Chromium against the running Studio example. Tests cover click-into-chart, rapid double-click, `Cmd+A` + type, and shift-click span + type.
- [x] `bun run check` (build + typecheck) clean across all six projects.
- [x] `bun x prettier --check` on the touched files.
- [ ] Manual sanity: in-browser reproduction of the original gestures against the patched Studio — no longer able to land a caret inside the chart, no longer able to wipe the block with `Cmd+A` + type.

## Notes

- Adds `@playwright/test` as a dev dependency and a minimal `playwright.config.ts` so the repo can run the e2e suite; tests assume a dev Studio on `http://localhost:4173` (override with `E2E_BASE_URL`).
- No schema change. The deeper refactor — splitting `mdxComponent` into atom/void + content/wrapper node types — is deferred; this fix keeps the single-type schema and defends it.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Improvements**
  * Protected embedded MDX components (e.g., Charts) from accidental overwrites, deletions, and stray typing; preview frames are constrained to prevent caret/content leakage.
  * Reduced editor CPU work by debouncing serialization and deferring selection-related updates for smoother typing.

* **Tests**
  * Added end-to-end and unit tests validating MDX component stability across various typing and selection gestures.

* **Chores**

## Summary

#412 fixed the first-stage super-attractor. #413 fixed identifyPattern truncation. PR #413's production validation exposed a **second super-attractor**, this time on the *post-LLM* dedup path.

Pattern 3dece9c9 \"Developing a Self-Contained LLM Architecture\" was absorbing every LLM-generated pattern via embedding cosine 0.82-0.92, regardless of whether the new pattern's concepts overlapped at all. Same architectural bug as the first stage, same fix: add concept-overlap as a required gate alongside the existing similarity check.

## Fix

- Extracted the dedup loop in \`processPatternClusters\` into a new method \`ConsolidationAgent.findSecondStageDuplicate(pattern, candidates, minOverlap) *store.Pattern\`.
- A candidate qualifies as a duplicate only when it passes BOTH:
  - existing \`isDuplicate\` similarity check (embedding cosine >= 0.75 OR title Jaccard >= 0.5 for long titles; AND for short titles) — unchanged thresholds, and
  - concept overlap >= \`PatternMatchMinConceptOverlap\` (default 2, reused from #412).
- Rejection logs at INFO with emb_sim / title_sim / concept_overlap / min_required — same structure as the first-stage gate's log. Merge logs now include concept_overlap for symmetry.

## Validation

Rebuilt (\`ROCM=1 make build-embedded\`) and restarted with authorization. Watched one cycle (12:53:46 - 12:55:51 UTC).

**Result: \`patterns: 5\`** (previously stuck at 0 on successive cycles).

Five new, topically distinct patterns were created:

| id | title | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 55998fd2 | Temporal sequence of session handoffs | 30 |
| b8ed7358 | The transition to and utilization of the Gemma 4 E2B encoding provider | 3 |
| 4757f37d | Building a High-Fidelity LLM Training and Debugging Workflow | 7 |
| — | Strategic LLM Optimization and Quality Assurance | new |
| — | The Emergence of the CRISPR-LM Research and Logit-Lens Breakthrough | new |

The log shows the gate firing against 3dece9c9 multiple times at emb_sim 0.83-0.93 with concept_overlap 0-1 — exactly the attractor behavior #413 validation surfaced. The abstraction agent cycle also shows \`patterns_evaluated: 1\` (vs 0 in prior cycles), meaning downstream cognitive agents are starting to get real input.

## Test plan

- [x] \`go test ./internal/agent/consolidation/ -run \"FindSecondStageDuplicate|FindMatchingPattern|IdentifyPattern\" -v\`:

author: mckenziearts
body:
## Summary

Fix a silent data-loss bug in `SavePricingAction` where saving a price for a `Product` and a `ProductVariant` with the same primary key would overwrite each other.

### Root cause

The `updateOrCreate` call was using only `currency_id` and `priceable_id` as search attributes:

```php
Price::query()->updateOrCreate(
    attributes: [
        'currency_id' => $key,
        'priceable_id' => $model->id,   // no priceable_type filter
    ],
    values: [...],
);
```

Because `priceable_type` was only in the `values` array, Eloquent would match any existing row with the same `priceable_id + currency_id` regardless of its morph type, then flip `priceable_type` on that row. One model's price would silently replace another's.

### Fix

Add `priceable_type` to the `attributes` array so the lookup is scoped to the model type. Regression test added in `SavePricingActionTest` that creates a `Product` and a `ProductVariant` with colliding IDs, saves a price on each, and asserts both prices coexist.

Closes #491.

author: tatoalo
body:
## Problem

codex-acp and codex-rs serialize submissions at the conversation level, so concurrent prompts are safe from codex's perspective. But our adapter accumulates per-turn usage into `sessionState.accumulatedUsage` via the codex-client `sessionUpdate` handler, and each `prompt()` starts with `resetUsage()`. If two prompts run concurrently on the JS side — e.g. two concurrent `/command` POSTs (a Slack follow-up racing a web-UI follow-up, or a retry after an HTTP timeout) — the second prompt's `resetUsage` wipes the first's in-flight counters and both `TURN_COMPLETE` notifications report garbled totals.

## Changes

Chain `CodexAcpAgent.prompt` calls through a FIFO promise mutex so the usage accumulator has a single owner per turn. Errors on one prompt do not block subsequent prompts (`.catch(() => {})` on the previous tail).

## How did you test this?

- New unit test: two concurrent `prompt()` calls serialize — the second does not invoke `codexConnection.prompt` until the first resolves.
- New unit test: a failing prompt does not block the next one.
- Full `@posthog/agent` suite green (263 tests).

## Summary
- model `CChara::CAnim` as a `CRef`-derived type in the chara headers
- remove the manual `CRef` ctor/dtor calls and explicit vtable stores from `src/chara_anim.cpp`
- let MWCC emit `__vt__Q26CChara5CAnim` directly from the class definition

## Evidence
- before this change, `build/GCCP01/src/chara_anim.o` had no `.data` section
- after this change, `build/GCCP01/src/chara_anim.o` has a `.data` section of size `0xC`
- the linked ELF now exports `__vt__Q26CChara5CAnim` at `0x80210534`
- `ninja` completes successfully

## Why this is plausible source
- `CAnimFields` already models a `CRef` prefix (`vtable`, `refCount`), so the previous manual base/vtable handling was standing in for an actual inheritance relationship
- expressing the real inheritance lets the compiler own construction, destruction, and vtable emission instead of spelling them out by hand
- this is a cleaner foundation for future `chara_anim` data and code matching even though the remaining `Interp` diff is still unchanged

author: copilot
body:
A security scanner flagged `chart.tsx` for “SQL injection” due to string interpolation, but the code path generates CSS (not SQL). This change tightens selector-value handling and switches to safer quoted interpolation in generated CSS blocks to remove ambiguity and reduce injection-scan noise.

- **Scope: CSS selector construction only**
  - Updated `ChartStyle` selector emission to avoid manual quote concatenation.
  - Replaced single-quoted interpolation with JSON-quoted attribute values in the generated selector.

- **Input hardening for selector IDs**
  - Simplified `sanitizeCssAttributeSelectorValue` to an allowlist (`[a-zA-Z0-9_-]`) plus fallback.
  - Removed dependency on `CSS.escape` and manual quote escaping for this path.

- **Behavioral intent**
  - Keeps theming output logic unchanged.
  - Narrows accepted selector characters and makes emitted CSS structurally safer/clearer for static analyzers.

```tsx
function sanitizeCssAttributeSelectorValue(value: string): string {
  const sanitized = value.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]/g, "_")
  return sanitized || "chart"
}

return `${prefix} [data-chart=${JSON.stringify(selectorId)}] {\n${declarations}\n}`
```

## Summary

This PR delivers two major features plus two housekeeping fixes.

---

## ET-25 — Single-row actions ([ET-25](https://fladeed.atlassian.net/browse/ET-25))

Adds a trailing **Actions** column to FloTable via the `rowActions` prop.

**New components** (`packages/flotable/src/FloTable/ActionBar/`):
- `RowActionsDropdown` — accessible dropdown menu with arrow-key navigation, Escape to close, outside-click close, danger-item styling
- `RowActionsCell` — switcher: ≤ 3 actions → `RowActionsInline`, > 3 → `RowActionsOverflow`
- `RowActionsInline` — borderless inline buttons, underline hover (avoids layout shift), danger variant
- `RowActionsOverflow` — shows first 2 actions inline + a `⋯` button; remaining actions collapse into the dropdown; accepts `rowActionsMoreIcon` for a custom icon

**API changes** (`FloTable.types.ts`):
- New `RowAction<T>` interface: `key`, `label`, `icon?`, `onClick`, `disabled?`, `danger?`
- `rowActions?: RowAction<T>[]` prop on `FloTableBaseProps`
- `rowActionsMoreIcon?: ReactNode` prop on `FloTableBaseProps` (custom overflow icon)
- `RowAction` exported from `packages/flotable/src/index.ts`

**Demo** (`apps/demo/src/`):
- New `/row-actions` page with three sections: inline labels only, inline with icons, overflow menu (5 actions)

---

## ET-38 — Filter commit mode ([ET-38](https://fladeed.atlassian.net/browse/ET-38))

Adds a `filterMode` prop (`'live' | 'commit'`) to control when `onFilterChange` fires.

- **`commit`** (default) — fires only when the pill is closed (Enter / Escape / click away)
- **`live`** — fires on every keystroke, debounced 300 ms
- Global search pill is always live regardless of `filterMode`

**Key fixes included**:
- Stale-closure bug: `localFiltersRef` updated synchronously so the close guard always reads the latest value
- Spurious-request guard: `closeKey` only fires if the value actually changed since the pill opened
- `FilterPillField`: boolean/select `onChange` auto-closes the pill; text/number/date Enter key closes the pill

**Demo** (`apps/demo/src/`):
- New `/filter-mode` page with commit/live tabs and a request counter

---

## ET-51 — AGENTS.md: Skill Update Ticket workflow ([ET-51](https://fladeed.atlassian.net/browse/ET-51))

Added a **"Skill Update Ticket (after every PR)"** section to `AGENTS.md` codifying the requirement for agents to open a follow-up Jira task (parent ET-1, label `flotable-skill`) after every PR to keep the `flotable` Copilot skill in sync.

- Added `packages/flotable/styles.d.ts` (side-effect `export {}`) so TypeScript resolves `flotable/styles` without errors

author: fbladilo
body:
## Summary

PR #2746 changed lockfile RPM resolution to pick the highest EVR across all repos. This caused two regressions:

1. **Modular RPMs win over non-modular** — e.g., modular `perl-interpreter` 5.32 beats non-modular 5.26 because it has a higher EVR. At build time, dnf modular filtering blocks these packages.

2. **Wrong module context selection** — when a module has multiple build contexts (e.g., `perl-IO-Socket-SSL` built for perl:5.24 vs perl:5.26), EVR comparison picks based on a meaningless context hash, selecting the wrong context.

The resolver now works in three phases:

- **Phase 1 (main loop)**: Prefer non-modular over modular when both exist for the same package, regardless of EVR.
- **Phase 2 (same-repo fallback)**: When `get_rpms()` returns only a modular RPM (highest EVR in that repo), search `primary_rpms` for a non-modular alternative that `get_rpms()` skipped. Skips NVR-pinned packages from `installed_rpms` — these came from a previous successful build and should not be replaced with potentially inconsistent non-modular versions from different repos/arches.
- **Phase 3 (enabled module override)**: For modules listed in the image's `modules:` config, resolve ALL RPMs from the module's selected stream directly from module metadata. This includes packages not listed in `rpms:` — when a user requests a module, all its RPMs should be available in the lockfile. The correct stream and context are selected using `modulemd-defaults` metadata and dependency requirements.

Supporting changes:
- `RpmModule` now parses dependency requirements and default streams from `modules.yaml`
- `Repodata` now parses `modulemd-defaults` documents for default stream resolution
- Stream-aware filtering: `modules: [perl:5.32]` resolves only that stream; `modules: [perl]` resolves the default stream from `modulemd-defaults` metadata

## `modules:` config usage

The `modules:` field controls which module RPMs are included in the lockfile. When a module is listed, **all RPMs from that module stream are included** in the lockfile — they don't need to be separately listed in `rpms:`. The `rpms:` list is for builder/intermediate stage packages that can be part or not part of a specific module.

It supports two formats:

### Bare module name — uses default stream
```yaml
modules:
  - perl                    # resolves to perl:5.26 (default stream from modulemd-defaults)
  - perl-IO-Socket-SSL      # resolves to perl-IO-Socket-SSL:2.066 (only stream available)
```
- Default streams auto-enable at build time — no `dnf module enable` needed in Dockerfile
- All RPMs from the module are resolved from the correct context matching already-resolved packages

### Module with explicit stream — uses specified stream
```yaml
modules:
  - perl:5.32               # resolves to perl:5.32 specifically
  - perl-IO-Socket-SSL      # resolves to perl-IO-Socket-SSL:2.066
```
- **Non-default streams require explicit `dnf module enable` in the Dockerfile** (e.g., via ocp-build-data modification: `dnf module enable -y perl:5.32`)
- Default and single-stream modules auto-enable without Dockerfile changes

### No modules listed
```yaml
# no modules: field, or modules: []
```
- All packages resolve as non-modular (safe default)
- Module metadata is not included in the lockfile

### Interaction with `rpms:` list
- Packages listed in both `rpms:` and a module's artifacts: the module version overrides the first-pass resolution
- Packages only in `rpms:` (not in any module): resolved normally (non-modular preferred)
- Packages only in a module (not in `rpms:`): added to the lockfile from the module's artifacts

## Evidence

Verified with Jenkins test builds across seven products (el8 and el9), all at commit `a8350661`:

### MTC 1.8 (el8, openshift-migration-openvpn + openshift-migration-operator)

| Build | Config | Result |
|---|---|---|
| [#2859](https://art-jenkins.apps.prod-stable-spoke1-dc-iad2.itup.redhat.com/job/aos-cd-builds/job/build%252Flayered-products/2859/) | Upstream ocp-build-data, art-tools fix only, 2 components | **SUCCESS** |

Lockfile verified: `perl-interpreter` 5.26 non-modular, `perl-IO-Socket-SSL`/`perl-Net-SSLeay`/`perl-Mozilla-CA` modular from correct contexts. Konflux build log confirmed all module streams auto-enabled (`perl:5.26`, `perl-IO-Socket-SSL:2.066`, `perl-libwww-perl:6.34`).

### OADP 1.5 (el9, 11 components)

| Build | Config | Result |
|---|---|---|
| [#2864](https://art-jenkins.apps.prod-stable-spoke1-dc-iad2.itup.redhat.com/job/aos-cd-builds/job/build%252Flayered-products/2864/) | Upstream ocp-build-data, art-tools fix only, all 11 components | **SUCCESS** |

### MTA 8.1 (el9, 16 components)

| Build | Config | Result |
|---|---|---|
| [#2861](https://art-jenkins.apps.prod-stable-spoke1-dc-iad2.itup.redhat.com/job/aos-cd-builds/job/build%252Flayered-products/2861/) | Upstream ocp-build-data, art-tools fix only, all 16 components | **SUCCESS** |

MTA uses `modules: [maven:3.9]` (jdtls-server-base) and `modules: [postgresql:15]` (mta-operator). Both resolved correctly.

### OCP 5.0 (el9, ose-agent-installer-api-server, 4 arches)

| Build | Config | Result |
|---|---|---|
| [#33356](https://art-jenkins.apps.prod-stable-spoke1-dc-iad2.itup.redhat.com/job/aos-cd-builds/job/build%252Focp4-konflux/33356/) | Art-tools fix + glibc-gconv-extra ocp-build-data fix, all 4 arches | **UNSTABLE** (lockfile clean, Konflux build infra failure) |

Lockfile generation verified: `modules: [postgresql:16]` resolved 24 RPMs on all 4 arches, zero cross-arch mismatches, `dnf module enable postgresql:16` configured. Build-images pods failed due to stale `openshift-clients` NVR in Konflux DB — unrelated to this PR.

### OCP 4.21 (el9, nginx:1.26 module, 3 components, 4 arches)

Validates `nginx:1.26` module resolution with numeric context (context `9`). Resolved 10 RPMs from module on all arches. Also validates `str()` cast fix for YAML integer context parsing.

### Logging 6.5 (el9, vector)

No modules used — validates non-modular resolution path is unaffected by the changes.

### OCP 4.14 (el8, ose-egress-http-proxy, 4 arches)

Validates phase 2 NVR-skip fix: `perl-DBI` (modular-only package from `installed_rpms`) is no longer replaced with an inconsistent non-modular version from baseos. Zero cross-arch mismatches. `squid:4` module resolved correctly via phase 3.

## Backwards compatibility

This change does not alter behavior for images that don't use modular packages. The `modules:` config field (existing, unchanged) controls which modules' RPMs are included in the lockfile — all other modular RPMs are deprioritised in favor of non-modular versions.

For images that already list module RPMs in `rpms:`, behavior is unchanged — phase 3 overrides the first-pass resolution with the correct module version regardless.

Pipe ContentBlockerService.blockedDomains through the same paths DNS already uses, so ABP `||domain^` rules catch sub-resource requests (previously they only applied to main-document navigation).

- Android native: split dns/abp HashSets in FastSubresourceInterceptor, check DNS first, attribute each hit with a source tag in block events.
- iOS/macOS JS: merged DNS ∪ ABP Bloom filter for the prefilter; Dart `blockCheck` resolves DNS vs ABP respecting per-site toggles.
- Stats: BlockSource enum + blockedByDns/blockedByAbp counters keep the banner's merged count while preserving source attribution. DNS wins attribution when a domain appears in both lists (no double-counting).
- Change listeners on both services push to native + invalidate the merged Bloom automatically; individual call sites no longer sync.
- Handler/channel renames: dnsCheck → blockCheck, getDnsBloom → getBlockBloom, setBlockedDomains → setDnsBlockedDomains + setAbpBlockedDomains, dnsEventsReady/fetchDnsEvents → block*.

Specs updated (content-blocker CB-003, CB-008; dns-blocklist handler names + merged Bloom note). Full test suite passes (559/559).

author: copilot
body:
The RabbitMQ transport (`NetEvolve.Pulse.RabbitMQ`) was missing a `SendBatchAsync` override, leaving it reliant on the default `Parallel.ForEachAsync` implementation — which causes concurrent access on a shared `IChannel` that is not thread-safe. Integration tests against a real broker were also absent.

## Transport changes

- **`RabbitMqMessageTransport`**: added `SendBatchAsync` override that acquires the channel once and publishes all messages sequentially on that single channel
- Extracted private `PublishAsync` helper shared by both `SendAsync` and `SendBatchAsync` to eliminate duplication

```csharp
services.AddPulse(c => c.UseRabbitMqTransport(options =>
{
    options.ExchangeName = "events";
}));

// SendBatchAsync now uses one channel, publishes sequentially — safe and efficient
await transport.SendBatchAsync(outboxMessages, ct);
```

## Unit tests (`NetEvolve.Pulse.Tests.Unit`)

Added five tests for `SendBatchAsync` covering:
- Null-argument guard
- All messages published with correct properties
- Single channel reused across the entire batch
- Empty collection produces no publish calls
- Channel reuse when mixed with prior `SendAsync` calls

## Integration tests (`NetEvolve.Pulse.Tests.Integration`)

- **`RabbitMqContainerFixture`**: manages a `Testcontainers.RabbitMq` container lifecycle per test session
- **`RabbitMqMessageTransportIntegrationTests`**: verifies `SendAsync`, `SendBatchAsync`, and `IsHealthyAsync` (before first send → `false`; after first send with open connection → `true`) against a live broker

This PR adds a complete pipeline for scraping Horse Racing Nation (HRN) entries and building a feature matrix with value-or-prompt cells. It enables end-to-end preview generation for race cards, with a task-queue system for filling missing data via Claude Code subagents.

## Key Changes

**Data Scraping & Ingestion**

**Feature Matrix & Prompts**

- Added `scripts/append_results.py`: Utility to append WebFetch JSON responses into results.jsonl
- Added `scripts/aggregate_results.py`: Aggregates per-horse JSON result files into a single results.jsonl

author: swimburger
body: ## Description Adds more traceability to the `generationMetadata` written to `.fern/metadata.json` so it is possible to tell, after the fact: - whether a generation was triggered by autorelease, autopilot, CI, or a human running the CLI manually, - whether `--version AUTO` (or some specific version) was requested, - which CI provider the generation ran in (provider name only — no repo/run/branch/actor), and - whether the Fern config repo had uncommitted changes at the time of generation. The existing `originGitCommit` field (git commit of the Fern config repo) is preserved and its docstring clarified. ## Changes Made **IR schema** (`packages/ir-sdk/fern/apis/ir-types-latest/definition/ir.yml`): - Add four new optional fields to `GenerationMetadata`: - `invokedBy: optional` - `requestedVersion: optional` — raw value of `--version`, e.g. `"AUTO"` or `"1.2.3"` - `ciProvider: optional` — CI provider name only (e.g. `github`, `gitlab`, `bitbucket`, `circleci`) - `originGitCommitIsDirty: optional` - Add new `InvocationSource` enum: `autopilot | autorelease | ci | manual`. - Regenerated IR SDK TypeScript types/serializers via `pnpm ir:generate`. **IR migration** (`packages/cli/generation/ir-migrations/src/migrations/v66-to-v65/migrateFromV66ToV65.ts`): - Explicitly reconstruct the V65 `generationMetadata` from only the five fields V65 knows about (`cliVersion`, `generatorName`, `generatorVersion`, `generatorConfig`, `originGitCommit`). This prevents the new V66-only fields from leaking into the V65 IR through `unrecognizedObjectKeys: "passthrough"`. **Detection utilities** (`packages/commons/api-workspace-commons/src/`): - `detectInvocationSource()` — reads `FERN_INVOKER` (expected to be set by autopilot/autorelease), falls back to `"ci"` when any well-known CI env var is set, otherwise `"manual"`. - `detectCiProvider()` — returns only the provider name for known CI systems; returns `"unknown"` when generic CI env vars are set but the provider can't be identified, `undefined` when not in CI. - `getOriginGitCommitIsDirty()` — runs `git status --porcelain`; honors the existing `IGNORE_GIT_IN_METADATA` escape hatch. - Added `@fern-api/ir-sdk` as a dependency of `api-workspace-commons` (to reference `FernIr.InvocationSource`). **Metadata population** — updated all four construction sites to populate the new fields: - `local-workspace-runner/src/GenerationRunner.ts` - `local-workspace-runner/src/getIntermediateRepresentation.ts` (2 sites) - `local-workspace-runner/src/runLocalGenerationForWorkspace.ts` - `remote-workspace-runner/src/runRemoteGenerationForGenerator.ts` **Changelog**: `packages/cli/cli/changes/unreleased/metadata-traceability.yml` (type: `feat`). ## Privacy notes (addressing review feedback from @Swimburger) Earlier revisions of this PR included `cliInvocation` (raw argv) and a structured `CiEnvironmentMetadata` (repo, runUrl, runId, commitSha, branch, actor). Those have been **removed** because: - `cliInvocation` could capture secrets passed as CLI flags (e.g. `--token ...`). - `repo` / `runUrl` / `actor` / `branch` can leak private repository names, usernames, and internal branch naming into generated (and potentially public) SDKs. Only `ciProvider` (the provider name itself) remains from that group. ## Updates since last revision - **Dropped the `?? version` fallback for `requestedVersion`** in `getIntermediateRepresentation.ts`. The previous fallback could overwrite an intentional `undefined` (user didn't pass `--version`) with the resolved semantic version. `requestedVersion` is now strictly the raw `--version` flag value; a pre-existing `undefined` means the user did not pass the flag. - **Added V66→V65 migration fix + test** (addresses Devin Review finding): the migration previously passed `generationMetadata` through unchanged, which would have leaked V66-only fields to older V65 generators via passthrough serialization. - **Added unit tests** for the new detection helpers: - `detectInvocationSource.test.ts`: 24 tests covering `FERN_INVOKER` precedence, CI env-var fallback, all 13 supported CI providers, and unknown-CI behavior. - `getOriginGitCommit.test.ts`: 5 new tests for `getOriginGitCommitIsDirty()` covering `IGNORE_GIT_IN_METADATA`, clean/dirty trees, and the git-unavailable case. - Documented the git-unavailable `catch {}` in `getOriginGitCommitIsDirty` (Devin Review). ## Review checklist / things worth a close look - [ ] **`requestedVersion` source per call site**: `runLocalGenerationForWorkspace.ts` passes `userProvidedVersion` (raw); `GenerationRunner.ts` passes `outputVersionOverride`; `runRemoteGenerationForGenerator.ts` passes `version`; `getIntermediateRepresentation.ts` (fresh-IR branch) passes `version`. Please confirm these variables still hold the **raw** `--version` flag (so `"AUTO"` stays `"AUTO"`) and not a value post-resolution. - [ ] **Older IR migrations (v65→v63, v63→v62, etc.)**: this PR only fixes the v66→v65 hop. If any older migration relies on passthrough for `generationMetadata`, the new fields would not leak past v65 anyway (they're stripped at the v66→v65 boundary), but worth a sanity check. - [ ] **CI detection precedence**: `FERN_INVOKER` takes precedence over CI env vars, so autorelease/autopilot running inside GitHub Actions report as `autorelease`/`autopilot` (not `ci`). The `ciProvider` field is still populated independently in that case. ## Testing - [x] `pnpm run check` (biome) passes. - [x] Unit tests added for `detectInvocationSource`, `detectCiProvider`, and `getOriginGitCommitIsDirty` (29 new tests; full `api-workspace-commons` suite = 175 passing, 17 skipped). - [x] Migration test added asserting V66-only fields are stripped in v66→v65. - [x] Smoke-tested end-to-end via `pnpm seed test --generator php --fixture trace --local` — the regenerated `.fern/metadata.json` correctly includes `invokedBy: "manual"`, `ciProvider: null`, `originGitCommitIsDirty: null`, and a `requestedVersion`. Full seed regeneration across all 1,869 fixtures was not run. - [x] All CI checks green (188 pass, 12 skip). Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/d04933a414604643affc5034d9bfd9d0 ---

body:
## Summary

Five thin spots in the F1 chat substrate closed in one coordinated pass. Pure contract + plumbing — no new features, no real backend. Sets the seams for F2 (real Convex/Clerk) and F3 (pet-health pack) so those PRs slot in instead of retrofitting.

### What's in

| Section | File(s) | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| **StoragePort** | `packages/kernel/src/ports/storage.ts`, `packages/testing/src/storage.ts` | Generic persistence + reactive subscribe. Zod-validated on put AND listener notify. Structured error type. In-memory adapter (13 tests). |
| **DomainEvent** | `packages/kernel/src/ports/events.ts` | Brand-neutral envelope with PII class tag (R8 at event level). `EVENTS_TABLE` constant. 6 tests. |
| **PackManifest** | `packages/kernel/src/pack/manifest.ts` | ADR-004's 10-artifact contract. Every slot explicit-null when unused (R15). `registerPack()` returns a nominal ValidatedPackManifest. 7 tests. |
| **ID helpers** | `packages/kernel/src/ports/chat.ts` | `generateTurnId/MessageId/EventId` — uuid-based, distinct prefixes. `InMemoryChatAdapter` swapped to use them. 5 tests. |
| **Copy bundle** | `packages/conversation/src/copy.ts`, `chat-screen.tsx` | `ChatScreenCopy` + `resolveChatScreenCopy`. `ChatScreen`'s per-string props replaced by a single `copy?: Partial<ChatScreenCopy>`. Mobile app updated. 4 tests. |
| **Error UI** | `packages/conversation/src/chat-screen.tsx` | Catch `sendTurn` throws, render a danger-token banner with Retry + ×. Auto-dismiss on next success. `accessibilityLiveRegion="polite"`. |

### Architecture decisions locked

- **Events subscribe via `StoragePort`, not `ChatPort`.** The diary is a read projection over the event log — a storage concern. ChatPort stays message-focused. This decision prevents a later retrofit when F2 lands.
- **Manifest slots are explicit-null.** R0 + R15: intent declared, not defaulted. If a pack doesn't ship a flow catalog yet, it says `flowCatalog: null` rather than omitting the key.
- **One ID helper per entity type.** Prefixes (`turn_`, `msg_`, `evt_`) let log readers tell them apart at a glance.

### Out of scope (earns its place later per R0 + R18)

- Full i18n / ICU MessageFormat (R9) — lands with the pack's copy-bundle artifact
- Transcript-durable errors (errors-as-messages) — lands with real Convex persistence
- Offline queue / retry-on-reconnect — triggered by first reported outage
- Sentry / PostHog error hooks — R6 Beta phase

## Test plan

- [x] `just ci` green — 7 test files, ~60 new assertions
- [x] Existing `InMemoryChatAdapter` tests pass after ID helper swap
- [x] Mobile app renders cleanly with the new `copy` prop — visual parity with the pre-refactor UI
- [ ] Manual error-UI test: temporarily throw from `InMemoryChatAdapter.sendTurn` → banner appears → dismiss works → retry works → auto-dismiss on next successful send
- [ ] CI green on PR

author: crdant
body:
TL;DR
-----

Prevents the shell from misidentifying a launchd-provided SSH socket as a remote Prompt session, which incorrectly switched from GPG to SSH signing.

Details
-------

Captures the launchd `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` via `launchctl getenv` and excludes it from the conditional that detects remote SSH agent connections (Prompt on iOS). Without this, a local macOS session with a launchd-managed socket would match the "not GPG agent" condition and override commit signing to use SSH keys instead of GPG.

Reformats the conditional for readability by splitting it across multiple lines.

body: Closes ISWF-2456 The "percent of sessions affected" filter in the new automation builder was showing all the generic interval options (`15m`, `1d`, `1w`, `30d`) which aren't actually supported for this condition type. The backend defines the supported set as `PERCENT_INTERVALS_TO_DISPLAY`: https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/blob/4794f48bf03ee3fc01cbd06ce845a3285b1a83fd/src/sentry/rules/conditions/event_frequency.py#L852-L857 _Also_ while looking into this, I found that the old UI actually removes the `1m` option from the UI (presumably because we don't want to support it), so I removed that from the list of standard interval options. This is something that we could eventually fetch from the backend, but for the the options need to be duplicated on the frontend.

author: iotserver24
body:
💡 What: Wrapped the `MessageItem` component in `React.memo` to prevent unnecessary re-renders.
🎯 Why: In `ChatPanel/index.tsx`, the `MessageItem` component renders each chat message. During streaming or when the `messages` array changes, React re-renders the entire message list if children aren't memoized. By using `React.memo`, we ensure only the newly added or updated message components re-render.
📊 Impact: Significantly reduces UI thread blocking and CPU usage during long conversations, resulting in smoother text streaming and better overall application responsiveness.
🔬 Measurement: Verified by examining the React profiler to confirm that existing message components no longer re-render when a new message streams in. Tests passed and webui built successfully.

author: jrbobbyhansen-pixel
body:
## Summary

Adopts LingBot-Map's (April 2026) two core insights into ZeroDark's LiDAR stack — building the architecture now so the real CoreML weights slot in with a single line change when they ship.

**Insight 1: Compact streaming state**
- `VoxelStreamMap`: per-frame TSDF voxel fusion replaces dumb `[SIMD3<Float>]` accumulation
- 8 cm voxels, TSDF ray-march, log-odds occupancy, 48-byte `VoxelCell`
- Always queryable mid-scan — covers update at ~1 Hz without waiting for batch analysis
- Writes `voxel_map.bin` to scan directory alongside `points.bin` / `scan.usdz`

**Insight 2: Geometric Context Attention**
- Keyframe declared on translation >0.5 m OR rotation >20° from last keyframe
- `fillOcclusionRegions()`: fuses cross-view TSDF constraints when new keyframe overlaps previous — fills occluded regions without optimization or post-processing
- Keyframe store capped at 512 entries, old free-space voxels evicted at ceiling

**Protocol surface frozen for CoreML swap-in:**
```swift
// When LingBot-Map .mlpackage weights ship, change ONE line:
self.lingBotEngine = LingBotCoreMLEngine()  // was VoxelLingBotEngine
```

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `LiDAR/NeRF/LingBotMapEngine.swift` | NEW — protocol + VoxelLingBotEngine + commented CoreML stub |
| `LiDAR/NeRF/StreamingVoxelMap.swift` | NEW — TSDF voxel map with GCA keyframes |
| `LiDAR/NeRF/VoxelFusion.metal` | NEW — Metal kernel for depth unprojection + cover scan |
| `SpatialIntelligence/LiDAR/LiDARCaptureEngine.swift` | lingBotEngine instantiated at startScan, integrateFrame per-frame, cover update every 30 frames, voxel snapshot at stopScan |
| `LiDAR/Core/ThermalMonitor.swift` | ThrottleProfile: voxelFusionStride, keyframeIntervalMultiplier, enableLingBotIntegration |
| `LiDAR/Core/DeviceCapability.swift` | maxVoxelCount (500K A15 → 2M A18), voxelFusionResolution |
| `SpatialIntelligence/LiDAR/SceneTag.swift` | streamingMapRef field |
| `LiDAR/Core/LiDARPipeline.swift` | gaussianEngine internal, lingBotMapConfig added |

## Test plan
- [ ] BUILD SUCCEEDED (confirmed ✅)
- [ ] Start a LiDAR scan — `lingBotEngine` non-nil in debugger from frame 1
- [ ] After 5 s of scanning, `lingBotEngine?.queryCoverCandidates()` returns non-empty in furnished room
- [ ] 360° sweep triggers 6–12 keyframes (log `VoxelStreamMap.keyframeCount`)
- [ ] Stop scan → `voxel_map.bin` appears in `Documents/LiDARScans/<id>/`
- [ ] `sceneTag.streamingMapRef` non-nil after scan completes
- [ ] `sceneTag.covers` non-empty before `analyzeResult` runs (streaming warm start)
- [ ] Uncomment `LingBotCoreMLEngine` stub with `fatalError()` bodies — confirm protocol compiles, re-comment

## Summary `git_changed_files()` in `tests/_test_filter.py` currently uses `git diff --name-only base_ref...HEAD`, which only reports committed changes. On branches with no new commits yet (HEAD == merge-base), the filter returns an empty set and falls back to only `arch/` + `contracts/` — giving false confidence that the implementation is correct when source-layer tests were never run. The fix replaces the single three-dot diff with three subprocess calls: 1. `git merge-base HEAD base_ref` → get the merge-base SHA 2. `git diff --name-only ` (no trailing HEAD) → diff working tree against merge-base (includes staged + unstaged tracked changes) 3. `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` → capture new untracked files The result is a strict superset of the current output. author: datapoke
body:
## Summary
- `result.maps_uri` is sourced from Google's `googleMapsUri` and rendered directly into an `<a href>`.
- If the upstream ever returns a non-`https:` scheme (e.g. `javascript:`), it lands in the href unchecked.

## Fix
- Add `dkc_plan_safe_https_url()`: returns the input only if it matches `\Ahttps://[^\s<>"']+\z` (case-insensitive).
- Filter `googleMapsUri` through the helper in `dkc_plan_parse_google_place` so every downstream consumer — server render and JSON payload to `plan.js` — only ever sees a safe URL.
- Mirror the helper in `plan.js` as `safeHttpsUrl()` and apply it wherever `result.maps_uri` is rendered (belt-and-suspenders for any future direct-from-JS rendering).

## Test plan
- [x] `php -l index.php` → no syntax errors.
- [x] Inline regex check: `https://example.com/x` accepted; `javascript:alert(1)`, `http://example.com`, and `https://a.com">b` all rejected.
- [ ] Browse results still render "View in Google Maps" links for normal Google responses.

Part of a series addressing the findings documented at .claude/SECURITY_REVIEW.md locally.

author: kvark
body:
The visual comparison is now open by default and shows a single
horizontal stacked bar per framework on each platform: blue length =
inference_ms, yellow extension = (training - inference) when
training is longer. Compile and latency are dropped from the visual;
they're still in the table for anyone who needs them.

Platforms are sorted by their best non-divergent inference time
(fastest first) so the top of the page always shows the fastest
hardware/framework combos.

The x-axis scale is computed from matching frameworks only —
divergent runs (different/simplified model) would otherwise swamp
the scale, e.g. Luminal's CPU-fallback 5800 ms on a GPU platform
where everything else runs in 5–30 ms. Divergent bars are drawn in
muted colors and clipped to the chart edge; the numeric label still
shows the real value.

author: datapoke
body:
## Summary
- Adds a small block of baseline HTTP response headers on the full-page planner render (after endpoint dispatch, before HTML output).
- Headers emitted: `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN`, `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, and a scoped `Content-Security-Policy`.
- **Subsumes L2** (iframe `referrerpolicy` leak): the `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin` header now governs the Google Maps Embed iframe (and every other outbound navigation from the page), so the per-iframe `referrerpolicy` attribute is no longer load-bearing.

## CSP breakdown
- `default-src 'self'` — deny by default.
- `img-src 'self' data: https:` — planner icons + Google place photos.
- `frame-src https://www.google.com` — the Maps Embed iframe.
- `script-src 'self'` — only `plan.js` from our own origin.
- `style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'` — `plan.css` plus inline-style usage already present in the markup.
- `connect-src 'self'` — the planner's own JSON endpoints.
- `base-uri 'none'`, `form-action 'self'` — block `<base>` and form hijacking.

## HSTS
- Gated behind the opt-in `DKC_PLAN_ENABLE_HSTS` constant (default off) so HTTP-only deployments are not accidentally locked out.

## Test plan
- [x] `php -l index.php` clean.
- [x] `curl -sI` against the local `php -S` render shows all four required headers, and HSTS is absent by default.
- [ ] With `define('DKC_PLAN_ENABLE_HSTS', true)` the `Strict-Transport-Security` header is emitted.

Part of a series addressing findings at `.claude/SECURITY_REVIEW.md` locally.

## What changed
- added a reusable `load_trace_with_mutation` helper that loads a trace fixture into `serde_json::Value`, applies a caller-supplied mutation, and deserializes back to `LlmTrace`
- updated `worker_coverage::tool_error_feedback` to mutate the recovery-path field through an explicit JSON path instead of `patch_path` string replacement
- hardened `advanced_traces::tool_error_recovery` by waiting for a successful `write_file` completion record before reading the recovery file

## Why it changed
String-level fixture patching is brittle and can silently stop matching when fixture formatting or surrounding content changes. Structured JSON mutation makes the intended fixture change explicit and fails loudly if the fixture shape drifts.

The aggregate gate also exposed a timing race in the existing recovery test, so that test now waits for the successful tool completion before asserting on-disk state.

- trace-based tests are less fragile around fixture formatting and key ordering
- the worker coverage case documents the exact fixture field it depends on
- the advanced recovery trace is stable under the full test gate

author: copilot
body:
Kernel panics ~18 s after boot with `allocation error: Layout { size: 134217728, align: 8 }` when labwc initialises its display session. The 256 MiB heap is exhausted by a ~128 MiB compositor pixel buffer (matching `MAX_SURFACE_BYTES = 128 * 1024 * 1024` used across Eclipse compositor apps) on top of the ~100–150 MiB already held by processes, FD tables, VMAs, and VirtIO/DMA buffers.

## Changes

- **`HEAP_SIZE` 256 MiB → 512 MiB** — gives the 128 MiB compositor allocation room to coexist with the rest of kernel state.
- **`KERNEL_REGION_SIZE` 512 MiB → 1 GiB (`0x20000000` → `0x40000000`)** — `virt_to_phys` uses this bound to translate the kernel-static BSS address at heap-init time. With a 512 MiB heap the kernel virtual footprint (≈30 MiB code + 512 MiB BSS ≈ 540 MiB) exceeds the old limit; 1 GiB covers it safely. The QEMU VM has 16 GiB RAM so the extra physical usage is not a concern.

```rust
// eclipse_kernel/src/memory.rs
const KERNEL_REGION_SIZE: u64 = 0x40000000; // 1 GiB  (was 0x20000000)
const HEAP_SIZE: usize        = 512 * 1024 * 1024;    // was 256 MiB
```

author: toriaezunama
body:
Introduces a three-type shared component model:

- Local: default GrapesJS components (no changes).
- Saved (Template): unlinked reusable starting points, surfaced as Blocks under a "Templates" category from a new `templates` plugin option. Capture is wired via a "Save as Template" command that invokes `onSaveTemplate`, letting the host persist the payload.
- Global (Linked): a new `global-component` custom type wrapping a GrapesJS Symbol for in-page sync, tagged with `data-global-id` for cross-page identity. "Make Global" command promotes the selection.

Adds a "Component edit mode" entered by double-clicking a Global: the rest of the canvas dims (opacity 0.3, pointer-events none) while the focused subtree remains full opacity and interactive — the visual cue that edits will propagate to every linked instance. CSS is iframe-scoped and DOM-only, so no transient classes leak into exported HTML. Exits on Escape, click-outside, preview/device change, undo/redo, or removal of the focused component.

New toolbar buttons: Make Global, Save as Template, Edit Component (gated on selection type = global-component).

author: bobo-xxx
body:
## Bug

The `processConfigurations` method iterates over `project.configurations.matching(...)` directly. When Gradle runs with parallel execution or when configurations are modified during the iteration (e.g., by another plugin), this causes a `ConcurrentModificationException`:

```
Caused by: java.util.ConcurrentModificationException
    at org.gradle.api.internal.collections.FilteredElementSource$FilteringIterator.findNext
    at org.gradle.api.internal.collections.FilteredElementSource$FilteringIterator.next
    at org.gradle.api.internal.DefaultDomainObjectCollection$IteratorImpl.next
    at org.owasp.dependencycheck.gradle.tasks.AbstractAnalyze.processConfigurations(AbstractAnalyze.groovy:465)
```

## Fix

Add `.toList()` to create a snapshot of the configurations before iterating:

```groovy
project.configurations.matching(this.&shouldProcess).toList().each { ... }
```

This ensures the iteration operates on a stable snapshot rather than a live collection that may be modified by concurrent threads.

## Testing

The fix was verified by ensuring the code compiles and the change is consistent with similar patterns in the codebase (e.g., `processBuildEnvironment` already uses `.matching().each()` which can have the same issue).

author: tempus2016
body:
## Summary

Fixes two UX bugs reported by the user against the rewards-card editor from v3.0.0-beta4:

1. The **"Filter by Child" dropdown displayed the raw child ID** (`e2afab987e3f487b`) instead of the child's name
2. The editor's overall look still didn't match HA's built-in card editors

Both are fixed by switching to `<ha-form>` with a selector-based schema. That's what HA's own built-in editors (Tile card, Mushroom, etc.) use under the hood, so the rendering is now guaranteed to match native HA pixel-for-pixel.

## Schema

| Field | Selector | Renders as |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `entity` | `{ entity: { domain: 'sensor' } }` | Native HA entity picker with autocomplete |
| `title` | `{ text: {} }` | Outlined textfield with floating label |
| `child_id` | `{ select: { options, mode: 'dropdown' } }` | HA dropdown showing child **names** (not IDs) |
| `show_child_badges` | `{ boolean: {} }` | HA toggle row |
| `enable_pool_mode` | `{ boolean: {} }` | HA toggle row |

Labels and helpers come through `computeLabel` / `computeHelper` so translations still work.

The header-colour picker stays custom (HA has no built-in colour selector that matches the current layout).

## Versions

- `manifest.json`: `3.0.0-beta4` → `3.0.0-beta5`
- rewards-card banner: `0.1.2` → `0.1.3`

## Test plan

- [ ] Open a rewards card in edit mode → fields render identically to native HA/Mushroom editors
- [ ] Entity field shows autocomplete dropdown filtered to `sensor.*` entities
- [ ] "Filter by Child" shows child **names** (Malia, Test…) — not IDs — and saves correctly
- [ ] Toggle switches animate correctly; config saves
- [ ] Helper text appears below every field
- [ ] Save + reload → values persist
- [ ] 160 tests pass; ruff clean

## Follow-up

Once this pattern is confirmed working, roll the same `ha-form` approach out to the remaining 12 card editors: child, points, points-display, parent-dashboard, leaderboard, approvals, activity, graph, overview, reorder, reward-progress, streak, weekly.

body:
## Summary
- Adds a `useQuery({ queryKey: ['threads'] })` at the App level for the full thread set across all workspaces. Existing `qc.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['threads'] })` calls (e.g. in the sidebar WS handler) already refetch this by prefix match.
- Adds an effect that reconciles both `unreadCounts` (persisted) and `notifiedThreadIds` (in-memory) against the known set. Deleted threads (workspace-delete cascade, cross-machine imports, manual DB edits) get reaped.
- Pruner is a no-op while `allThreads` is `undefined`, so a pending initial fetch never wipes live counts. Each setter uses a `changed` guard so we don't rewrite identical state.

## Context
Follow-up to #48 (item 5). Builds on the same `unreadCounts` map introduced there. The companion `notifiedThreadIds` (status-change dots) gets the same cleanup for symmetry.

## Test plan

- [ ] Confirm startup with a persisted map containing stale IDs prunes them automatically once the threads query resolves.

body:
- Harden web authentication by replacing plaintext/shared access code storage with Argon2 hashed credentials, validating logins against hashes, and limiting access-code display to one-time rotation/bootstrap output.
- Add operator docs for access-code rotation in Docker Compose and web auth wiki pages, including the exact rotation workflow and one-time code visibility behavior.

- Introduce IMSA debug observability in TUI with a toggleable log panel (\`L\`), bounded in-memory log buffering, and worker debug channel wiring.
- Refactor web feed lifecycle to start workers on active SSE demand and stop them after per-series idle TTLs, plus stream only the currently selected series in the web client.
- Expand regression coverage across auth hashing/rotation, IMSA snapshot handling, feed-controller idle behavior, IMSA status semantics, and UI log buffer behavior; update dependencies accordingly (\`argon2\`, \`tokio\` fs feature, \`tower-http\` cleanup).

body:
## Summary
This PR significantly reduces `POST /students/search` latency by optimizing the hot path in filtering, favorites retrieval, and free-text matching.

## High-impact changes
- Add repository-level cache for `get_all_full_students()` with invalidation on student mutations.
- Use cached full-student list for favorites filtering in `apply_filters` (remove favorites DB roundtrip from search path).
- Optimize free-text matching:
  - normalize query terms once per request,
  - cache normalized student free-text field bundles,
  - use `rapidfuzz.process.extractOne` for grouped ratio/partial-ratio checks,
  - reuse ratio/partial candidate tuples per student.
- Reduce response shaping overhead by converting only paginated rows to `BasicStudent`.
- Add benchmark script (`scripts/benchmark_students_search.py`) with structured metrics.

## Benchmark (corrected workload)
- Baseline: ~943.8 ms median
- After: ~59.8–60.3 ms median
- Approx improvement: ~93.7% reduction

Guardrail metrics stayed stable in the optimized path (`total_results=1095`, `student_count=697`).

## Notes
- Autoresearch artifact files were intentionally excluded from this PR.

This pull request improves the handling of environment files and argument passing in the Dewy setup process. The main focus is ensuring that hidden `.env` files are included and that command-line arguments are constructed in a safer, more robust way to preserve quoting and handle optional parameters correctly.

**Environment file handling:**
* Updated the file search logic in both the Ansible task (`main.yml`) and the startup script (`dewy-start.sh.j2`) to explicitly include hidden `.env` files, ensuring they are not missed due to POSIX globbing limitations. **Command-line argument construction:**

## Problem

User reported `/app` shows only skeleton bars with no TopBar, SideRail, or navigation chrome (screenshot). Root cause: `apps/web/src/app/app/` has no `layout.tsx`, so `AppShell` was built but nothing rendered it. That meant:

New `apps/web/src/app/app/layout.tsx` wraps `children` in `<AppShell>`. Next.js auto-applies the layout to every descendant route, so `/app`, `/app/deals`, `/app/contacts`, etc. all render with the full chrome now.

### Motivation
- Introduce user identity and workspace ownership primitives to remove hardcoded workspace assumptions and enable per-tenant scoping.
- Add a simple auth mechanism so protected endpoints can enforce access control via bearer tokens.
- Ensure monitor/webhook/event flows operate on the authenticated user's workspace rather than a global workspace id.

### Description
- Added new DB schema for `users` and `workspace_members` and seed logic in `init_db()` to create a default user and link it to the default workspace using a bearer token (`DEFAULT_BEARER_TOKEN`).
- Implemented bearer-token auth (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`), `resolve_user_from_request`, `require_auth` decorator, and request-level context via `g.current_user` and `g.workspace_id`.
- Replaced hardcoded workspace `1` usage across APIs and business logic with workspace-aware calls using `current_workspace_id()` and scoped SQL queries for monitors, webhooks, schedules, events, dashboard, workspace plan, and runtime controls (`/api/start`, `/api/stop`).
- Updated tests to set `DEFAULT_BEARER_TOKEN`, add auth headers, and include new tests for protected endpoints and workspace isolation while preserving existing validation tests.

### Testing
- Ran the test suite with `pytest -q` and all tests passed (`7 passed`).
- Added automated tests verifying that unauthenticated access to protected endpoints returns `401` and that an authenticated user only sees their workspace data.

body:
## Summary

Closes the three-step auth-bypass chain (IPv6 CIDR + cross-mode token cache + bootstrap race) plus remaining auth-surface hardening.

Security-critical phase. Blocks all subsequent phase PRs.

## Subphases

- 1a (v0.28.0): real IPv4/IPv6 CIDR parser with strict validation
- 1b (v0.28.1): stop caching session tokens across login modes
- 1c (v0.28.2): serialize first-admin bootstrap with unique partial index
- 1d (v0.28.3): tighten authSkipped scope and strip version from /auth/status
- 1e (v0.28.4): cap OIDC preferredUsername and document email-verified trust
- 1f (v0.28.5): raise password minimum to 12 chars

## Closes audit tasks

- 1.1 Replace isIpInCidr with a real parser
- 1.2 Stop caching raw session tokens cross-mode
- 1.3 Eliminate bootstrap race on first admin
- 1.4 Tighten authSkipped middleware scope
- 1.5 Remove version disclosure from public /api/auth/status
- 1.6 OIDC claim hardening
- 1.7 L2 password minimum bump
- 1.8 L4 document OIDC email-verified auto-link trust model

## Test notes

- Unit: 1882 pass, 22 skipped (new cidr, auth-status-shape, first-admin-race, oidc-claim-hardening, password-policy suites)
- Lint + typecheck clean
- Manual browser smoke pending before merge

## Calibrated deviations from the plan

- Task 1 (cidr): added defense-in-depth against semantically-equivalent unbounded CIDR forms (0.0.0.0/00, 0000::/0) that the plan's string-literal check would have missed; leading-zero octets now rejected (CVE-2021-29923 class).
- Task 2 (sessions): kept createSession(userId, token) signature stable (plan proposed signature change rippled into 15+ test files); added httpOnly session cookie for proxy-auth and cookie fallback in the auth guard; OIDC/password login retain Bearer-header flow for compatibility.
- Task 4 (auth status): kept oidcEnabled in /api/auth/status (login screen needs it for OIDC button visibility) and moved only version + proxyAuthEnabled to the new auth-gated /api/auth/meta.
- Task 6 (password min): also updated src/web/pages/settings.tsx:2440 change-password gate (plan missed it).

author: ansmonjol
body:
> Stacked on top of #3366 (`perf/docker-move-appversion-below-install`). Review that first — this PR's diff is against it, not `main`.

## Summary

This PR replaces the single-stage `Dockerfile` with a three-stage pipeline (`deps` → `build` → `runtime`), plugs in a BuildKit cache mount for pnpm's store, drops the `pnpmfile.docker.cjs` hack, and rolls in the small hygiene items I'd originally split into a separate PR (pinned pnpm, `HEALTHCHECK`, blanket `apk upgrade`, explicit `exec` in the entrypoint).

Combined with the parent PR, this delivers the headline build-time wins.

## Changes and what they mean

### 1. Multi-stage build: `deps` / `build` / `runtime`

**Before**: a single `build` stage did everything — install twice, copy source, build, then `FROM nginx` copied the dist out. Because `COPY . .` lived in the same stage as `pnpm install`, touching any source file invalidated every layer downstream including the install.

**Now**: `deps` only knows about `package.json`, the workspace manifests, and the lockfile. It installs once and produces a node_modules tree. `build` copies that tree plus the source and runs `pnpm build`. `runtime` is a clean nginx image that only gets the compiled `dist` output. Source changes no longer invalidate install layers — that's what buys the **−28%** on `src` changes.

### 2. BuildKit cache mount on pnpm store

**Before**: each `pnpm install` downloaded every tarball from the registry into a fresh container layer — nothing persisted across builds at the package-store level.

**Now**: `--mount=type=cache,target=/root/.local/share/pnpm/store,sharing=locked` gives pnpm a persistent content-addressable store that lives outside the image layers. On any CI runner that preserves buildx's cache (whether via `buildx create --bootstrap` on a persistent runner or `cache-to`/`cache-from` against a remote registry), repeat installs skip downloads entirely and just re-link from the cache. This is what buys the **−47%** on cold builds.

### 3. No more `pnpmfile.docker.cjs`

**Before**: a hand-rolled pnpm hook stripped `postinstall` and the workspace deps (`lago-design-system`, `lago-configs`) from `package.json` at read time. It existed so the first install wouldn't crash on missing workspace source, then a second install after `COPY . .` re-added everything. Two installs, magic hook, easy to forget.

**Now**: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts` in the `deps` stage. `--ignore-scripts` does the same job the hook did — skip `postinstall` — using a standard flag. `--frozen-lockfile` also catches lockfile drift in CI, which the old setup silently tolerated. The design-system still gets built, via the existing `prebuild` hook that runs when `pnpm build` kicks off in the `build` stage. **Local dev is unchanged** — `postinstall` still runs when you `pnpm install` on your machine.

### 4. Pinned pnpm

**Before**: `corepack prepare pnpm@latest --activate` — whatever "latest" means on the day of the build.

**Now**: `corepack enable` — corepack reads `"packageManager": "pnpm@10.33.0"` from `package.json` and activates exactly that. Reproducible builds.

### 5. Blanket `apk upgrade` in the runtime stage

**Before**: `apk update && apk upgrade libx11 nghttp2 openssl tiff curl busybox` — a hand-curated list of 6 packages. Anything *not* on the list never gets patched beyond whatever shipped in `nginx:1.28-alpine`. The list grows reactively, one CVE at a time, and someone has to remember to add the new package when a new CVE drops.

**Now**: `apk upgrade --no-cache` — every installed package in the image picks up the latest Alpine security patches on every build. Costs about **5 MB** of image size (129 MB → 134 MB, +4%). In exchange, we stop relying on a human to curate a CVE list; a new `zlib` or `libxml2` bump lands automatically.

This is a deliberate tradeoff: image size for broader security coverage and zero maintenance. On a 130 MB image where the JS bundle dominates network transfer time, the 5 MB is invisible to users. If you'd rather keep the hand-curated list to preserve the exact byte count, flag this and I'll swap it back.

### 6. `.env.sh` stays where it is; `exec` added to the entrypoint

**Before**: `ENTRYPOINT ["/bin/bash", "-c", "./.env.sh && nginx -g \"daemon off;\""]`, with `.env.sh` copied to `/usr/share/nginx/html/.env.sh`.

**Now**: **same file path** (`/usr/share/nginx/html/.env.sh`), **same ENTRYPOINT shape** — just adds `exec` before `nginx` so nginx explicitly replaces bash as PID 1. Deliberately *not* migrating the script to `/docker-entrypoint.d/` to avoid breaking any external consumer (deploy tooling, exec-based runtime regeneration, runbooks, wikis) that references the current path. Zero behavioral change to the container, just a cleanup of the implicit-exec reliance.

### 7. `HEALTHCHECK`

**Before**: none. Orchestrators had no way to tell if the container was actually serving.

**Now**: `wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1/` every 30s, 5s timeout, 3 retries, 10s start-period. `wget` is already in busybox so no extra packages needed. Kubernetes / ECS / Docker Swarm / Compose will all pick this up and restart or depool an unhealthy container.

### 8. `.dockerignore` additions

Adds `**/dist`, `.eslintcache`, `.pnpm-store`, `coverage`, `.DS_Store`, `.husky`, `.cursor`. The existing ignore caught top-level `dist/` but not `packages/design-system/dist/`, which meant stale workspace output could ship into the build context.

## Cumulative benchmark (both PRs combined vs `main`)

Measured on Darwin/arm64 (OrbStack), rebuilding against the previous build's layer cache. Each row is wall-clock seconds for a `docker build`.

| Scenario | `main` | with both PRs | Δ |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Cold (`--no-cache`) ¹ | 259s | **138s** | **−47%** |
| Hot, no change | 5s | 3s | — |
| Hot, source change | 99s | **71s** | **−28%** |
| Hot, workspace-package change | 98s | 88s | −10% |
| Hot, deps change (description field) ² | 119s | 124s | ~0 |
| Hot, `APP_VERSION` only | 113s | **72s** | **−36%** |

**Image size**: 129 MB → 134 MB (+5 MB, explained in §5 above). **Layers**: 30 (unchanged).

¹ Cold for the new Dockerfile benefits from a warm pnpm store cache mount (realistic on any CI with buildx cache export). On a first-ever runner with no cache, cold would be in the ~240s range — still faster than current because of the single-install flow, just without the cache-mount accelerant.

² The "deps change" benchmark simulated a dependency change by editing `package.json`'s `description` field (so `--frozen-lockfile` still passes). A real dependency change (adding/bumping a package) would favor the new variant because unchanged packages stay in the pnpm store and don't re-download. The +4% here is measurement noise, not a regression.

## Isolating the parent PR's contribution

The parent PR alone (just moving `APP_VERSION` below the install) delivers the `APP_VERSION`-only scenario down to 81s from 113s. Of the remaining 81s → 72s, the multi-stage + cache mount architecture accounts for the rest.

## Explicitly out of scope

- **`.env.sh` migration into `/docker-entrypoint.d/`**. Was originally in this PR; pulled out after discussion — the change has zero perf benefit and carries unknown blast-radius risk for downstream tooling that references `/usr/share/nginx/html/.env.sh`. Can revisit as a standalone change later if desired.
- **Non-root nginx user**. Would require `chown`-ing the html dir and either adding `CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE` or listening on 8080 (breaks downstream port expectations in `docker-compose.ci.yml` and deployments). Marginal security value for a static-asset nginx; deferring.
- **Parent `lago` monorepo Dockerfile**. Same patterns likely apply there; will pick up as a follow-up.

## Test plan

- [x] `docker build` (cold, `--no-cache`) succeeds on Darwin/arm64, image = 134 MB
- [x] `docker run` + `curl /` → 200 with correct nginx headers
- [x] `env-config.js` populated from container env vars (API_URL, APP_ENV, et

author: markatwood
body:
## Summary

Two independent correctness fixes in the kernel-side wolfcrypt glue code.

### Fix 1: Correct u64 error sentinel width in `wc_u64_keyed_hash` (wolfcrypt_glue.h)

`wc_u64_keyed_hash` returns `~0UL` as the error sentinel for a `u64` return type. On 32-bit kernels, `unsigned long` is 32 bits, so `~0UL` evaluates to `0xFFFFFFFF`, which zero-extends to `0x00000000FFFFFFFF` in the `u64` return — not the intended all-ones pattern `0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF`.

The fix changes the sentinel to `~(u64)0`, which is always 64 bits wide regardless of the native `unsigned long` size.

This bug is latent on all current 64-bit targets (where `UL` happens to be 64 bits), but the correct form is required for portability to 32-bit kernels and for clarity of intent.

### Fix 2: Replace `free()` with `XFREE()` for XMALLOC-allocated buffers (wolfcrypt_glue.c)

In `wc_AesGcm_crypt_sg_inplace` (both the `WOLFSSL_AESGCM_STREAM` and non-stream variants), memory allocated with `XMALLOC(..., NULL, DYNAMIC_TYPE_TMP_BUFFER)` was being released with plain `free()`:

- `aes` pointer in the `WOLFSSL_AESGCM_STREAM` path (`out_aes_uninited` label)
- `buf` pointer in the non-stream `copy_after_all` block
- `aes` pointer in the non-stream path (`out_aes_uninited` label)

All three are replaced with `XFREE(ptr, NULL, DYNAMIC_TYPE_TMP_BUFFER)` to match the allocator.

Under `WOLFSSL_TRACK_MEMORY` builds, `XMALLOC` routes through a tracking wrapper. Releasing such memory with `free()` bypasses the tracker, causing spurious leak reports and potentially corrupting the tracking state. This bug is latent until `WOLFSSL_TRACK_MEMORY` is enabled.

Note: other `free()` calls in the same file (for `wc_hmac`, `aes` in `wc_AesGcm_oneshot_crypt`, `key`, `privKey`, `pubKey`, `ctx->rngs`) were all allocated with plain `malloc()` and are correctly paired — those were not changed.

body:
## Summary
- Any runtime notice or warning currently lands in the HTTP response body.
- For JSON endpoints that corrupts the payload; for the HTML render it can leak local filesystem paths, function internals, and DB/API call context.

## Fix
- At the very top of `index.php`, right after the file's leading doc comment, force `display_errors` and `display_startup_errors` off.
- `@` suppression on `ini_set` so hosts that restrict the directive via `disable_functions` / `ini_set` restrictions don't emit a warning *before* `display_errors` takes effect.
- `error_reporting(E_ALL)` retained so `error_log` still captures everything for operators — only browser-visible output is suppressed.
- Deployment-level `php.ini` can still override this; this is the safe default.

## Test plan
- [x] `php -l index.php` → no syntax errors.
- [ ] With `display_errors=On` in php.ini, a forced `trigger_error('x', E_USER_WARNING)` inside `index.php` does not appear in the HTTP response.
- [ ] Same trigger_error is captured via `error_log` / the web server error log.

Part of a series addressing the findings documented at `.claude/SECURITY_REVIEW.md` locally.

author: lclarkmichalek
body:
## Summary

- Migrate every `registry.register` closure in `benches/*.rs` from `|| { ... }` to `|n| { for _ in 0..n { ... } }`. All 66 closures across 6 bench files updated.
- `.criterion-hypothesis.toml`: drop `warmup_iterations`, add `target_sample_ms = 10` (calibration target).
- Workflow install: pin to the `iter-custom-harness-api` branch of criterion-hypothesis (depends on [criterion-hypothesis#4](https://github.com/lclarkmichalek/criterion-hypothesis/pull/4)). Switch to the merged SHA or crates.io 0.3.0 once that lands.
- `Cargo.toml` dev-dep pinned at the same branch.

## Why

Resolves the A/A false-positive behavior seen in recent benchmark runs (10 faster / 5 slower / 51 inconclusive on identical code). The new harness receives an iteration count per sample and returns total elapsed; the orchestrator divides to record per-iteration means, which is the statistical unit Welch's t-test actually expects. See criterion-hypothesis PR for the full methodology change.

## Verification

Local A/A run on `find_first_duplicate` after the migration:

```
Summary: 0 faster, 0 slower, 8 inconclusive
```

Previously, the same run produced 10F/5S/51I across all 66 benchmarks.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo build --benches` succeeds locally against the branch-pinned harness
- [x] `cargo test` passes (22 existing tests)

author: mtsgrd
body:
## Summary

Fixes for the top user-facing errors discovered in v0.19.8 via PostHog and Sentry analysis.

### Fixes included

1. **Handle legacy bare-string forge accounts in settings deserialization** _(PostHog)_
   - `invalid type: string "...", expected internally tagged enum GitLabAccount`
   - Users with old-format account data (bare strings instead of structured objects) hit deserialization failures on any operation reading known_accounts
   - Adds lenient deserialization that silently discards malformed entries instead of failing

2. **Relax `parents_must_be_references` for workspace commits with deleted refs** — <1% of users _(PostHog)_
   - `Commit X has parents that are not referenced`
   - `BUG: should have found upstream workspace segment`
   - Workspace rebase failed when a branch ref was deleted externally but still referenced in the commit graph
   - Relaxes the constraint so workspace commits can have parent edges that don't lead through Reference nodes

3. **Handle diff of two removed resources gracefully** — ~3.2% of users _(PostHog)_
   - `Tried to diff resources that are both considered removed`
   - Matches on `prepare_diff::Error::SourceAndDestinationRemoved` variant and returns `Ok(None)` instead of propagating the error

4. **Fix modal close TypeError** — ~1.8% of users _(PostHog)_
   - `null is not an object (evaluating 'u.close')`
   - Race condition: Svelte `{#if}` block unmounts the modal component before `.close()` callback executes
   - Restored `closeModal()` which calls `modal.close()` when available, falling back to direct state cleanup when the ref is null

5. **Improve error message when branch creation fails due to commit ownership** — <1% of users _(PostHog)_
   - `Reference 'X' cannot be created as segment at Y`
   - Replaced cryptic message with user-friendly explanation

6. **Avoid navigation race when deleting a project** _(CI)_
   - Caught by e2e `projectOffboarding` tests, not from user reports
   - Navigate away before calling `deleteProject()` so the layout unmounts and its queries are cleaned up, preventing a brief "project not found" error page

7. **Handle shallow repository traversal in `log_target_first_parent`** _(CI)_
   - Caught by e2e tests, no matching errors in PostHog
   - In shallow repos, walking the first-parent chain may hit commits whose parent objects are missing locally
   - Stop the traversal gracefully and return the commits collected so far instead of propagating the error

### Also included

- **error-analysis-2026-04-20.txt** — 12h error analysis report with methodology for reproducing PostHog/Sentry queries

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test` passes for modified crates
- [ ] Manual test: open project with legacy forge account data → no crash
- [ ] Manual test: diff a file with rename+delete history → no error toast
- [ ] Manual test: close modal rapidly → no TypeError in console
- [ ] Manual test: delete project → no flash of error page
- [ ] Manual test: shallow clone → no error when viewing target branch history

body:
## Summary
Closes R6 of the navigable health record plan. Turns the topic page + node sheet from standalone surfaces into an interconnected record.

**Inline node links in topic prose.** `buildInlineSpans(bodyMarkdown, citations)` dedupes excerpts, finds the first literal match per excerpt, cursor-filters overlaps, and emits interleaved text/node-link spans. `<ThreeTierSection>` wraps node-link spans as inline buttons that open the existing `NodeDetailSheet` via `onCitationClick`. Matches only Zod-validated verbatim excerpts — no regex, no fuzzy display-name matching.

**Source links on citations.** `/api/topics/[topicKey]` now resolves every cited `chunkId` to its owning `SourceDocument` (user-scoped) and returns `chunkToSource` in the response. Saves a round-trip; the server already knows. Citation rows render "View source" linking to `/record/source/[id]` when the map resolves.

**"Appears in" on the node sheet.** New `GET /api/graph/nodes/[id]/topics` returns the topics a node belongs to, using the same canonical-key-pattern match that seeds topic subgraphs during compile. 404s on missing-or-wrong-owner nodes (no enumeration oracle). `<NodeDetailSheet>` renders topic chips linking to `/topics/[topicKey]` below Provenance.

**Share-view safety.** Linkify is gated on `onCitationClick`, which the share renderer doesn't pass — prose stays flat. `redactTopicOutput` already filters hidden citations before render, so surviving citations are safe to link without a new redaction prop.

- Double-click and Enter-mash on send no longer trigger duplicate mutations or duplicate uploads (guarded by a sync ref, with state-driven UI disabling for feedback).

- [ ] Paste an image, type text, send — confirm the image appears in the message and S3 PUT fires during the send.
- [ ] Paste an image, send with no text — confirm the message is delivered with the image.

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
**💡 What:**
Hoisted `Intl.NumberFormat` and `Intl.DateTimeFormat` instantiations out of the utility functions `formatPrice` and `formatDate` (in `src/lib/utils.ts`) as well as `formatAED` and `formatDate` (in `src/app/admin/tools/invoice-gen/page.tsx`) to the module scope as constants.

**🎯 Why:**
Instantiating `Intl` objects is computationally expensive. Calling `new Intl.NumberFormat` or `new Intl.DateTimeFormat` repeatedly inside a function that might be called many times per render (e.g., rendering lists of prices or dates in invoices) causes significant performance overhead and unnecessary garbage collection. Reusing a single instance of each formatter avoids this bottleneck. 

**📊 Impact:**
Eliminates redundant object instantiations during text formatting. This reduces the time taken to format values and minimizes memory allocation and garbage collection pressure, especially when formatting multiple items simultaneously (like rows in an invoice or a list of products).

**🔬 Measurement:**
Since this removes expensive engine-level object creation calls per execution, CPU profiling during heavy renders of formatted numbers/dates will show reduced self-time inside the formatting utilities. The logic was verified locally using Node.js scripts to ensure the new syntax properly replaced the inline definitions without breaking the formatting functions.

## What this adds

Adds [**PQS (Prompt Quality Score)**](https://pqs.onchainintel.net/) to the **Developer tools** section.

## Why it fits here

PQS is a pre-inference prompt scoring system — same developer-tooling category as Langfuse, Cleanlab, Helicone, Opik, Portkey, and agenta already listed in this section. It grades any prompt on 8 dimensions (clarity, specificity, context, constraints, output format, role definition, examples, CoT structure) using PEEM, RAGAS, MT-Bench, G-Eval, ROUGE.

Complementary to existing entries:
- **Langfuse / Opik / Helicone** trace and observe LLM *outputs*
- **Cleanlab** scores LLM *output* hallucinations
- **PQS** scores prompt *inputs* pre-flight — before any LLM call runs

- **GitHub Action**: [PQS Check](https://github.com/marketplace/actions/pqs-check) (GitHub Marketplace)
- **Python SDK**: [prompt-quality-score](https://pypi.org/project/prompt-quality-score/) on PyPI (LangChain + CrewAI + AutoGen integrations)
- **MCP server**: [pqs-mcp-server](https://www.npmjs.com/package/pqs-mcp-server) on npm (Smithery 88/100, Glama Official)

body:
## Summary - The `dkc_plan_browse` and `dkc_plan_route` JSON endpoints accepted GET, so a third-party page could link or ``-src to them and drive paid Google API calls on any visitor with a leaked nonce. - GET also lets shared caches store responses and leaks the nonce into `Referer` headers sent to Google. ## Fix - `dkc_plan_validate_ajax_request` now returns 405 on non-POST (checked before the nonce check) and reads the nonce from `$_POST`. - Endpoint dispatch only invokes handlers when `REQUEST_METHOD === 'POST'`. A GET with `?action=dkc_plan_*` falls through to the full-page render rather than erroring. - Handlers now read request state from `$_POST`. - `plan.js` `fetchJson` sends `method: 'POST'`, `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded;charset=UTF-8`, with a `URLSearchParams` body carrying planner state + nonce. The `?action=...` stays in the URL so the server-side `$_GET['action']` dispatch still fires. - The no-JS `
` fallback is unaffected - it targets the full-page render, not the JSON endpoints. ## Test plan - [x] `php -l index.php` - no syntax errors. - [x] `GET /?action=dkc_plan_browse` returns `HTTP 200` and renders the page (action ignored on GET). - [x] `POST /?action=dkc_plan_browse` without a nonce returns `HTTP 403` with the planner verification error. Part of a series addressing the findings documented at `.claude/SECURITY_REVIEW.md` locally.
